title: Check report access after sharing is revoked
preconditions: A member account previously had access to a shared home's reports. The owner has revoked that member's access.
steps: Sign in as the former member.
Open the shared home's Energy reports page or follow a saved report link.
expected: The former member cannot view the home's report data and receives a clear access or unavailable message.

title: Invite an email with mixed letter case
preconditions: The owner is signed in and has an available member place. The intended invitee's account uses the same email address with different letter case.
steps: Open household sharing and invite the email address using different letter case.
On the invitee's iPhone, open the invitation and sign in to the matching account.
Check whether the home appears.
expected: The invitation is associated with the intended account regardless of email letter case, and the invitee can join the home.

title: Reject away temperature below minimum
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and paired with an online thermostat. Away mode settings allow temperature entry.
steps: Open away mode settings.
Try to enter a temperature below 5 degrees.
Save or confirm the entry.
expected: The app does not accept a temperature below 5 degrees and clearly indicates the allowed range.

title: Receive mains interruption notification
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. A paired thermostat is in a test setup that can report an interrupted mains supply.
steps: Interrupt mains power to the thermostat using the test setup.
Wait for the app to receive the status.
Check the iPhone notification centre.
expected: The app sends a notification that mains power was interrupted and identifies the affected thermostat. It does not report a low battery unless that condition is also present.

title: Check away mode with no internet connection
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, away mode is active, and the paired thermostat is operating normally.
steps: Enable Airplane Mode on the iPhone.
Open the home controls in the app.
Attempt to change away mode or its target.
expected: The app clearly indicates that it cannot confirm or send the change while offline. The thermostat retains its last confirmed heating control and the app does not report an unsent change as applied.

title: Check display after time and date change
preconditions: The thermostat is online and its time can be changed through the supported setup or test environment.
steps: Change the system time or timezone using the approved method.
Observe any displayed time or schedule information.
Restore the original time setting.
expected: Displayed time-related information reflects the updated setting and does not show malformed or contradictory values.

title: Open each zone's controls
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in as a household member. The home has at least two zones.
steps: Open the home zone list.
Select each zone in turn.
Check that the selected zone's controls and thermostat status are displayed.
expected: Each zone opens its own controls and status, with the selected zone clearly identified.

title: Invite an address already in the household
preconditions: An owner is signed in. The household already has a member with a known email address.
steps: Enter the existing member's email address in the invite form.
Try to send the invitation.
expected: The dashboard explains that the address is already a member. It does not send a duplicate invitation or add another member entry.

title: Schedule a period near the end of the day
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the selected day has room for another period. The thermostat is online.
steps: Add a period at a valid late time, such as 23:30.
Set its target to 17 degrees.
Save and inspect the day.
expected: The app saves the period at the selected late time with a 17 degree target. The time is not moved to another day.

title: Handle thermostat offline during away change
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the paired thermostat can be disconnected from power or network for testing.
steps: Disconnect the thermostat from power or its network.
Try to change the away target in the app.
Reconnect the thermostat and refresh its status.
expected: The app identifies that the thermostat is unavailable or the change is pending, rather than claiming the target is active. On reconnection, the thermostat and app converge on the confirmed setting.

title: Check schedule with temperature sensor disconnected
preconditions: A schedule is saved and the temperature sensor can be safely disconnected by an authorised tester. The thermostat is powered.
steps: Disconnect the temperature sensor using the approved test method.
Open the thermostat schedule display and wait for fault detection.
Note the displayed error and schedule state.
Reconnect the sensor and check the schedule.
expected: The thermostat reports E-217 for the disconnected temperature sensor. The saved schedule is not deleted or altered.

title: Use one-hour boost for a zone
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone has an online thermostat and boost is available.
steps: Open the zone controls.
Start a one-hour boost for the zone.
Verify the boost status and displayed end time.
expected: The dashboard shows boost active for the selected zone for one hour. Other zones are not shown as boosted unless separately selected.

title: Check boiler demand in frost protection
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on, frost protection is active, the boiler is responsive, and the room temperature is below 5 degrees.
steps: Observe the thermostat's heating status.
Check the boiler's heat-demand indicator.
expected: The thermostat requests heat to protect against frost, and the boiler indicates a heating demand.

title: Check report after one-hour boost
preconditions: The app is signed in to a home with a paired thermostat and an available monthly report. The boiler is operational.
steps: Start a one-hour boost from the app.
After the boost completes, open the monthly energy report.
Check that the report remains available and covers the expected month.
expected: The monthly report loads normally after the boost and does not display an unrelated error or incorrect reporting period.

title: View report before any heating data exists
preconditions: A home and thermostat are paired, but no report data has yet been generated for the selected month.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Select the month before any report data was generated.
expected: The dashboard explains that report data is not yet available. It does not show misleading energy figures or an unexplained blank report.

title: Check readings with a hearing accessibility alert
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and supports a visual alert for an on-device status event. Live sensor readings are available.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Trigger a safe, supported status event that produces a visual alert.
Read the alert and then return to the sensor view.
expected: The visual alert is distinguishable from the sensor readings, and both readings are available again after dismissing or leaving the alert.

title: Reject an account email already in use
preconditions: The tester is signed in and another account already uses the email address to be entered.
steps: Open profile settings.
Replace the current email with the address used by the other account.
Save the change.
expected: The change is rejected and the existing email remains on the account. The dashboard does not reveal private information about the other account.

title: Check sensor values do not overlap display labels
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying temperature and humidity. The normal screen uses labels or units for these readings.
steps: Wake the display.
Read the temperature and humidity values and their labels.
Turn the dial one step and return to the normal screen if needed.
expected: Each numeric value is clearly associated with the correct sensor and unit. Text, digits and units do not overlap or become clipped.

title: Show an offline thermostat in its zone
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone contains a thermostat that can be made offline by disconnecting its network.
steps: Disconnect the thermostat from Wi-Fi.
Open or refresh the zone overview.
Inspect its status and available controls.
expected: The zone identifies the thermostat as offline or unreachable. The dashboard does not present stale readings as current or claim that a new setting has been applied.

title: Schedule the minimum target temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and a schedule can be edited. The selected day has room for another period or an existing period to edit.
steps: Open a period in the schedule editor.
Set its target temperature to 5 degrees.
Save the schedule.
Reopen the period and inspect its target.
expected: The thermostat accepts and displays 5 degrees as the period's target temperature.

title: Check display readability during update
preconditions: An update is available and the thermostat display is clean and functioning. The room can be viewed from normal standing distance.
steps: Start the update on the thermostat.
View the progress display from normal standing distance and at a slight angle.
Check that progress and any warning remain visible through a screen refresh.
expected: Progress, warnings, and completion status are legible on the round display without relying on colour alone. The display does not go blank in a way that leaves the user unsure whether installation is active.

title: Check sensor readings after an extended warm-up
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live readings in a room with stable conditions. A safe, gradual room temperature increase can be made.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Raise the room temperature gradually and hold it steady for ten minutes.
Observe both readings during the hold and after the room returns to its prior condition.
expected: The readings remain available during the sustained change and settle as the room conditions stabilise, without becoming stuck or displaying a sensor fault.

title: End a zone boost early
preconditions: A one-hour boost is active for the thermostat's zone.
steps: Press the boost button again or use the displayed control to end boost.
Check the zone's boost status.
Check that the zone returns to its normal control state.
expected: Boost ends promptly and is no longer indicated as active. The zone resumes its normal target or schedule control.

title: Verify display after a brief power interruption
preconditions: The thermostat is connected to mains power and operating normally. It is safe to briefly interrupt its supply.
steps: Disconnect mains power briefly.
Restore mains power.
Observe the startup and home screen.
expected: The thermostat returns to a usable display and retains its configured settings; it does not become stuck on a blank or partial screen.

title: Navigate account forms using only a keyboard
preconditions: The tester is signed out and the registration or sign-in page is open in a desktop browser.
steps: Use Tab and Shift+Tab to move through all form controls.
Use the keyboard to enter valid test values.
Submit using the appropriate keyboard control.
Observe the focus position and validation feedback.
expected: All controls are reachable and operable without a mouse, focus order is logical, and focus is visible. Submission and validation feedback can be accessed by keyboard.

title: Update the account email address
preconditions: The tester is signed in and can access account profile settings. A new, unused email address is available.
steps: Open profile settings and enter the new email address.
Save the change and complete any requested verification.
Check the profile email shown after verification.
expected: The email address changes only after the dashboard's required verification is complete. The updated address is shown and the account remains secure.

title: Check sensor readings during pairing timeout
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and can enter its on-device pairing flow. No compatible Wi-Fi network is available to complete pairing.
steps: Start pairing using the thermostat controls.
Leave the pairing flow until it times out.
Check the display and return to the sensor view.
expected: The thermostat indicates E-104 after pairing times out; local sensor readings are still available when the sensor view is displayed.

title: Display humidity reading during ordinary use
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and its humidity sensor is connected. The normal screen includes humidity readings.
steps: Wake the display if it is asleep.
Read the displayed humidity.
Wait one minute and read it again.
expected: The display shows a humidity value as a percentage. The value is readable and no humidity fault is shown.

title: Navigate sign-in with VoiceOver
preconditions: VoiceOver is enabled on the iOS device and the app is on the sign-in screen.
steps: Swipe through the sign-in controls using VoiceOver.
Listen to the labels for the email and password fields and sign-in button.
Activate each field and enter valid credentials using the accessible keyboard.
expected: VoiceOver announces meaningful labels and control roles, and the tester can reach and operate all sign-in controls.

title: Owner initiates an allowed update action
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in as the home owner and an update is available. The product's owner permissions allow any displayed update action.
steps: Open the thermostat's firmware screen.
Use the available update action, if offered.
Check the thermostat and app status.
expected: An allowed action is accepted and the app reports its status accurately. Any installation remains within the permitted overnight window unless the product explicitly identifies a non-installing preparation action.

title: Return from frost protection to normal heating
preconditions: Frost protection is active and the thermostat is online. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open heating controls.
Disable frost protection or select normal heating.
Check the resulting target and mode.
expected: Frost protection is no longer active. Normal heating resumes using the current target or schedule, as shown consistently in the app and on the thermostat.

title: Check household member away mode access
preconditions: The home has an owner and a household member account. The member is signed in to the Android app.
steps: Open away mode controls as the member.
Turn away mode on if the control is available.
Check the resulting state as the owner.
expected: The member can change away mode only if their household permissions allow it. Any permitted change is shown consistently to the owner and thermostat.

title: Navigate between report months
preconditions: The user is signed in and has report data for two adjacent months. The report provides previous and next month controls.
steps: Open one of the months with report data.
Use the next-month control, then the previous-month control.
expected: Each control displays the report for the adjacent month, and returning to the previous month restores its period and figures.

title: Reject a temperature outside the allowed range
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and an editable schedule period is available.
steps: Edit the period's target temperature.
Try to enter a value below 5 degrees or above 30 degrees.
Attempt to save the period.
expected: The app prevents saving an out-of-range target and identifies the allowed range of 5 to 30 degrees. The previously saved target remains unchanged.

title: Reject an incorrect password
preconditions: A verified Dormouse account exists and the tester knows its email but will use an incorrect password.
steps: Open the sign-in screen.
Enter the account email and an incorrect password.
Submit the form.
expected: The app denies access, shows a non-revealing error message and keeps the user signed out.

title: Handle an unknown email at sign-in
preconditions: The tester is signed out and has an email address that is not registered with Dormouse.
steps: Enter the unregistered email address and any password.
Submit the sign-in form.
expected: Sign-in is denied with a message that does not disclose account registration status. No account is created.

title: Prevent a member removing the owner
preconditions: An owner and a member have accounts with access to the same home. The member is signed in to the web dashboard.
steps: Open household sharing settings as the member.
Look for an option to remove the owner.
Try any available route to remove or change the owner's access.
expected: The member cannot remove the owner or change the owner's ownership. The owner remains listed and retains full access.

title: Keep schedule changes after reloading
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a configured zone.
steps: Change a schedule period and save it.
Reload the web dashboard.
Open the same zone and period.
expected: The saved change is still shown after reload. No duplicate period is created.

title: Enforce the household member limit
preconditions: The home has an owner and eight members, and the owner is signed in to the iOS app. A further valid email address is available for testing.
steps: Open household sharing for the home.
Choose to invite another member.
Enter the valid email address and try to send the invitation.
expected: The invitation is not sent because the household member limit has been reached, and the app explains the limit.

title: Use a half-degree schedule setting
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and a paired thermostat is available for schedule editing.
steps: Open a schedule period's temperature control.
Set the temperature to 19.5 degrees and save.
expected: The schedule saves and displays 19.5 degrees without rounding it to a whole degree.

title: Pair after switching the iPhone to another 2.4 GHz network
preconditions: The thermostat is in pairing mode. The iPhone can connect to two available 2.4 GHz networks, and the selected network has a valid password and internet access.
steps: Start pairing and select the first available network.
Before confirming the network details, switch the iPhone to the second network in iOS Settings.
Return to the app, select the second network, and complete pairing.
expected: The app pairs the thermostat to the second network selected during setup. The thermostat connects successfully without using credentials from the first network.

title: Pair using TalkBack
preconditions: TalkBack is enabled on the Android phone. The thermostat is in pairing mode and a 2.4 GHz network with known credentials is available.
steps: Navigate the pairing flow using TalkBack gestures.
Select the network and enter its password using the screen reader.
Complete setup and listen to the resulting status.
expected: Interactive controls and status messages have meaningful spoken labels and focus order. The user can complete pairing and hear confirmation that the thermostat was added.

title: Log in with the new password after a password reset
preconditions: A Dormouse account whose password has just been changed using the emailed link. The app is installed and logged out.
steps: Open the Dormouse app.
Enter the account's email address and the new password.
Tap Log in.
Log out, then try to log in again with the old password.
expected: The new password opens the home screen with the account's thermostats. The old password is refused with 'Incorrect email or password'.

title: Handle cloud outage during update status check
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and running older firmware. The Dormouse cloud can be made unavailable while the Android device retains internet access.
steps: Make the Dormouse cloud unavailable.
Open the thermostat firmware status in the app.
Restore cloud access and refresh the status.
expected: The app clearly reports that firmware status cannot be retrieved while the cloud is unavailable. It does not display a misleading update success or failure, and status can be retrieved after service returns.

title: Check heating controls for a humidity sensor fault
preconditions: The thermostat is online and a test setup can trigger a humidity sensor fault. The dashboard shows device health or sensor status.
steps: Trigger a humidity sensor fault.
Open the zone's heating and device status pages.
Check humidity and heating controls.
Restore the humidity sensor and refresh.
expected: The dashboard reports the humidity fault, including E-221 where available, and does not show a fabricated humidity value. Heating controls remain available unless the fault prevents heating; the fault clears after recovery.

title: Prevent overlapping scheduled periods
preconditions: The thermostat has two periods on one day, and the editor offers period timing controls. The periods can be adjusted to create an overlap if validation is absent.
steps: Open the day's schedule and edit the second period.
Set its start time to overlap the first period, if the editor allows this input.
Attempt to save the schedule.
Review any validation message and the saved periods.
expected: The thermostat does not save an ambiguous overlapping schedule; it clearly identifies the invalid timing or adjusts it using a clear, consistent rule.

title: Check report at month boundary
preconditions: The home has energy data on the last day of a month and the first day of the next month. The Android device date is set correctly.
steps: Open the energy reports just after the month changes.
Open the new month's report.
Open the previous month's report.
expected: The new month and previous month have distinct periods, and data is attributed to the correct month.

title: Preserve sign-in email after a password error
preconditions: A Dormouse account exists and the sign-in screen is available.
steps: Enter the account email and an incorrect password.
Submit the form.
Review the fields after the error appears.
expected: The app keeps the email available for correction and clears or masks the password according to the app's security behaviour.

title: Check pairing after a thermostat restart
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A safe means to restart it is available without damaging the device.
steps: Open the pairing flow and reach the network selection screen.
Restart the thermostat using the approved method.
Wait for the display to return, then open pairing again.
expected: The thermostat restarts to a usable state and can enter pairing again. It does not show a false paired state or retain a corrupted selection.

title: Update with the dial turned during download
preconditions: The thermostat is online, an update is available, and its display shows update progress.
steps: Start the update and wait until progress is visible.
Turn the dial several times during the download.
Check the progress display and wait for completion.
expected: Dial input does not change the update selection or corrupt progress. The update finishes or continues with a clear, accurate status.

title: Pair with Bluetooth permission denied
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. Bluetooth access has not been granted to the app, and the thermostat is ready to pair.
steps: Start adding a thermostat.
Deny the Bluetooth permission request if it appears.
Review the app guidance.
Grant permission in iOS settings and retry.
expected: The app explains that the permission is needed for the pairing flow and does not falsely report success. After permission is granted, the user can resume or restart pairing.

title: Sign out and prevent access through browser back
preconditions: The tester is signed in to the web dashboard.
steps: Open an account page containing private information.
Use the dashboard sign-out control.
Use the browser Back button to revisit the private page.
Refresh the page.
expected: The account is signed out. Private account content is not accessible after sign-out, and the dashboard requests authentication.

title: Check report layout in landscape orientation
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, a report is available, and the device supports landscape orientation.
steps: Open a monthly report in portrait orientation.
Rotate the device to landscape.
Review the report and its navigation controls.
expected: The report remains usable in supported orientations, with values and controls visible and correctly labelled. If landscape is not supported, the app remains stable and preserves the report.

title: Run a boost for one zone
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in with permission to control the home. The home has at least two online zones.
steps: Open one zone's controls.
Start a one-hour boost.
Check the other zone's status.
expected: Boost is active for the selected zone for one hour. The other zone does not show boost as active.

title: Set a zone target to the lowest temperature
preconditions: A zone with an online thermostat exists. The Android app is signed in to the home.
steps: Open the zone's heating controls.
Set the target temperature to 5 degrees.
Check the app display and the thermostat display.
expected: Both displays show a target of 5 degrees. The app accepts the lowest supported target without rounding it up.

title: Check temperature stability in a steady room
preconditions: The thermostat is installed in a room with stable ambient conditions. The unit has been powered on long enough for its readings to settle.
steps: Note the displayed temperature.
Wait five minutes without touching the thermostat or changing room conditions.
Note the displayed temperature again.
Repeat the observation once.
expected: The temperature reading remains stable, with no unexplained repeated fluctuations. Any change is consistent with the room conditions and display resolution.

title: Check report after sharing access is removed
preconditions: The account has previously viewed a shared home's report. The home owner can remove the account's household access.
steps: Remove the account from the shared household using the owner's account.
Return to the Android app as the removed member.
Attempt to open the shared home's report.
expected: The removed member can no longer access the shared home's report, including through a previously open screen.

title: Check target temperature survives a restart
preconditions: Thermostat is paired and has a manually selected target temperature different from its scheduled target. Safe power isolation is available.
steps: Note the displayed target temperature.
Restart the thermostat using its approved power isolation method.
Wait for the home screen to return.
Check the displayed target temperature.
expected: The thermostat restarts without an unexpected error and shows the retained target, or the applicable scheduled target if the product specification says manual overrides do not persist.

title: Pair with a hidden 2.4 GHz network
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A hidden 2.4 GHz network is active, and its exact network name and password are known.
steps: Open pairing on the thermostat.
Choose the option to enter a network manually.
Enter the network name and password, then confirm.
Wait for the connection and pairing result.
expected: The thermostat connects to the hidden network and completes pairing. The display shows the ready state without an error code.

title: Receive an alert when a firmware update fails
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe test setup can simulate a failed thermostat firmware update without leaving the device unusable.
steps: Run the firmware update failure simulation.
Wait for the thermostat to report the failure.
Check the Android notification shade and app.
expected: A notification reports that the firmware update failed and identifies the affected thermostat. The app does not claim that the update completed successfully.

title: Verify error code remains legible after screen redraw
preconditions: The thermostat is displaying a recoverable error code such as E-110.
steps: Wait for at least one screen refresh or status update.
Observe the error code and its message.
Navigate away and return to the error view if supported.
expected: The code and message remain legible and consistent after screen redraw and navigation.

title: Check report for an unpaired thermostat
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to a household with no paired thermostats and no energy history.
steps: Open Energy reports.
Review the empty-state message and available actions.
expected: The app explains that no thermostat or report data is available and guides the user to an appropriate next step. It does not display fabricated usage.

title: Show required-field errors during sign-up
preconditions: The iOS app is open on the account creation screen.
steps: Leave all required fields blank.
Submit the form.
expected: The app marks the required fields and displays clear validation feedback without creating an account.

title: Check zone report when one zone has no data
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to a household with two zones; one has report data and the other has none for the selected month.
steps: Open the report for the zone with data.
Switch to the zone with no data.
expected: The first zone's data is shown only for that zone. The second zone shows a clear no-data state and does not inherit the first zone's values.

title: Verify schedule behaviour across daylight saving change
preconditions: A schedule is saved for a day affected by a daylight saving clock change. A supported test setup can simulate that date and time.
steps: Set a period close to the clock change.
Advance the test setup through the clock change.
Check the schedule and thermostat behaviour.
expected: The schedule handles the skipped or repeated local time consistently, without creating duplicate periods or losing the saved schedule. The app's displayed time agrees with the thermostat's schedule.

title: Check E-510 firmware failure display
preconditions: An approved test setup can simulate a firmware update failure without corrupting production firmware.
steps: Run the approved simulation of a failed firmware update.
Observe the thermostat display after the failure is reported.
Press the dial once and check that the display responds.
expected: The display shows E-510 for the failed firmware update. The thermostat remains responsive and does not falsely indicate a successful update.

title: Validate mismatched new password confirmation
preconditions: The tester is signed in and password change settings are open.
steps: Enter the correct current password.
Enter different values in the new password and confirmation fields.
Submit the change.
expected: The change is rejected and the confirmation mismatch is identified. The account password remains unchanged.

title: Respect Reduce Motion during account navigation
preconditions: The iOS app is installed. Reduce Motion is enabled in iOS settings, and the app is signed out.
steps: Open the app and navigate between sign-in and account recovery.
Return to sign-in and open the two-step verification screen using a test account.
Observe transitions and confirm controls remain usable.
expected: Account screens remain readable and usable with Reduce Motion enabled. Navigation avoids unnecessary motion effects and does not block or delay access to controls.

title: Open a report for a month with no data
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and there is a month in the report period with no recorded energy data.
steps: Open Energy reports.
Select the month with no recorded data.
expected: The app clearly indicates that no report data is available for that month. It does not show another month's data as if it belonged to the selected month.

title: Change password using the current password
preconditions: The tester is signed in to an account and knows its current password.
steps: Open account security settings.
Enter the current password and a new password that meets the rules.
Save the change.
Sign out and sign in with the new password.
expected: The password change succeeds and the new password works. The previous password no longer authenticates the account.

title: Check temperature display after sensor self-test
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and operating normally. The manufacturer's supported procedure for initiating a sensor self-test is available, if one exists.
steps: Record the current temperature and humidity readings.
Run the supported sensor self-test, if available.
Wait for the test to complete.
Check the display for readings or fault codes.
expected: After the self-test, the display returns to valid temperature and humidity readings if both sensors pass. Any detected sensor fault is clearly indicated using the applicable error code.

title: Reject a target below the supported range
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a configured zone.
steps: Add or edit a schedule period.
Try to enter a target below 5 degrees.
Attempt to save the period.
expected: The dashboard does not save an out-of-range target and identifies the permitted range of 5 to 30 degrees. No invalid value is applied to the schedule.

title: Check temperature display around freezing room conditions
preconditions: The thermostat is installed in a suitable controlled environment capable of safely reaching a temperature near zero degrees. The unit remains within its specified operating conditions.
steps: Record the displayed temperature at room conditions.
Gradually cool the environment towards zero degrees.
Observe the temperature display as it crosses the zero-degree point.
Stop cooling and restore safe room conditions.
expected: The display continues to show a valid temperature as the reading crosses zero degrees. There is no sign error, blank value, or sensor fault.

title: Sign out and return to the signed-in account
preconditions: The Android app is installed and signed in to a verified Dormouse account. The account has two-step verification disabled.
steps: Open the account or profile area.
Tap Sign out and confirm if prompted.
Reopen the app and sign in with the account's valid email and password.
expected: The app signs out and shows the sign-in screen. After valid credentials are entered, it opens the account's signed-in view.

title: Check that cleared faults are not repeatedly alerted
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe setup can simulate and then clear a thermostat fault.
steps: Simulate a thermostat fault and wait for its notification.
Clear the fault.
Wait for two minutes and check notifications.
expected: The original alert remains understandable, and the app reflects that the fault has cleared. No repeated alert claims that the cleared fault is still active.

title: Create the maximum number of zones
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. The home has no zones and has four available thermostats.
steps: Create a zone and assign one thermostat.
Repeat until four zones exist, assigning one thermostat to each.
Open the zones overview.
expected: The home can contain four zones, each with its assigned thermostat. All four zones are listed and usable.

title: Sign-in screen layout
preconditions: The app is installed and signed out.
steps: Open the app.
Check the sign-in screen shows the Dormouse logo, an email field, a password field, a Sign in button and a 'Reset your password' link.
Leave the password field empty and look at the Sign in button.
expected: Every element is visible without scrolling, and Sign in stays disabled until both fields are filled in.

title: Use away mode with TalkBack
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and paired with an online thermostat. TalkBack can be enabled on the phone.
steps: Enable TalkBack.
Navigate to the away mode control using screen reader navigation.
Activate the control and listen for its updated state.
expected: TalkBack announces the control name, its current state, and the updated state after activation. The control can be operated without relying on visual cues.

title: Check report layout in landscape
preconditions: A monthly report is available. Android screen auto-rotation is enabled.
steps: Open the monthly energy report in portrait orientation.
Rotate the device to landscape.
Review the report and its navigation controls.
expected: The report remains readable and usable in landscape, or the app maintains a clear supported layout without clipping essential information.

title: Stop a zone boost early
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in with permission to control the home. A one-hour boost is active on a zone.
steps: Open the boosted zone's controls.
Stop or cancel the boost.
Check the zone status.
expected: The boost is no longer active for that zone, and the app shows its normal heating control status.

title: Validate malformed email addresses
preconditions: The tester is signed out and the account registration page is open.
steps: Enter a malformed email address and a valid password.
Submit the form.
Review the email field and any validation message.
expected: The form rejects the malformed address and identifies the email field with a clear explanation. No account is created.

title: Edit schedule as a household member
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in as a household member with permission to manage schedules. The home has an online thermostat and a saved schedule.
steps: Open the thermostat schedule.
Change a period to a valid target and save.
Reopen the schedule.
expected: The member can save the schedule change and sees the saved value. The change is applied to the correct home and thermostat.

title: Check dashboard after sensor disconnect
preconditions: The thermostat is online and a test setup can disconnect its temperature sensor. The dashboard can display device errors.
steps: Disconnect the temperature sensor.
Refresh the zone heating page.
Review the temperature, target and device status.
Reconnect the sensor and refresh again.
expected: The dashboard identifies the temperature reading as unavailable or faulty and shows E-217 where available. It does not present a missing reading as a valid room temperature; the error clears after recovery.

title: Accept a household invitation
preconditions: An invitation has been sent to a valid email address. The invitee has access to the email account and can use the Android app.
steps: Open the invitation link on the Android device.
Sign in or create an account using the invited email address.
Accept the invitation.
expected: The invitee joins the household and can see its shared thermostat information. The owner sees the invitee as a household member.

title: Handle schedule periods in the wrong order
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the selected day has at least one saved period.
steps: Add or edit a period with a start time earlier than the preceding period.
Attempt to save the schedule.
Inspect the schedule.
expected: The app either orders periods chronologically or prevents the invalid ordering with a clear message. No period is silently assigned an unintended time.

title: Complete two-step verification with a valid code
preconditions: A Dormouse account has two-step verification enabled and the tester can access its configured second factor. The tester is signed out.
steps: Enter the correct email address and password.
Request or retrieve the current verification code.
Enter the code and submit it.
expected: The app signs in to the correct account after both factors are accepted. The code is not displayed in plain text after submission.

title: Accept a household invitation
preconditions: A valid household invitation has been sent to an email address. The invitee can access that email and the web dashboard.
steps: Open the invitation link while signed out.
Sign in or create an account using the invited email address.
Accept the invitation.
Open the home dashboard.
expected: The invitation is accepted and the invitee can access the shared home. The owner sees the invitee listed as a member.

title: Check display legibility from standing position
preconditions: The thermostat is mounted at its normal household height and is powered on. Room lighting is typical for the installation.
steps: Stand at the usual viewing distance.
Read the room temperature and target temperature.
Turn the dial once and read the updated target.
expected: The room and target temperatures are legible from the normal viewing distance, and the updated target is clearly distinguishable.

title: Check pairing screen readability from normal distance
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired and positioned at its normal installation height in ordinary indoor lighting.
steps: Open the pairing screens on the thermostat.
Read the prompts and network selection from a typical standing position.
Check that errors and the current selection are distinguishable.
expected: Pairing instructions, selection state and errors are legible at normal viewing distance. The user can identify the next action without needing to guess.

title: Set the minimum heating target
preconditions: The thermostat is online and controllable from the dashboard. No schedule or mode is preventing manual target changes.
steps: Open the target temperature control.
Set the target to 5 degrees.
Save the change.
Check the displayed target.
expected: The target is accepted and shown as 5 degrees. The dashboard does not allow a target below 5 degrees.

title: Check report for selected home
preconditions: The signed-in account can access two homes with different monthly energy data.
steps: Select the first home and open its monthly report.
Note the home name and report values.
Switch to the second home and open the same month's report.
expected: Each report is associated with the selected home and shows that home's data only.

title: Verify away mode persists after signing out
preconditions: The Android app is signed in to an owner account, and away mode is enabled. The phone has internet access.
steps: Sign out of the app.
Sign back in with the same account.
Open the home controls and view away mode.
expected: Away mode is still enabled and its existing settings are shown.

title: Receive a high temperature alert
preconditions: A user account is signed in and temperature alerts are enabled. A test condition or approved simulator can trigger a high temperature alert for the home.
steps: Trigger the high temperature alert condition.
Open the dashboard notifications view.
Inspect the new alert.
expected: A notification identifies the high temperature condition and the correct home or zone. The alert is visible in the dashboard without being duplicated.

title: A weekday schedule changes the temperature at the set times
preconditions: A paired thermostat and a test clock that can be moved forward.
steps: Create a Monday to Friday schedule: 19 degrees at 06:30, 16 degrees at 08:30.
Save it and move the test clock to 06:29 on a Tuesday.
Watch the target temperature as the clock passes 06:30 and 08:30.
expected: The target temperature changes to 19 at 06:30 and to 16 at 08:30, on the thermostat and in the app.

title: Cancel active boost
preconditions: The thermostat is online and boost is active. The iOS app is signed in.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Cancel boost.
Check the boost status.
expected: Boost is no longer active and the app returns to normal heating control.

title: Verify heating demand indication
preconditions: The thermostat is paired with a responsive boiler. Set a target above the room temperature, with heating demand permitted.
steps: Check the home screen while the room is below target.
Observe the heating status indication.
Lower the target below room temperature using an approved control method.
Check the heating status again.
expected: The display clearly indicates heating demand when the room is below target and no demand when the target is below room temperature. The displayed status agrees with boiler control state.

title: Check display behaviour during Wi-Fi loss
preconditions: Thermostat is paired and operating normally. The router can be switched off temporarily without disrupting mains power.
steps: Note the current target and room temperature on the display.
Switch off the router for several minutes.
Observe the display and use the dial to inspect local controls, without changing settings.
Restore the router and wait for reconnection.
expected: The display keeps local heating status usable during the outage and indicates connectivity loss if applicable. It returns to connected status after reconnection without losing the displayed target.

title: Check sensor display while the boost button is pressed
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live readings. Heating is available and the boost button is enabled.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Press the boost button to start a one-hour boost.
Check the sensor view while boost is active.
expected: The thermostat continues to show both live sensor readings while indicating that boost is active.

title: Check notification text with keyboard only
preconditions: A signed-in user has notifications available. A keyboard is available and pointer input is not used during the test.
steps: Navigate to the notifications view using the keyboard.
Move focus through the notification controls.
Open a notification using the keyboard.
expected: All notification controls can be reached and operated with the keyboard. Focus remains visible and the opened notification is identified clearly.

title: Update one thermostat in a zoned home
preconditions: The home has at least two paired thermostats in separate zones. An update is available for one thermostat only.
steps: Open the zone list in the Android app and record each thermostat's status.
Allow the selected thermostat's update to complete.
Check both zones and their controls in the app.
expected: Only the selected thermostat updates. The other zone remains online with its settings and controls unchanged.

title: Check report as a shared household member
preconditions: A household member has app access to a home with monthly report data. The member is signed in on Android.
steps: Open the shared home in the app.
Open its energy reports.
Check the report period and data.
expected: The member can view the report if their household access permits it, and the report belongs to the shared home.

title: Check away mode across app and thermostat
preconditions: The Android app is paired with a powered, connected thermostat. Away mode is off.
steps: Turn on away mode in the Android app.
Check the mode on the thermostat display.
Turn away mode off in the app.
expected: The thermostat reflects each confirmed change from the app. The app and thermostat show matching states after each change.

title: Check notification timing during an overnight update
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe test setup can simulate a firmware update during the 02:00 to 04:00 update window.
steps: Simulate an overnight update starting during the allowed window.
Check the phone during the update.
Check the phone after the update finishes.
expected: The app sends only status notifications configured for the update process and does not send a misleading failure alert during a successful update. Any completion alert arrives after the update finishes.

title: Check display with large text setting
preconditions: The thermostat offers a text-size or accessibility display setting. It is on the home screen.
steps: Enable the largest available text setting using the thermostat controls.
Inspect the home screen and navigate to a menu with longer labels.
Restore the original text size.
expected: Text is enlarged as requested and remains readable; essential values and controls are not lost or overlapped. Restoring the setting returns the original layout.

title: Attempt to add a seventh daily period
preconditions: The selected day already has six saved periods. The thermostat is paired and the schedule editor is available.
steps: Open the selected day's schedule.
Choose Add period.
Attempt to configure and save a seventh period.
expected: The thermostat does not add a seventh period and keeps the six existing periods unchanged.

title: Pair using a visible 2.4 GHz network
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network is available with its password, and the pairing app is ready on a phone.
steps: Open pairing on the thermostat using the dial.
Select the visible 2.4 GHz network.
Enter its password using the thermostat controls.
Confirm the details and wait for pairing to finish.
expected: The thermostat joins the selected network and completes pairing. Its display shows the paired or ready state without an error code.

title: Check report on a narrow browser window
preconditions: A report with data is available. The browser window can be resized to a narrow desktop width.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Resize the browser window to a narrow width.
Inspect the report and use its available controls.
expected: The report content adapts to the narrow viewport without obscuring figures or controls. Any necessary scrolling still allows the user to reach all report content and controls.

title: Check notification after signing out
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe test alert can be generated, and the user can sign out of the app.
steps: Sign out of the Android app.
Generate a test alert for the former account's home.
Check the Android notification shade.
Sign back in and review the alert.
expected: The signed-out app does not reveal private home or account details in a notification. After signing back in, the app follows its access rules and shows only alerts the account is permitted to view.

title: Set the maximum heating target
preconditions: The thermostat is online and controllable from the dashboard. No schedule or mode is preventing manual target changes.
steps: Open the target temperature control.
Set the target to 30 degrees.
Save the change.
Check the displayed target.
expected: The target is accepted and shown as 30 degrees. The dashboard does not allow a target above 30 degrees.

title: Check away mode across multiple zones
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to a home with two paired zones and away mode available.
steps: Open the home's away controls.
Enable away mode.
Check the status and target for each zone.
expected: Away mode is applied consistently to the zones according to the home's configured away behaviour. The app shows each zone's status and does not leave a zone silently on a conflicting home target.

title: Handle location services disabled
preconditions: Geofencing is enabled and location permission is granted. Android location services can be switched off.
steps: Switch off Android location services.
Open the Dormouse app.
Review the geofencing status.
expected: The app reports that location services prevent geofencing from working. Manual away mode remains usable and the app does not claim a location-based change occurred.

title: Attempt to create a fifth zone
preconditions: The home already has four zones. The Android app is signed in as the home owner.
steps: Open Zones and choose Add zone.
Enter a unique name and attempt to save.
Review the displayed result.
expected: A fifth zone is not created. The app clearly explains the four-zone limit and preserves the existing zones.

title: Reject a password missing a required character class
preconditions: The tester is signed out and the registration page displays the password composition rules.
steps: Enter a valid email and a password that omits one required character class.
Submit the form.
Review the password validation message.
expected: The password is rejected and the missing requirement is identified. No account is created.

title: Raise target by one half-degree
preconditions: The thermostat is online and the iOS app is signed in. Its current target is 20 degrees.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Increase the target once.
Check the displayed target in the app and on the thermostat.
expected: The target changes from 20 to 20.5 degrees and both displays agree.

title: Use the thermostat with reduced vision
preconditions: A thermostat is assigned to a zone and is ready for local control. The tester can assess the display at a typical standing distance with reduced vision.
steps: Wake the display and identify the zone and current target.
Turn the dial one detent and observe the feedback.
Press the dial and verify the confirmed target.
expected: Zone identity, target, and confirmation are readable at a typical standing distance with sufficient contrast. The change can be distinguished from the previous value.

title: Check temperature reading with nearby cold object
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live readings. A sealed, cool object is available and can be held near the unit without contact.
steps: Record the displayed temperature.
Hold the cool object near, but not against, the thermostat for one minute.
Remove it and observe the temperature for two minutes.
expected: The temperature responds to the local cooling if the nearby air changes, then trends back towards the room level; the display does not show an implausible sudden jump.

title: Handle disconnected temperature sensor
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and online. Its temperature sensor can be disconnected safely, and the Android app is signed in.
steps: Disconnect the temperature sensor.
Open heating controls in the Android app.
Check the thermostat display and app for sensor status.
expected: The thermostat displays E-217. The app identifies the temperature sensor problem and does not present a disconnected reading as a current valid temperature.

title: Check report after account session expires
preconditions: The iOS app has an expired or revoked account session and a monthly report is available online.
steps: Open Energy reports.
Attempt to load a report using the expired session.
expected: The app requests authentication or reports that the session has expired. It does not expose newly fetched private report data.

title: Receive failed firmware update notification
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. A paired thermostat is in a controlled test setup that can fail an overnight firmware update and report the result.
steps: Configure the test update to fail during the 02:00 to 04:00 update window.
Allow the update attempt to finish.
Check the iPhone notification centre and the thermostat status in the app.
expected: The app reports that the firmware update failed and identifies the affected thermostat. The notification does not claim that the update succeeded.

title: Set target temperature from iOS
preconditions: The thermostat is paired, online and controlling a responsive boiler. The iOS app is signed in and connected to the same home.
steps: Open the home screen in the iOS app.
Select the thermostat and set its target to 21 degrees.
Check the target shown in the app and on the thermostat.
expected: The app and thermostat show a target of 21 degrees. The boiler is called for heat if the measured temperature is below the target.

title: Check temperature response to a controlled cool change
preconditions: The thermostat is in a stable room and its displayed temperature has settled. A controlled source of slightly cooler room air is available without directing airflow at the sensor.
steps: Record the displayed temperature.
Introduce the cooler air into the room without touching the thermostat.
Wait for the room temperature to change gradually.
Observe the displayed temperature at intervals.
expected: The displayed temperature moves down as the room cools, without jumping erratically. The reading settles as the room conditions stabilise.

title: Set the maximum scheduled temperature
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the selected day has an editable schedule period. The thermostat is online.
steps: Edit the period's target temperature.
Set the target to 30 degrees.
Save and reopen the period.
expected: The app accepts and displays 30 degrees. The thermostat receives the 30 degree target.

title: Check display behaviour when humidity sensor is unavailable
preconditions: The thermostat is powered. A safe, manufacturer-approved method is available to make the humidity sensor unavailable without affecting the temperature sensor.
steps: Make the humidity sensor unavailable using the approved method.
Wait for the thermostat to detect the condition.
Check the displayed error and temperature reading.
expected: The display shows E-221 for the humidity sensor fault. The temperature reading remains available if its sensor is still functioning.

title: Open an expired invitation
preconditions: An invitation link is available that has passed its configured expiry time.
steps: Open the expired invitation link.
Try to accept it.
Return to the sign-in or sharing page.
expected: The expired invitation cannot be accepted and the dashboard explains that it is no longer valid. No household access is granted.

title: Copy a schedule to another day
preconditions: A saved schedule exists for one day and the Android app is signed in.
steps: Use the schedule copy or duplicate action for that day.
Choose a different day and confirm.
Open the destination day's schedule.
expected: The destination day contains the copied periods and temperatures. The source day's schedule is unchanged.

title: Check sensor readings while the thermostat is handled
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live sensor readings. The housing is accessible and safe to touch.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Hold the thermostat housing in your hands for one minute.
Release it and observe both readings for two minutes.
expected: The readings remain visible during handling and respond to the change in the device's immediate environment without freezing or showing an error.

title: Handle cloud loss while saving a schedule
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and online, with a thermostat schedule available to edit. A means to interrupt cloud connectivity is available.
steps: Interrupt the thermostat's or app's connection to the Dormouse cloud.
Change a schedule and attempt to save.
Restore connectivity and reopen the schedule.
expected: The app reports that the save cannot be confirmed while cloud service is unavailable and does not claim success. After connectivity returns, it shows the actual saved schedule.

title: Check away mode follows a schedule change
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, a schedule is configured, and away mode is active.
steps: Change the current schedule period's target in the app.
Save the schedule change.
Check the active target and away status.
expected: Away mode remains active and the thermostat continues to use the away target. The schedule change is saved for the applicable home operation without unexpectedly cancelling away mode.

title: Receive a notification for a humidity sensor fault
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe test setup can simulate a thermostat humidity sensor fault.
steps: Simulate a humidity sensor fault.
Wait for the app to receive the status.
Check the Android notification shade.
expected: A notification identifies a humidity sensor fault and the affected thermostat. It does not describe the fault as a temperature sensor failure.

title: Handle thermostat offline when changing target
preconditions: The Android app is signed in. The paired thermostat can be made unavailable to the Dormouse cloud without changing the phone connection.
steps: Make the thermostat unavailable to the cloud.
Attempt to change its target temperature in the app.
Restore the thermostat connection and check its target.
expected: The app reports that the thermostat is offline or that the change could not be confirmed. Once reconnected, the thermostat has not silently applied a different target.

title: Verify display during firmware update
preconditions: Thermostat has an approved firmware update available, sufficient power and a stable Wi-Fi connection. Run within the permitted update window or use an approved test method.
steps: Start the update using the supported procedure.
Observe the display through download, installation and restart.
Do not operate controls unless prompted.
Check the home screen after the update completes.
expected: The display provides clear update progress or status and does not appear frozen or invite unsafe interruption. After completion, the thermostat returns to normal operation with its settings retained.

title: Change a target while schedule is active
preconditions: A schedule is active for the zone and the thermostat is online. The dashboard offers a manual target change.
steps: Note the active scheduled target.
Set a different target using the manual control.
Save the change.
Check whether the dashboard shows a temporary override or schedule change.
expected: The dashboard clearly indicates how the manual change affects the active schedule, including any override duration if applicable. The selected target is applied without silently corrupting the saved schedule.

title: Check temperature display with rapid room cycling
preconditions: The thermostat is in a controlled environment that can be changed safely between two moderate temperatures. Do not exceed the unit's operating conditions.
steps: Record the initial displayed temperature.
Change the environment moderately warmer and observe the reading.
Change it back towards the initial condition and observe again.
Allow the environment to settle.
expected: The temperature reading follows the direction of each room change without oscillating independently of the environment. It settles as conditions stabilise.

title: Retry a report after connectivity returns
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, a report is available, and the cloud was unavailable during an initial load attempt.
steps: Restore the Dormouse cloud connection.
Retry loading the report.
expected: The report loads successfully after connectivity returns. The previous failure state is cleared and the selected month remains correct.

title: Handle pairing timeout
preconditions: The thermostat is in pairing mode and the Android app is ready to pair it. The phone is kept idle or prevented from completing setup until the pairing window expires.
steps: Start pairing in the app.
Allow the pairing process to remain incomplete until it times out.
Check the thermostat display and app, then restart pairing.
expected: The thermostat displays E-104 after the pairing attempt times out. The app reports the timeout and can begin a fresh pairing attempt.

title: Check E-312 boiler fault display
preconditions: An approved test setup can make the boiler report a fault safely.
steps: Use the approved setup to cause the boiler to report a fault.
Request heating from the thermostat.
Observe the displayed error.
expected: The thermostat displays E-312 for the boiler-reported fault and does not mislabel it as E-305.

title: Cancel unsaved schedule changes
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a saved schedule.
steps: Open a saved period and change its target temperature.
Cancel or navigate away without saving.
Reopen the period.
expected: The saved target remains unchanged. The dashboard does not apply the cancelled edit.

title: Handle an expired email verification link
preconditions: A Dormouse account exists with an unverified email address. Its verification link has expired.
steps: Open the expired verification link on the Android phone.
Return to the app and request a new verification email, if offered.
Open the new message and use its link.
expected: The expired link is rejected with a clear explanation. A newly issued link verifies the intended account.

title: Check boost button press does not alter target
preconditions: Boost is inactive and the target temperature is set to a known value.
steps: Note the displayed target temperature.
Press the boost button once.
Observe the target and boost status on the display.
expected: Boost activates and the normal target temperature remains unchanged.

title: Check no heating demand when room reaches target
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and the room can be warmed safely. The boiler is responsive and the target is set above the room temperature.
steps: Allow the heating to run until the room reading reaches the target.
Observe the heating status on the display.
expected: The thermostat stops requesting heat when the room reaches the target, subject to its normal control tolerance.

title: Set target temperature from the Android app
preconditions: The thermostat is paired, online and controlling a responsive boiler. The Android app is signed in and connected to the same home.
steps: Open heating controls for the thermostat.
Set the target temperature to 20 degrees.
Check the app and thermostat display.
expected: The app and thermostat show a target of 20 degrees. If the room is below target, the thermostat requests heat from the boiler.

title: Set a zone to the minimum target
preconditions: A thermostat is assigned to an active zone and is ready for local control.
steps: Turn the dial down until the target reaches 5 degrees.
Press the dial to confirm the target.
Turn the dial down once more.
expected: The target can be set to 5 degrees and does not go below it. The display remains clear and responsive at the lower limit.

title: Check local heating control without cloud access
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and operating normally. A controlled method is available to block cloud access while keeping local power and boiler connectivity available.
steps: Block the thermostat's access to the Dormouse cloud.
Change the target using the dial and confirm it.
Observe the display and boiler demand.
expected: The thermostat displays E-110 for the cloud connection failure. Local target adjustment remains available and heating demand follows the selected target.

title: Check dial control without relying on colour
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and showing the home screen. The tester can inspect the display using monochrome or colour-vision simulation if available.
steps: Change the target using the dial.
Inspect the target and heating status indicators.
Confirm the target.
expected: The target and heating status can be understood from text, numbers or shapes without relying on colour alone.

title: Avoid extending an active boost accidentally
preconditions: A one-hour boost is already active on an online thermostat. The dashboard displays the active boost control.
steps: Open the boost control.
Review its label and remaining time.
Select the control once.
Check the new boost status and expiry time.
expected: The dashboard clearly communicates whether the action cancels or restarts boost. It does not silently extend the boost without showing the updated expiry time.

title: Operate schedule controls without pressing dial
preconditions: A schedule is saved and the thermostat display and dial are working. The tester can turn the dial gently without pressing it.
steps: Turn the dial to bring up or move through the thermostat's schedule-related display, if available.
Observe the screen after each turn without pressing the dial.
Press the dial to open the highlighted item.
expected: Turning the dial changes the highlighted selection or value without activating it. Pressing the dial activates the selected item.

title: Receive boiler fault notification
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. A paired thermostat is connected to a test boiler simulator able to report a boiler fault.
steps: Cause the boiler simulator to report a fault.
Wait for the thermostat and app to receive the fault.
Check the iPhone notification centre and open the notification.
expected: A fault notification identifies the affected thermostat or zone and gives the available fault information. Opening it takes the user to relevant fault details without reporting a different fault.

title: Check boost button during a screen warning
preconditions: A non-blocking warning that does not prevent normal operation is present on the display. Heating is otherwise available.
steps: Press the boost button once.
Check the warning and boost status on the display.
Press the boost button again if safe to cancel the test boost.
expected: The warning remains readable and the boost action is registered only if the warning permits it. The display gives a clear indication of whether boost started.

title: Pair with a full household member list
preconditions: The home already has an owner and eight members. The thermostat is powered, unpaired, and near a known 2.4 GHz network with a valid password.
steps: Start pairing on the thermostat.
Select the available 2.4 GHz network and enter its password.
Confirm the details and wait for the result.
expected: The thermostat pairs with the home even though its household member limit is reached. The display confirms connection and does not report a household-sharing error.

title: Boost button heats for one hour then returns to the schedule
preconditions: A thermostat following a schedule, with a test clock.
steps: Press the boost button once.
Move the test clock forward 60 minutes.
expected: Heating comes on straight away and the display counts down from 60. After an hour the thermostat goes back to the scheduled temperature.

title: Pair a replacement after removing the old thermostat
preconditions: A thermostat has been removed from the app, and a replacement thermostat is in pairing mode. The Android app is signed in to the intended home.
steps: Open the home and start adding a thermostat.
Pair the replacement using a valid 2.4 GHz network.
Check the home device list and its thermostat details.
expected: The replacement is added to the intended home as one device. The removed thermostat is not shown as online or duplicated.

title: View the current monthly energy report
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to an owner account with a paired thermostat and an available report for the current month.
steps: Open the iOS app.
Open Energy reports.
Select the current month.
expected: The report opens and identifies the selected month. Its energy data and any displayed totals match the data available for that month.

title: Check mains power interruption recovery
preconditions: The thermostat is operating normally with a known target set. A safe, controlled method is available to interrupt and restore mains power.
steps: Interrupt mains power to the thermostat.
Restore mains power.
Wait for the thermostat to restart and inspect its display.
expected: The thermostat displays E-402 during the interruption. After power is restored, it restarts and returns to normal operation with the previously set target retained.

title: Invite an address with invalid format
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard and can open household sharing settings.
steps: Enter an email address without a valid format.
Try to send the invitation.
expected: The dashboard rejects the address and explains that a valid email address is required. No invitation is created or sent.

title: Check display and controls recover after error clears
preconditions: The thermostat is displaying a recoverable error such as E-101, and the cause can be corrected during the test.
steps: Observe the error screen and note its message.
Correct the underlying condition.
Wait for the thermostat to update, then use the dial to navigate.
expected: The error indication clears or changes appropriately when its cause is resolved, and the display and controls return to normal operation.

title: Check temperature response to a controlled warm change
preconditions: The thermostat is in a stable room and its displayed temperature has settled. A safe way to warm the room gradually is available.
steps: Record the displayed temperature.
Gradually warm the room without directing heat at the thermostat.
Observe the displayed temperature at intervals.
Stop when the room conditions stabilise.
expected: The displayed temperature trends up as the room warms, without implausible abrupt changes. The reading settles as the room conditions stabilise.

title: Open a notification from the lock screen
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, lock screen notifications are allowed, and a paired thermostat can generate a test notification. The iPhone is locked.
steps: Generate a test notification from the thermostat or app.
Tap the notification on the lock screen.
Authenticate if iOS requests it.
expected: The notification opens the relevant screen in the iOS app after any required authentication. No account or thermostat controls are exposed on the lock screen beyond the user's iOS privacy settings.

title: Recover pairing after switching apps
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The thermostat is ready to pair on a suitable 2.4 GHz network.
steps: Start pairing and reach the network details step.
Switch to another app for one minute.
Return to the Dormouse app.
Resume or restart pairing and complete setup.
expected: The app preserves valid entered information or clearly explains that the flow must be restarted. It does not show a false success or create duplicate thermostats.

title: Create an account with valid details
preconditions: The Android app is installed and the tester has an email address not registered with Dormouse. The phone has internet access.
steps: Open the app and choose to create an account.
Enter a valid email address and a password that meets the displayed requirements.
Accept the required terms and submit the form.
Complete any verification the app requests.
expected: The account is created and the app confirms success. The tester is signed in or is prompted to sign in.

title: Delete one schedule period
preconditions: A schedule with at least two periods exists for the selected day. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open the selected day's schedule editor.
Delete one period and save.
Reopen the schedule.
expected: The deleted period is absent. All other periods remain saved with their original settings.

title: Refresh schedules after reconnecting
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and a thermostat has a saved schedule. The phone can be temporarily disconnected from the internet.
steps: Disconnect the phone from the internet.
Change a schedule and note any save status shown.
Reconnect the phone and refresh the schedule.
expected: The app clearly reports whether the offline change was saved or could not be saved. After reconnection, the displayed schedule matches the confirmed saved version.

title: Check Dynamic Type on update screen
preconditions: The iOS device's text size is set to the largest supported Dynamic Type size. The app is signed in and a thermostat's firmware screen is available.
steps: Open the firmware screen in the iOS app.
Read the version, status, warning and available controls.
Navigate to any update details or error message.
expected: Text remains readable and essential status and controls are not clipped or obscured. The user can reach update details and actions at the enlarged text size.

title: Confirm member cannot transfer ownership
preconditions: The test account is an accepted household member, not the owner. The household has at least one other member.
steps: Open household sharing settings as the member.
Look for an ownership transfer option or attempt to open its route.
Review the available actions and app response.
expected: The member cannot transfer ownership. No ownership change is made, and the owner remains unchanged.

title: Pair a thermostat on a 2.4 GHz network
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The thermostat is powered on, nearby, and the iPhone is connected to a working 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.
steps: Open the app and choose to add a thermostat.
Select the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network and enter its password.
Follow the app instructions to start pairing.
Wait for pairing to finish.
expected: The thermostat pairs successfully and appears in the app with its online status. No pairing error is shown.

title: Pair thermostat already associated with another home
preconditions: The thermostat has previously been paired to a different Dormouse home. The Android app is signed into a separate account, and the thermostat can be reset to pairing mode.
steps: Start pairing from the second account's app.
Attempt to add the thermostat using valid 2.4 GHz network details.
Follow any ownership or reset guidance shown.
expected: The app does not silently expose the thermostat to the second home. It clearly explains the existing association and provides an authorised way to transfer or reset it.

title: Remove a thermostat from a zone
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone contains an online thermostat and another zone is available.
steps: Open the assigned thermostat's zone controls.
Remove it from the zone without deleting the thermostat from the home.
Save and inspect the zone.
expected: The thermostat is no longer assigned to the zone but remains registered to the home. The zone shows no assigned thermostat if none remain.

title: Handle stale location while away
preconditions: Geofencing is enabled in the Android app, and the phone has a previously recorded location. Away mode is off.
steps: Set the phone location permission to allow access only while using the app.
Leave the app closed and move outside the home geofence.
Reopen the app and inspect away mode.
expected: The app does not use the stale location to enable away mode. It shows the current away state accurately and requests or explains the location access needed for geofencing.

title: Use schedule controls with TalkBack
preconditions: TalkBack is enabled on the Android phone. The user is signed in and can open a thermostat schedule.
steps: Navigate the schedule editor using TalkBack.
Focus a period's time, temperature and save controls.
Change a value and save using spoken navigation.
expected: Interactive schedule controls have meaningful spoken labels and state. The user can change and save a period without relying on visual position alone.

title: Remove a household member
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the iOS app and the home has at least one accepted member. The member can check their app during the test.
steps: Open household sharing and select the accepted member.
Choose to remove the member and confirm.
On the member's iPhone, refresh the home list.
expected: The member is removed from the home and can no longer access it in the app.

title: Update with backup batteries low
preconditions: An update is available and the thermostat displays E-401 for low backup batteries. Mains power is stable.
steps: Open the firmware update option on the thermostat.
Attempt to start the update.
Read the resulting message and check the update state.
expected: The thermostat either safely permits updating on stable mains or clearly blocks it with a battery warning. It does not begin an update that cannot be recovered safely.

title: Reject an incorrect Wi-Fi password
