expected: The thermostat displays E-401 while backup batteries are low. The warning clears after normal battery power is restored.

title: Reject a 5 GHz-only network
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A 5 GHz-only Wi-Fi network is available, with no 2.4 GHz network available.
steps: Open pairing and scan for networks.
Check whether the 5 GHz-only network is offered.
If offered, attempt to select it and continue.
expected: The thermostat does not complete pairing over the 5 GHz-only network. It either excludes the network from selection or clearly indicates that a compatible network is required.

title: Handle mains interruption during update
preconditions: The thermostat can report E-402 after a controlled power interruption. An update is available, and the test can be performed safely by a qualified person.
steps: Start or schedule an update in an approved test setup.
Interrupt mains power at a controlled point in the test.
Restore power and check the thermostat and app status.
expected: After power returns, the thermostat recovers to a safe state and reports an accurate update result or E-510 if the update failed. The app does not claim success unless the new firmware is confirmed.

title: Verify highlighted item is visually distinct
preconditions: A menu is open with at least two selectable items.
steps: Turn the dial until a different item is highlighted.
Observe the highlighted and unhighlighted items.
Move the highlight back once.
expected: The current item is unambiguously distinguishable from other items on every selection change.

title: Reject an unregistered email at sign-in
preconditions: The tester has an email address that is not registered and is on the sign-in page.
steps: Enter the unregistered email and a password.
Submit the form.
Review the response.
expected: Sign-in is denied and private account information is not disclosed. The response is clear and consistent with the dashboard's account security policy.

title: Check report labels with a screen reader
preconditions: A screen reader is installed and running in the test browser. The user can open an energy report with data.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Navigate through the report using screen reader reading commands.
Listen to the report controls, headings and energy values.
expected: The screen reader announces meaningful page and report headings, control names, selected options and energy values with their labels and units. No essential report information is available only through visual styling.

title: Prevent member access to owner-only sharing controls
preconditions: The user is an accepted household member, not the owner, and is signed in to the iOS app.
steps: Open the shared home.
Open household sharing.
Check the available controls for managing invitations and members.
Try to access any owner-only control.
expected: The member can view only the sharing information permitted to them and cannot invite, remove, or change members as the owner.

title: Cancel a pending invitation
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the iOS app and the home has a pending invitation that has not been accepted.
steps: Open household sharing for the home.
Select the pending invitation.
Choose to cancel or revoke it and confirm if prompted.
Check the invitation list.
expected: The pending invitation is no longer active and is shown as cancelled or removed.

title: Keep the owner from removing themselves
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the iOS app and is listed in household sharing as the owner.
steps: Open household sharing for the home.
Select the owner's own entry.
Try to remove or leave the home using the member removal control.
expected: The app does not remove the owner through the member removal control and explains that owner access cannot be removed this way.

title: Password reset email arrives within two minutes
preconditions: A Dormouse account with a mailbox the tester can read.
steps: Open the web dashboard and choose 'Forgot your password?'.
Enter the account's email address and submit.
Start a timer and watch the mailbox.
expected: An email from Dormouse with a reset link arrives within two minutes. The link opens a page to choose a new password.

title: Reject a household invitation
preconditions: A valid household invitation is pending for the test account. The invitation has not expired or been withdrawn.
steps: Open the invitation link.
Choose to decline the invitation.
Return to the Android app and open household sharing.
expected: The account does not join the household. The invitation is marked declined or no longer available, and no household devices are shared with the account.

title: Check schedule while offline
preconditions: A schedule is saved on the thermostat. Wi-Fi can be disconnected without removing power, and the thermostat can still be operated locally.
steps: Disconnect the thermostat from Wi-Fi.
Open Schedules using the dial.
Review a saved period and make a local schedule change.
Reconnect Wi-Fi and check the schedule again.
expected: The thermostat can display and save schedule settings locally while offline. The saved schedule remains present after reconnection.

title: Check notification for humidity sensor fault
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. A paired thermostat is in a test setup that can report a humidity sensor fault.
steps: Simulate a humidity sensor fault.
Wait for the app to receive the status.
Check the iPhone notification centre.
expected: The app reports the humidity sensor fault and identifies the affected thermostat. It does not show a misleading humidity reading as current.

title: Verify update result after pairing timeout
preconditions: The thermostat can be made to report E-104 pairing timed out, and an update is available. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Cause a pairing timeout before the update check.
Open the thermostat status in the app.
Restore the pairing or network connection and check firmware status again.
expected: The app identifies the pairing or connectivity issue without presenting it as a firmware failure. After reconnection, the app retrieves the actual update status.

title: Verify temperature reading after a sudden warm-air change
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live sensor readings. A safe, controllable source of warm air is available; do not direct hot air at the device.
steps: Record the displayed temperature.
Briefly direct warm air near the thermostat without touching it.
Remove the warm-air source and observe the display for two minutes.
expected: The displayed temperature rises in response to the local change and then trends back towards the room temperature after the source is removed.

title: Check notification contrast and status cues
preconditions: A signed-in user has both read and unread notifications. The dashboard is viewed at normal zoom with browser accessibility inspection available.
steps: Open the notifications view.
Compare read and unread notification styling.
Inspect status indicators and text contrast.
expected: Read and unread states are distinguishable without relying on colour alone. Notification text and status cues remain legible against their backgrounds.

title: Check sensor display after repeated button presses
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and showing its normal sensor screen. The boost function is not active.
steps: Press the boost button once.
Press it again to cancel or dismiss the resulting state, as applicable.
Wait for the normal sensor screen to appear.
Check the displayed temperature and humidity.
expected: The sensor screen returns with valid temperature and humidity values. Button presses do not cause missing, frozen, or malformed readings.

title: Handle an unresponsive boiler in a zone
preconditions: A zone is paired to a thermostat connected to a test boiler that can be made unresponsive. The Android app is signed in to the home.
steps: Make the test boiler stop responding.
Open the affected zone and request a heating change.
Check the app status and the thermostat display.
expected: The app reports that heating could not be delivered for the affected zone. The thermostat displays E-305, and other zones remain available.

title: Respect update permissions for a household member
preconditions: A household member without update-management permission is signed in to Android. The thermostat has an available update.
steps: Open the thermostat firmware status as the member.
Check whether an update control is available.
Attempt to access any update action shown.
expected: The app follows the home's permission rules and prevents unauthorised update management. The member receives a clear explanation rather than a silent failure.

title: Apply a schedule to a zone
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone has an online thermostat and a schedule can be configured.
steps: Open the schedule for the zone.
Add two periods with different valid target temperatures.
Save the schedule and reopen it.
expected: Both periods and their target temperatures remain saved for the selected zone. The schedule is associated with that zone, not another zone.

title: Check available networks can be rescanned
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A 2.4 GHz network is switched on after pairing setup has opened.
steps: Open the Wi-Fi network selection screen.
Switch on the 2.4 GHz network and allow it to become available.
Use the thermostat's rescan option, if shown.
Select the newly available network.
expected: The rescan lists the newly available network. The user can select it and proceed with pairing.

title: Schedule different targets for different days
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and the schedule editor is available. At least two days can be edited.
steps: Set a period on one day to a chosen target and save it.
Open a different day and set the same period time to a different target.
Save the second day's schedule.
Review both days.
expected: Each day retains its own target; editing the second day does not change the first day's period.

title: Check sensor readings with ventilation near the unit
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live sensor readings. A fan can circulate room air without blowing directly onto the thermostat.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Run the fan to circulate room air for three minutes.
Turn the fan off and observe both readings for two minutes.
expected: Both readings remain available and change only if the air conditions around the thermostat change; neither reading becomes blank or erroneous.

title: Receive a pairing timeout notification
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A thermostat is ready to pair, and a safe setup can allow the pairing attempt to time out.
steps: Start pairing in the Android app.
Allow the pairing attempt to time out without completing it.
Check the Android notification shade and app.
expected: The app reports that pairing timed out and offers a clear way to try again. It does not show the thermostat as successfully paired.

title: Prevent inviting the owner's own email
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the Android app with a known account email address.
steps: Open the invite-member form.
Enter the owner's account email address.
Try to send the invitation.
expected: The app rejects the owner's email with a clear explanation. No invitation or duplicate membership is created.

title: Use heating controls with enlarged Android text
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and connected to a paired thermostat. Android display or font size is set to the largest supported setting.
steps: Open the heating screen.
Review the target, temperature, and boost controls.
Change the target and check that feedback remains visible.
expected: Text and controls remain readable and usable without essential information being clipped or obscured. The target change is clearly confirmed.

title: Verify member access after signing out
preconditions: The test account is an accepted household member with a working Android app session.
steps: Sign out of the Android app.
Sign back in using the same member account.
Open the household view.
expected: The account still belongs to the household and sees the same shared devices and information. Signing out does not remove or duplicate membership.

title: Set minimum target temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is online and the iOS app is signed in. The current target is above 5 degrees.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Set the target to 5 degrees.
Try to decrease the target further.
expected: The target is 5 degrees. The app does not allow a target below 5 degrees.

title: Avoid duplicate notifications after refresh
preconditions: A user account is signed in and a known notification is visible in the dashboard.
steps: Note the notification message and timestamp.
Refresh the dashboard page.
Check the notification list for that event.
expected: Refreshing does not create a second notification for the same event. The original notification remains available with its original timestamp.

title: Navigate account forms with TalkBack
preconditions: TalkBack is enabled on the Android phone. The tester is signed out and can open the sign-in and registration forms.
steps: Navigate each form using TalkBack swipe gestures.
Listen to the labels and states of the email, password, and action controls.
Activate a form action using TalkBack.
expected: Controls are announced with meaningful labels, roles, and states in a logical order. The tester can identify and activate the intended actions without relying on sight.

title: Rotate dial to lower the target temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and not in a menu. The target is above 5 degrees.
steps: Turn the dial anticlockwise several clicks.
Read the target temperature on the display.
expected: The target temperature decreases in half-degree steps. The displayed value matches the selected target.

title: Check sensor reading visibility for colour vision deficiency
preconditions: The thermostat is displaying temperature and humidity. A tester with colour vision deficiency or a suitable assessment method is available.
steps: Inspect the sensor screen in its normal state.
Identify each reading using its text label and digits.
Check that any status colours do not obscure or replace the labels.
Repeat after waking the display if it was asleep.
expected: Temperature and humidity can be identified from text and digits without relying on colour alone. Relevant values remain distinguishable in the normal screen state.

title: Prevent adding a seventh daily period
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has a zone with six periods saved for the test day.
steps: Open the test day's schedule.
Try to add another period.
expected: The dashboard prevents a seventh period from being added and clearly explains the six-period limit. The existing six periods remain unchanged.

title: Check report with VoiceOver
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, a monthly report is available, and VoiceOver is enabled on the iPhone.
steps: Open Energy reports with VoiceOver enabled.
Navigate through the month selector and report values.
Move to any report chart or graphic.
expected: VoiceOver announces the report month, key values and controls with meaningful labels and order. Any chart information needed to understand the report is available in an accessible form.

title: Check password entry with Android autofill
preconditions: Android autofill or a password manager has a saved Dormouse test account. The tester is signed out.
steps: Open the sign-in form and invoke Android autofill.
Select the saved Dormouse credentials.
Submit the form.
expected: The correct credentials populate the intended fields without being exposed in the wrong field. Sign-in succeeds if the saved credentials are current.

title: Pair with Android battery optimisation enabled
preconditions: Android battery optimisation is enabled for the Dormouse app. The thermostat is in pairing mode and a 2.4 GHz network is available.
steps: Start pairing and submit valid network details.
Leave the app in the foreground while the device connects.
Wait for the completion status and check the thermostat list.
expected: Battery optimisation does not interrupt the foreground pairing flow. The app reports completion only after the thermostat has been added.

title: Set the minimum scheduled temperature
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the selected day has an editable schedule period. The thermostat is online.
steps: Edit the period's target temperature.
Set the target to 5 degrees.
Save and reopen the period.
expected: The app accepts and displays 5 degrees. The thermostat receives the 5 degree target.

title: Copy a schedule between days
preconditions: One day has a saved schedule and another day has a different or empty schedule. The thermostat is paired.
steps: Open the source day's schedule.
Choose the schedule copy option and select the destination day.
Confirm the copy.
Review the source and destination schedules.
expected: The destination day matches the copied schedule. The source day remains unchanged.

title: Check humidity display at humid-room conditions
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and its humidity sensor is connected. The room is humid but within the sensor's supported operating range.
steps: Wake the thermostat display.
Read the humidity value.
Check that the value is legible.
expected: The thermostat displays a numeric humidity percentage within the valid 0 to 100 percent range and shows no humidity fault.

title: Check screen reader labels in sharing
preconditions: TalkBack is enabled on the Android device. The owner is signed in and household sharing settings are available.
steps: Navigate the sharing screen using TalkBack gestures.
Move focus through the member list and invitation controls.
Activate a member action and listen to its confirmation or prompt.
expected: TalkBack announces meaningful labels, roles, and states for sharing controls and members. Focus order is usable, and destructive actions have an understandable confirmation.

title: Use account forms with enlarged text
preconditions: Android display or font size is set to its largest supported setting. The tester is signed out and can open the sign-in form.
steps: Open the sign-in form.
Inspect the fields, labels, errors, and primary action at enlarged text size.
Enter valid credentials and submit.
expected: Text remains readable and important controls remain visible and operable without overlap or clipping. Sign-in can be completed at the enlarged setting.

title: Pair using iPhone in landscape orientation
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The thermostat is ready to pair, and the iPhone supports landscape orientation in the app.
steps: Rotate the iPhone to landscape.
Start adding a thermostat.
Enter valid network details and complete pairing.
expected: The pairing screens and controls remain usable in landscape, with no essential content hidden. Pairing completes successfully.

title: Navigate update status with TalkBack
preconditions: TalkBack is enabled on the Android device. The app is signed in and the thermostat has an update status to display.
steps: Navigate to the thermostat firmware status using TalkBack.
Swipe through the status text and available actions.
Activate a safe status or help action using TalkBack.
expected: TalkBack announces the thermostat identity, firmware status, errors and actions in a meaningful order. Interactive controls have accessible names and can be activated without sight.

title: Verify controls after successful update
preconditions: A firmware update has just completed successfully on the thermostat. The boiler is available for a controlled heating check.
steps: Use the dial to change the target by one half-degree step.
Press the dial to confirm the selection.
Press the boost button and inspect the displayed mode.
expected: The dial changes the target by exactly one half-degree step and confirms it correctly. The boost button works as expected and the thermostat displays the resulting heating state accurately.

title: Pair one thermostat twice from the same account
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. One thermostat is already paired to the account and online.
steps: Open the add-thermostat flow again.
Attempt to pair the same thermostat a second time.
Review any duplicate-device message.
Return to the home device list.
expected: The app prevents a duplicate entry or directs the user to the existing thermostat. The account shows only one entry for the device.

title: Preserve schedule after firmware update
preconditions: A schedule with at least two different target temperatures is configured. An update is available for the paired thermostat.
steps: Record the scheduled periods and target temperatures in the app.
Allow the update to complete overnight.
Review the schedule and verify the next scheduled change.
expected: All schedule periods and targets remain unchanged after the update. The next scheduled temperature change occurs at its configured time.

title: Add a zone from the iOS app
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in as the home owner. One thermostat is paired to the home, and a second unassigned thermostat is powered on nearby.
steps: Open the home and choose the option to add a zone.
Follow the app prompts to pair the second thermostat.
Name the new zone and save it.
expected: The second thermostat is paired and listed as a separate zone in the home. Its zone name is shown in the app.

title: Reject a two-step code after its expiry
preconditions: A Dormouse account has two-step verification enabled. The tester can obtain a code and wait until it expires.
steps: Request or retrieve a verification code.
Wait until the code expires.
Enter the expired code and submit it.
expected: The expired code is rejected. The app explains that a current code is required and allows the tester to request or enter a valid code.

title: Check sensor readings with large text setting
preconditions: The thermostat offers a larger-text or accessibility display setting. Both sensors are functioning.
steps: Enable the largest available text setting.
Return to the normal screen.
Check the temperature and humidity readings.
expected: Both readings and their units remain visible and distinguishable in the larger-text setting, with no clipped digits or overlapping labels.

title: Pair when the household has reached its thermostat limit
preconditions: The signed-in owner account already has four thermostats assigned across its zones. A further thermostat is in pairing mode and available on a working 2.4 GHz network.
steps: Start adding the thermostat in the iOS app.
Select the available Wi-Fi network and proceed until the app checks the home's thermostat capacity.
Review the message and return to the home overview.
expected: The app clearly reports that the home has reached the four-thermostat limit and does not add the new thermostat. Existing thermostats and zones remain unchanged.

title: Prevent duplicate invitations
preconditions: The owner is signed in and has already sent a pending invitation to a valid email address.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Try to invite the same email address again.
Review the app response and pending list.
expected: The app prevents a duplicate invitation or explains that one is already pending. Only one pending invitation for that email address is shown.

title: Handle loss of connection while inviting
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the iOS app and has a home with an available member place. The iPhone can have its network connection disabled during the test.
steps: Open household sharing and enter a valid email address.
Disable the iPhone's network connection.
Try to send the invitation.
Restore the network and check the invitation list.
expected: The app reports that it could not send the invitation and does not show it as successfully sent unless it is actually created after reconnection.

title: Check no duplicate alert for one event
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. A paired thermostat is online and able to generate a repeatable test event.
steps: Generate one test event.
Wait for the notification and note its content.
Keep the phone online and wait for any delayed delivery.
Check whether the same event appears more than once.
expected: One event produces no duplicate notification. The event remains correctly identifiable in the app.

title: Frost warning notification when the house drops below 5 degrees
preconditions: A thermostat on the test bench with its temperature reading overridden, and notifications allowed on the phone.
steps: Set the overridden reading to 4.5 degrees.
Wait one minute and look at the phone.
expected: A 'Frost warning' notification arrives, and frost protection turns the heating on whatever mode the thermostat is in.

title: View report for a selected zone
preconditions: The user's home has at least two configured zones with report data. The user can access the web dashboard.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Select one zone from the zone control.
Select a different zone from the zone control.
expected: The report identifies the selected zone and shows its report data. Changing zones updates the report to the newly selected zone.

title: Check boost button press while boost is active
preconditions: A one-hour boost is active.
steps: Press the boost button briefly once.
Observe the display and boost status.
Check that the display remains responsive.
expected: The press follows the documented boost-button behaviour and does not create an invalid duration or freeze the display.

title: Check report at high browser zoom
preconditions: A report with data is available. The browser can zoom the page to 200 percent.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Set browser zoom to 200 percent.
Inspect the report and operate its period and zone controls.
expected: Report labels and values remain readable and controls remain usable at 200 percent zoom. Essential information is not clipped or hidden behind overlapping content.

title: Decline a household invitation
preconditions: A valid household invitation is available to the invitee. The invitee can access the invitation on an iPhone.
steps: Open the invitation link on the iPhone.
Choose to decline the invitation.
Return to the Dormouse app and open the home list.
expected: The invitation is declined, and the home is not added to the invitee's app.

title: Check notification accessibility and contrast
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and a paired thermostat can generate a test notification. Enable iOS Increase Contrast and, where available, Differentiate Without Colour.
steps: Generate a test notification and open its details in the app.
Review text, icons, status indicators and action controls.
Navigate the screen using touch and any enabled accessibility settings.
expected: Notification details and controls remain distinguishable without relying on colour alone. Text and controls remain legible and usable with the selected accessibility settings.

title: Check sensor display after repeated dial turns
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and showing its normal sensor screen. No settings menu is open.
steps: Turn the dial several clicks in one direction.
Turn it several clicks in the opposite direction.
Allow the display to return to the sensor screen if it changes.
Check the temperature and humidity values.
expected: Both sensor values remain available and correctly formatted after the dial activity. The display does not become stuck on partial or corrupted values.

title: Handle periods entered out of time order
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and a schedule editor is open for a day with at least two periods.
steps: Set the later period to an earlier time than the preceding period.
Save the schedule.
expected: The app either orders the periods chronologically or prevents saving and explains the time-order requirement. It does not show a misleading saved order.

title: Check report as a household member
preconditions: A household owner has shared access with a member account, and the household has report data.
steps: Sign in to the iOS app as the household member.
Open Energy reports.
Open a month with available data.
expected: The member can view the report if their household access permits it. The report is for the correct shared household, not the member's unrelated household.

title: Set a period at the end of the day
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and a schedule editor is open.
steps: Set a schedule period to start at 23:30.
Save and reopen the schedule.
expected: The period is saved and displayed at 23:30 on the intended day, without being moved to another day.

title: Check TalkBack reads a thermostat notification clearly
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. TalkBack is available and enabled, and a safe test alert can be generated.
steps: Enable TalkBack if it is not already enabled.
Generate a thermostat alert.
Focus the notification with TalkBack.
Listen to the spoken notification.
expected: TalkBack announces the notification text and relevant control without omitting the alert's meaning. The spoken text does not rely on colour or an icon alone.

title: Receive low battery notification
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. A paired thermostat is running on backup batteries in a test setup that can report low battery.
steps: Set the thermostat to report low backup battery.
Wait for the app to receive the status.
Check the iPhone notification centre.
expected: A low battery notification identifies the affected thermostat. The notification does not imply that mains power has failed.

title: Remove a zone from the home
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in as the home owner. The home has at least two zones.
steps: Open settings for a zone that is not the only zone.
Choose the option to remove the zone and confirm.
Return to the zone list.
expected: The removed zone no longer appears in the home. The other zones remain available and unchanged.

title: Check frost protection above its target
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on, frost protection is active, the boiler is responsive, and the room temperature is above 5 degrees.
steps: Observe the thermostat's heating status.
Check the boiler's heat-demand indicator.
expected: The thermostat does not request heat while the room temperature is above the 5 degree frost protection target.

title: Handle location permission changed to Never
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, geofencing is enabled, and location permission is set to Always. The home is currently in its normal occupied state.
steps: In iOS Settings, change Dormouse location permission to Never.
Return to the app and open away settings.
Check the geofencing status and any guidance shown.
expected: The app indicates that geofencing cannot operate without location permission and provides a route or instructions to restore permission. The home does not switch to away mode solely because permission was revoked.

title: Prevent repeated sign-in attempts after lockout
preconditions: An account is available and signed out. The test environment's documented sign-in attempt limit is known.
steps: Submit an incorrect password repeatedly until the documented limit is reached.
Attempt to sign in with the correct password.
Review the response and any recovery guidance.
expected: The app applies the documented lockout or delay and does not grant access during it. It explains how to proceed without revealing whether the account exists.

title: Handle unsupported Wi-Fi security during pairing
preconditions: A 2.4 GHz access point is configured with a Wi-Fi security mode unsupported by the thermostat. The Android app is signed in, and the thermostat is in pairing mode.
steps: Start thermostat setup in the app.
Select the test access point and enter its valid password.
Submit the network details.
Read the app message and check the thermostat display.
expected: The app explains that the selected network security mode cannot be used and does not claim that pairing succeeded. The thermostat remains available for another setup attempt.

title: Check sensor readings when the thermostat is gently tilted
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live sensor readings. It can be safely lifted or tilted without disconnecting its power.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Gently tilt the thermostat and return it to its normal position.
Observe the readings and display for one minute.
expected: The display remains stable and both sensor readings remain available, with no spurious sensor fault shown.

title: Control the correct zone in a multi-zone home
preconditions: The home has at least two paired, online thermostats assigned to distinct zones. The user can control both zones from the dashboard.
steps: Open the first zone and note its target.
Set its target to 20 degrees and save.
Open the second zone and note its target.
Refresh both zones and compare targets.
expected: Only the first zone changes to 20 degrees. The second zone retains its own target and neither thermostat receives the other zone's setting.

title: Check away controls with Voice Control
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and away mode controls are available. Voice Control is enabled and configured on the iPhone.
steps: Open the home's away controls.
Use Voice Control to select the away mode control.
Use Voice Control to confirm or save the change.
expected: Visible away controls have usable spoken names and can be activated and saved using Voice Control. The app shows the resulting confirmed mode.

title: Sign in using email letter case variation
preconditions: A verified Dormouse account exists. The tester is signed out and knows its email address and password.
steps: Change the letter case in the email address while keeping the same characters.
Enter the correct password and submit the sign-in form.
expected: The app treats email letter case consistently with account identity rules and signs in to the correct account, or explains clearly if the entered address is not accepted.

title: Receive an update failure alert
preconditions: A user account is signed in and update alerts are enabled. An approved test method can simulate firmware update error E-510.
steps: Simulate firmware update error E-510 on a test thermostat.
Open the dashboard notifications view.
Inspect the update notification.
expected: A notification reports the firmware update failure and identifies the affected thermostat. It does not state that the update succeeded.

title: Show clear error when iOS location services are disabled
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and geofencing is enabled. Location permission is set to Always, but iOS Location Services are disabled system-wide.
steps: Open the Dormouse app and navigate to away settings.
Check the geofencing status and any error or guidance.
Re-enable Location Services and return to the away settings.
expected: The app explains that system Location Services are off and that geofencing cannot operate. After Location Services are re-enabled, the app reflects the restored availability without requiring account sign-in again.

title: View report when one zone has no data
preconditions: The user's home has two zones, with report data in one and no report data in the other for the selected month.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Select the month with the differing zone data.
Select the zone that has no report data.
expected: The dashboard clearly indicates that report data is unavailable for that zone and month. It does not display another zone's figures as the selected zone's data.

title: Create a daily heating schedule
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to an owner account and paired with an online thermostat. The thermostat is in schedule mode.
steps: Open the thermostat's schedule in the iOS app.
Add a period for today starting at 07:00 with a target of 20 degrees.
Save the schedule.
Check the schedule view and thermostat display.
expected: The app saves the 07:00 period and shows its 20 degree target. The thermostat displays the scheduled target when the period begins.

title: Show update status to a household member
preconditions: A household member account is signed in to the Android app and has permission to view the thermostat. An update is available.
steps: Open the thermostat details as the household member.
View the firmware status.
Compare the displayed status with the owner account.
expected: The member can view the firmware status allowed by their permissions, and it matches the current device state. The app does not expose owner-only controls to a member without permission.

title: Operate update flow with spoken guidance
preconditions: An update is available. The tester can use the thermostat controls without relying on small visual details.
steps: Navigate to the update option using the dial and press.
Follow the prompts using only their text, symbols, and physical control feedback.
Confirm or cancel the update, then check the resulting status.
expected: Each choice and the result are distinguishable using the thermostat itself, without requiring an app or web dashboard. The dial and button actions produce consistent, understandable feedback.

title: Reject mismatched registration passwords
preconditions: The tester is signed out and can access a registration form with password confirmation.
steps: Enter a valid unused email address.
Enter different values in the password and confirmation fields.
Submit the form.
expected: The app rejects the submission and explains that the passwords do not match. No account is created.

title: Reject an incorrect Wi-Fi password
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A visible 2.4 GHz network is available, but the entered password will be incorrect.
steps: Open pairing and select the network.
Enter an incorrect password and confirm.
Observe the display and available recovery options.
expected: The thermostat does not report successful pairing. It indicates that the network credentials were rejected and allows the user to retry without locking up.

title: Check report while thermostat is offline
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, a thermostat has report history, and the thermostat can be taken offline while cloud access remains available.
steps: Open a month with existing report data.
Take the thermostat offline.
Refresh the report.
expected: The app handles the offline thermostat without losing or mislabelling historical report data. Any delay or missing live data is clearly distinguished from the monthly report.

title: Keep shared home visible after app restart
preconditions: The user is an accepted household member and the shared home is visible in the iOS app.
steps: Close the Dormouse app fully.
Reopen the app and sign in if prompted.
Open the home list.
expected: The shared home remains available to the member without requiring a new invitation.

title: Cancel schedule changes without saving
preconditions: A saved schedule exists for a day. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open the schedule editor and change a period.
Leave the editor using its cancel or discard action.
Reopen the schedule.
expected: The app discards the unsaved change. The period retains its previously saved time and temperature.

title: View a household report with multiple zones
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to a household with at least two zones and available monthly reports.
steps: Open Energy reports.
Select the household-wide view if offered.
Compare its displayed scope with the individual zone reports.
expected: The app clearly identifies whether the report covers the household or an individual zone. Any household total is presented consistently with its included zones.

title: Check cloud connection error presentation E-110
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and its local Wi-Fi remains available. The Dormouse cloud can be made unreachable in the test environment.
steps: Make the Dormouse cloud unreachable while keeping local Wi-Fi available.
Observe the thermostat display for the connection status.
Restore cloud access after noting the result.
expected: The thermostat displays E-110 with a clear cloud connection error indication and does not mislabel the fault as a missing Wi-Fi network.

title: Use heating controls with Android screen reader
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and connected to a paired thermostat. TalkBack is enabled on the phone.
steps: Navigate to the thermostat's heating controls using TalkBack.
Identify the current temperature and target using spoken labels.
Change the target by one increment and confirm the change.
expected: TalkBack announces the heating controls and values with meaningful labels. The target can be changed and the applied value is announced without relying on visual cues alone.

title: Set maximum target temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and online. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open heating controls.
Set the target to 30 degrees.
Try to raise the target once more.
expected: The target is set to 30 degrees. It cannot be set above 30 degrees.

title: Resend a pending invitation
preconditions: The owner is signed in and a household invitation is pending. The app provides a resend action for pending invitations.
steps: Open the pending invitation in household sharing.
Choose to resend the invitation.
Check the invitation status.
expected: The app confirms the resend without creating a duplicate household member or invitation entry. The invitation remains pending.

title: Apply a schedule to the correct zone
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to a home with two paired thermostats in separate zones. Both zones have schedules.
steps: Open the schedule for the first zone.
Change one period to a different valid target and save.
Inspect the schedules for both zones.
expected: Only the first zone's schedule changes. The second zone retains its original periods and targets.

title: Check schedule behaviour around a clock change
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has a scheduled period on a date when the dashboard's time zone observes a daylight-saving clock change.
steps: Open the schedule date in the dashboard.
Review the displayed time zone and period start times.
Save a valid edit and reopen the date.
expected: The dashboard presents schedule times consistently in the home's configured time zone. Saving and reopening the schedule does not shift periods unexpectedly because of the clock change.

title: Check special characters in Wi-Fi password
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A 2.4 GHz network password includes supported special characters, and the exact password is known.
steps: Select the network and open password entry.
Use the dial to enter the password, including its special characters.
Submit the password and wait for the result.
expected: The character selection allows the password to be entered accurately. The thermostat connects and pairs successfully.

title: Use heating controls with VoiceOver
preconditions: VoiceOver is enabled on the iOS device. The app is signed in and a thermostat is online.
steps: Navigate to the thermostat controls using VoiceOver.
Identify the target control and its current value.
Adjust the target by one half-degree using the accessible control.
expected: VoiceOver announces the target control and its value, and announces the updated value after adjustment. The thermostat receives the new target.

title: An invited household member can change the temperature but not the schedule
preconditions: An owner account and a second account invited to the home as a member.
steps: Log in as the member.
Change the target temperature.
Open Schedules and try to edit a period.
expected: The temperature change works. The schedule opens read-only with the message 'Only the owner can change schedules'.

title: Start one-hour boost from iOS
preconditions: The thermostat is online and the iOS app is signed in. Boost is not active and the boiler is responsive.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Start boost.
Check the boost status and heating response.
expected: The app shows boost as active for one hour and requests heat from the boiler when needed.

title: Operate heating controls with reduced dexterity
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and connected to a paired thermostat. Android touch and accessibility settings are configured for the user's normal use.
steps: Open heating controls.
Tap the target adjustment and boost controls using deliberate, single taps.
Check that only the intended action is applied.
expected: Controls respond reliably to individual taps and give clear feedback. A single tap does not cause an unintended repeated temperature change or boost action.

title: Receive a thermostat back online alert
preconditions: A user account is signed in and device alerts are enabled. A test thermostat is offline and its offline notification is available.
steps: Restore the thermostat's connection.
Wait for the dashboard to report the connection recovery.
Open the notifications view.
expected: A recovery notification identifies the same thermostat or zone as the offline alert. The dashboard shows the thermostat as online.

title: Handle notification service error
preconditions: A signed-in account can access the dashboard. An approved test method can simulate a failed notification request.
steps: Open the notifications view while the request failure is active.
Inspect the page response.
Restore the service and retry the view.
expected: The dashboard shows a clear error or retry state and does not present incomplete data as a successful load. After recovery, retrying loads the available notifications.

title: Prevent a seventh daily period
preconditions: The selected day already has six saved periods. The iOS app is signed in.
steps: Open that day's schedule.
Choose to add another period.
Check the app response.
expected: The app does not add a seventh period. It explains that no more than six periods can be scheduled per day.

title: Check unassigned thermostat behaviour
preconditions: A thermostat is paired to the home but has not been assigned to a zone. The home contains at least one configured zone.
steps: Wake the thermostat display.
Open the zone selection or assignment view.
Attempt to control heating before assigning a zone.
expected: The thermostat identifies that it is unassigned and does not silently change another zone's settings. It provides an available route to select or assign a zone.

title: Check notification sound and haptics settings
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. The iPhone is not in Silent Mode or Focus unless the test specifically sets those modes, and a paired thermostat can generate a test notification.
steps: Set the iPhone notification sound and haptics preferences to an enabled state.
Generate a test notification.
Observe sound and haptic behaviour.
Disable sound or haptics and repeat with a new event.
expected: The notification follows the applicable iOS sound and haptic settings. Disabling a setting prevents that alert type without suppressing the notification itself.

title: Edit a saved schedule period
preconditions: A schedule with at least two periods exists for the selected day. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open the selected day's schedule.
Change one period's time and temperature, then save.
Reopen the schedule.
expected: The edited period shows the new time and temperature. Other periods retain their original settings.

title: Check sensor readings across a display theme change
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and offers more than one display theme or colour scheme. Live readings are available.
steps: Record the temperature and humidity shown.
Change the display theme using the thermostat controls.
Check both readings and restore the original theme.
expected: Both sensor readings remain present and legible after the theme change, and their values are not changed by the display setting.

title: Receive a thermostat offline alert
preconditions: A user account is signed in and device alerts are enabled. A test thermostat or approved simulator can be taken offline.
steps: Take the test thermostat offline.
Wait for the dashboard to report the device status change.
Open the notifications view.
expected: An offline notification identifies the affected thermostat or zone. The dashboard does not report the thermostat as online while it remains offline.

title: Review schedule across midnight boundary
preconditions: The schedule editor permits a period to be set near midnight. The thermostat is paired and has an editable day.
steps: Open the day's schedule and add or edit a period.
Set its start time to the latest time the editor permits.
Save and review the displayed time and day assignment.
expected: The thermostat displays the selected time accurately and assigns the period to the selected day without shifting it unexpectedly.

title: Cancel pairing before network selection
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired and is at the start of its pairing flow.
steps: Open pairing on the thermostat.
Use the displayed control to cancel or go back.
Confirm cancellation if prompted.
expected: The thermostat exits pairing and returns to its normal unpaired screen. It does not claim to be paired or show an error.

title: Check sensor display after prolonged operation
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and installed in a stable room. It can remain undisturbed for the duration of the test.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Leave the thermostat operating normally for 30 minutes.
Check the display without pressing controls.
Record both sensor values again.
expected: The display remains responsive and continues to show valid sensor readings after prolonged operation. It shows no sensor error or frozen screen.

title: Check pairing with weak Wi-Fi signal
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A 2.4 GHz network is available at a weak but usable signal level.
steps: Open pairing and scan for networks.
Select the weak-signal network and enter its valid password.
Submit the details and observe the result.
expected: The thermostat either completes pairing reliably or reports a clear connection failure without freezing. The displayed network status does not falsely indicate a completed connection.

title: Switch between two zones
preconditions: Two paired thermostats are assigned to different zones in the same home. Both zones have distinct names and targets.
steps: Use the thermostat's zone selector to open the other zone.
Note its displayed name and target temperature.
Return to the original zone and check its displayed target.
expected: Each zone displays its own name and target. Changing zones does not alter either zone's target.

title: Pair using Switch Control
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. Switch Control is enabled and configured, and the thermostat is ready to pair.
steps: Navigate the add-thermostat flow using Switch Control.
Select the Wi-Fi network and enter its password.
Start pairing using Switch Control.
Follow the status and finish setup.
expected: All required pairing actions can be focused and activated with Switch Control. Pairing succeeds without requiring touch-only gestures.

title: View recent notifications
preconditions: A user account is signed in to the web dashboard. At least one notification has been generated for the home.
steps: Open the notifications view.
Inspect the most recent notification.
expected: The view shows the latest notification with its message and a clear date and time. The notification is associated with the correct home.

title: Start one-hour boost from the app
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and online, and the boiler is responsive. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open heating controls.
Start boost.
Check the app for boost status and its duration.
expected: The app confirms that boost is active for one hour, and the thermostat requests heat as required.

title: Operate the dial with limited dexterity
preconditions: A thermostat is assigned to a zone and its display and dial are working. The tester can assess operation using one hand or limited grip.
steps: Wake the thermostat without holding or squeezing the dial continuously.
Turn the dial slowly by one detent.
Press the dial to confirm the target change.
expected: The dial and press action can be completed with clear, consistent feedback and without unintended multiple changes. The display confirms the selected zone and final target.

title: Check zone controls with screen reader
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard with a screen reader enabled. The home has at least one zone with an online thermostat.
steps: Open the zones overview and listen to the announced zone names and statuses.
Navigate to the zone target control.
Change the target and listen for the updated value.
expected: Zone names, statuses and control labels are announced meaningfully. The target control's current and updated values are announced without relying on colour alone.

title: Pair when the account session has expired
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the account session has expired. The thermostat is ready to pair on a suitable 2.4 GHz network.
steps: Open the app and start or resume adding a thermostat.
Respond to the sign-in prompt with valid account credentials.
Complete two-step verification if requested.
Retry or resume pairing.
expected: The app requires successful authentication before associating the thermostat with the account. After sign-in and verification, pairing can be completed without losing track of the device.

title: Enforce the household member limit
preconditions: The household has an owner and eight accepted members. The owner is signed in to the Android app.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Try to invite another email address.
Review the app response and member list.
expected: The app prevents adding a ninth member and explains that the household limit has been reached. Existing membership remains unchanged.

title: Handle cloud unavailable during heating control
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and the thermostat is paired. The Dormouse cloud can be made unavailable while the phone and local heating equipment remain powered.
steps: Make the Dormouse cloud unavailable.
Attempt to change the heating target in the Android app.
Check for an error on the thermostat and status in the app.
expected: The thermostat displays E-110 when it cannot reach the cloud. The app indicates the connection problem and does not falsely confirm a remote change.

title: Check notification privacy on the lock screen
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. The Android lock screen is configured to hide sensitive notification content.
steps: Lock the phone.
Generate a thermostat notification.
View the notification on the lock screen.
Unlock the phone and open the notification.
expected: The lock screen respects Android's hidden-content setting and does not expose unnecessary household details. After unlocking, the notification opens the relevant app screen.

title: Check zone target step size
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in with permission to control the home. The home has an online zone.
steps: Open the zone's temperature control.
Increase the target by one step.
Decrease the target by one step.
expected: The target changes in half-degree increments and returns to its starting value after the two adjustments.

title: Correct a mistyped Wi-Fi password
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The thermostat is ready to pair and a suitable 2.4 GHz network is available.
steps: Start pairing and enter an incorrect password.
Submit the details and wait for failure.
Edit the password to the correct value.
Retry pairing.
expected: The first attempt fails without adding the thermostat. The corrected credentials allow pairing to complete.

title: Handle loss of cloud connection
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and powered. The iOS app is signed in; the home internet connection can be interrupted for this test.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Disconnect the home internet connection.
Check the app status and thermostat display.
expected: The app reports that the thermostat cannot be reached or that cloud connectivity is unavailable. The thermostat displays E-110 when it cannot reach the Dormouse cloud.

title: Check away status notification
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and iOS notifications are enabled for Dormouse. Away mode can be changed in the app.
steps: Change away mode from off to on in the app.
Check the iOS notification centre.
Change away mode back to off and check again.
expected: Any configured away mode notifications accurately describe the change and do not report a transition that failed. If notifications for manual changes are not configured, the app still shows the correct status without an unrelated alert.

title: Retry a failed firmware update
preconditions: A previous update attempt failed and E-510 is visible or recorded. The cause has been removed, and the thermostat is online with stable power.
steps: Open the thermostat's update status in the iOS app.
Use the available retry action, or wait for the next permitted update window.
Check the displayed firmware version and error status.
expected: The retry is accepted and its status is shown accurately. On success, the new version is reported and E-510 clears; on failure, the error remains visible with no false success.

title: Set a period at midnight
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and a schedule editor is open.
steps: Set a schedule period to start at 00:00.
Save and reopen the schedule.
expected: The period is saved and displayed at 00:00 on the intended day, without shifting to another day.

title: Pair after entering an empty password
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The selected 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network requires a password, and the thermostat is ready to pair.
steps: Start adding the thermostat and select the network.
Leave the password field empty.
Attempt to continue.
Review validation feedback.
expected: The app prevents submission and identifies the password field as required. No pairing attempt is falsely recorded as successful.

title: Check app after thermostat restart
preconditions: An update is in progress or has just completed and the thermostat will restart as part of the update. The iOS app is signed in and connected.
steps: Observe the update status in the iOS app as the thermostat restarts.
Wait for the thermostat to reconnect.
Refresh the firmware screen in the app.
expected: The app shows a temporary reconnecting or updating state during restart rather than a false failure. After reconnection, it displays the confirmed version and final update result.

title: Check sensor readings for a user with limited reach
preconditions: The thermostat is mounted in its intended position and powered, with live readings available. The tester can assess interaction from a comfortable standing or seated position.
steps: View the temperature and humidity from a comfortable position without touching the thermostat.
Use the dial from that position to access the sensor view if it is not already shown.
Confirm the readings can be read without stretching or needing to hold the device.
expected: Both sensor values are visible and readable from the intended viewing position, and accessing them does not require moving or lifting the thermostat.

title: Check readings after brief power interruption
preconditions: The thermostat is operating from mains power and both sensors are functioning. It is safe to briefly interrupt power using the normal safe procedure.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Briefly interrupt and restore mains power.
Wait for the thermostat to finish restarting.
Check both readings.
expected: After restart, both sensor readings are shown again and the thermostat returns to its normal screen. Any power interruption indication clears when power is restored, according to the device behaviour.

title: Check sensor display during a firmware update
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and connected to a stable network. A scheduled or approved test firmware update can be started safely.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Start the firmware update using the approved procedure.
Observe the thermostat display throughout the update and after completion.
expected: The display clearly indicates update progress or status and does not present stale sensor values as live; live readings return after the update completes.

title: Check away mode with multiple zones
preconditions: The home has at least two paired zones, and the Android app can control them. Away mode is off.
steps: Turn on away mode for the home.
Open each zone's controls.
Check each zone's mode and target.
expected: Away mode is applied consistently to the zones covered by the home setting. The app clearly identifies any zone that is excluded or has a different state.

title: Set a half-degree zone target
preconditions: A zone with an online thermostat exists. The Android app is signed in to the home.
steps: Open the zone's heating controls.
Set the target temperature to 19.5 degrees.
Reopen the zone controls and check the target.
expected: The target remains 19.5 degrees in the app and on the thermostat. It is not rounded to a whole degree.

title: Pair after granting nearby-device permission
preconditions: The Android app is installed, and its nearby-device permission has not yet been granted. The thermostat is in pairing mode and a 2.4 GHz network is available.
steps: Start pairing in the app.
Grant the nearby-device permission when Android requests it.
Continue setup using valid network details.
expected: The app proceeds with device discovery after permission is granted. Pairing completes and the thermostat appears in the app.

title: Receive a notification for a disconnected temperature sensor
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe test setup can simulate a disconnected thermostat temperature sensor.
steps: Simulate a disconnected temperature sensor.
Wait for the thermostat and app to report the fault.
Check the Android notification shade.
expected: A notification clearly reports a temperature sensor fault and identifies the affected thermostat. It does not show a normal temperature reading as current.

title: Create a daily heating schedule
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard and has a paired, online thermostat. A home and heating zone are configured.
steps: Open the zone's schedule page.
Add one period for today with a start time and target temperature.
Save the schedule and view the zone schedule.
expected: The saved period appears on the correct day with the selected time and temperature. The dashboard confirms the schedule was saved.

title: Recover after denying nearby-device permission
preconditions: The Android app is installed and nearby-device permission has not been granted. The thermostat is in pairing mode.
steps: Start pairing and deny the nearby-device permission.
Observe the app guidance and Android permission state.
Open the relevant Android settings from the app or system settings, grant permission, and retry.
expected: The app explains that permission is needed and does not remain stuck or claim success. After permission is granted, pairing can proceed.

title: Display shows E-217 when the temperature sensor is disconnected
preconditions: A test thermostat with its back cover off, so the temperature sensor cable can be unplugged.
steps: Unplug the temperature sensor cable.
Wait one minute and read the display.
Plug the cable back in and wait one minute.
expected: E-217 appears within one minute and heating switches off for safety. The error clears and normal control resumes once the sensor is reconnected.

title: Check readings are readable in bright ambient light
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and both sensor readings are available. The display can be viewed in a brightly lit room without exposing it to excessive heat.
steps: Wake the display in bright ambient light.
Read the temperature and humidity values.
Change viewing angle slightly and read them again.
expected: The readings remain legible in bright ambient light and from a modest viewing angle. No glare or layout issue makes either value ambiguous.

title: Use away mode with large text
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and paired with an online thermostat. Android font size can be increased.
steps: Increase Android font size using system settings.
Open the Dormouse app's away mode controls.
Turn away mode on and review the result.
expected: Away mode controls and status remain readable and usable without clipped text or hidden actions. The mode change is confirmed clearly.

title: Set target to the minimum temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and showing the target temperature control. The boiler is operating normally.
steps: Turn the dial anticlockwise until the target reaches 5 degrees.
Try turning the dial anticlockwise once more.
expected: The target remains at 5 degrees and cannot be lowered further. The display remains responsive and shows no unexpected error.

title: Open the current month's energy report
preconditions: The user is signed in to the web dashboard and has a home with a paired thermostat. The current month has report data.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Select the current month.
expected: The dashboard displays the current month's report for the selected home, with its available energy figures and period clearly identified.

title: Schedule a period at midnight
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a configured zone.
steps: Open the schedule for a day.
Add a period with a start time of 00:00 and a valid target.
Save and review the day's schedule.
expected: The period is saved at 00:00 on the selected day and is not shifted to another day.

title: Pair with local network permission denied
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. Local Network access has been denied to the app, and the thermostat is ready to pair.
steps: Start adding a thermostat.
Deny the iOS Local Network permission request if it appears.
Review the app guidance.
Grant Local Network access in iOS settings and retry.
expected: The app explains that Local Network access is required for pairing and provides a route to iOS settings. Pairing can proceed after access is granted.

title: Announce account errors with TalkBack
preconditions: TalkBack is enabled on the Android device. The app is installed and signed out.
steps: Open the sign-in screen and focus the email field.
Leave the email field empty and submit the form.
Listen to the TalkBack announcement and move focus to the relevant field.
expected: The app identifies the missing email in a TalkBack-readable announcement, associates the error with the field, and keeps focus usable for correction.

title: Handle mains power interruption
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and configured. Mains power can be interrupted and restored safely, and the Android app is signed in.
steps: Interrupt mains power to the thermostat safely.
Check the thermostat display and app status.
Restore mains power and check the heating target.
expected: The thermostat displays E-402 during the interruption. After power is restored, it returns to operation and retains the configured target.

title: Reject periods in an invalid time order
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a configured zone.
steps: Open the test day's schedule.
Create periods whose start times are out of order or conflict, such as 10:00 followed by 09:00.
Attempt to save.
expected: The dashboard either orders valid periods consistently or prevents conflicting times from being saved with a clear explanation. It does not apply an ambiguous schedule.

title: Check half-degree target increments
preconditions: A thermostat is assigned to an active zone. Its target is below 30 degrees.
steps: Turn the dial up by one detent.
Read the target on the display.
Turn the dial down by one detent.
expected: The target changes in half-degree increments only. Turning back one detent restores the original target.

title: Load older notifications
preconditions: A user account is signed in and has more notifications than fit on the first page or initial list.
steps: Open the notifications view.
Use the control to load or open older notifications.
Inspect the newly displayed entries.
expected: Older notifications are added or displayed without duplicating entries already shown. The displayed entries retain their correct messages and timestamps.

title: Check a zone sensor fault
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in. A test thermostat is assigned to a zone and can be placed into a temperature sensor fault state showing E-217.
steps: Cause the zone thermostat to report E-217.
Open the affected zone in the iOS app.
Review its status and temperature controls.
expected: The app identifies the affected zone and reports the sensor fault. It does not present an invalid sensor reading as a normal current temperature.

title: Pair a fourth thermostat in a home
preconditions: The home already has three paired thermostats. A fourth thermostat is in pairing mode, and the Android app is signed in as the owner.
steps: Start adding a thermostat from the home screen.
Pair the fourth thermostat using valid network details.
Review the home and zone device list.
expected: The fourth thermostat pairs successfully and is available for the home to assign to a zone. All four thermostats are listed distinctly.

title: Use zone controls with larger text
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the home has an online zone. Increase iOS text size to the largest size supported for the app.
steps: Open the zone list.
Open a zone's controls.
Navigate to the target and boost controls.
expected: Zone names and control labels remain readable and usable. Text does not overlap essential controls or prevent access to the zone settings.

title: Resume update after iOS app restart
preconditions: An update is available and the iOS app is signed in. The update is in progress or its progress can be safely simulated in a test environment.
steps: Open the update status screen in the iOS app.
Close and reopen the app while the update is in progress.
Check the update status and progress.
expected: The app reconnects and displays the actual update state without restarting or duplicating the installation. Progress is not shown as complete until the thermostat confirms completion.

title: Set a zone target temperature
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone contains an online thermostat and heating control is available.
steps: Open the zone controls.
Set the target temperature to 20 degrees.
Save the setting and refresh the page.
expected: The zone target remains 20 degrees after refresh. Its thermostat receives the target and displays or reports 20 degrees.

title: Control the correct thermostat in a zone
preconditions: Two thermostats are paired in the same home with different targets. The iOS app is signed in.
steps: Select the first thermostat in the iOS app.
Change its target by one half-degree.
Check the targets of both thermostats.
expected: Only the selected thermostat's target changes. The other thermostat retains its original target.

title: Handle sign-in with no credentials
preconditions: The iOS app is open on the sign-in screen.
steps: Leave the email and password fields empty.
Tap the sign-in button.
expected: The app requests the required credentials and sends no sign-in request.

title: Create six periods in one day
preconditions: The selected day has no periods, or enough periods can be removed to make room. The thermostat is paired and responsive.
steps: Open the selected day's schedule.
Add periods one at a time until six periods are present.
Set a start time and target for each period.
Save and review all six periods.
expected: The thermostat saves and displays six periods for the day with their configured values.

title: Set the minimum target temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and its target can be adjusted. The target is above 5 degrees.
steps: Turn the dial anticlockwise until the target reaches 5 degrees.
Turn the dial anticlockwise once more.
Check the displayed target.
expected: The display shows 5 degrees and does not go below it.

title: Withdraw a pending invitation
preconditions: The owner is signed in, and a household invitation is pending. The invitee has not accepted it.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Select the pending invitation.
Choose to withdraw or cancel it and confirm.
expected: The invitation is removed from the pending list and can no longer be accepted. The invitee remains outside the household.

title: Handle loss of Wi-Fi during pairing
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. The 2.4 GHz network can be switched off after the thermostat has started connecting.
steps: Start pairing and submit valid network credentials.
Switch off the Wi-Fi access point while the thermostat is connecting.
Observe the display and recovery controls.
Restore the access point and retry.
expected: Pairing is not reported as successful while Wi-Fi is unavailable. The thermostat remains responsive and can complete pairing after the network is restored.

title: Check humidity sensor fault code
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and operating normally. A safe method is available to simulate a humidity sensor fault without damaging the device.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Simulate a humidity sensor fault.
Wait for the thermostat to detect the fault.
Read the display and note any error code.
expected: The display shows E-221 for the humidity sensor fault. The temperature reading remains available if its sensor is unaffected.

title: Return home and end geofenced away mode
preconditions: Geofencing is enabled and the phone is outside the configured home area. Away mode is on because of geofencing.
steps: Return the phone to the configured home area.
Allow the app to update its location.
Check the home controls.
expected: The app detects arrival and ends geofenced away mode according to the configured behaviour. The thermostat resumes the normal schedule or target.

title: Disable away mode manually
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and away mode is active for a home with a paired thermostat.
steps: Open the home controls in the iOS app.
Turn off away mode.
Check the app status and thermostat target.
expected: The app shows away mode as off. The thermostat returns to the applicable home heating control, such as the current schedule.

title: Toggle password visibility on sign-up
preconditions: The iOS app is open on a screen with a password field and its visibility control.
steps: Enter a password in the field.
Tap the password visibility control.
Tap the control again.
expected: The first tap reveals the entered password and the second masks it again without changing its value.

title: Verify zone separation for a household member
preconditions: The home has two zones and a non-owner household member account. The Android app can be used to sign in as that member.
steps: Sign in as the household member and open Zones.
Open each zone and review its thermostat name and target.
Change one permitted zone target, then check the other zone.
expected: The member sees zones belonging to the shared home with the correct thermostat associations. A permitted change affects only the selected zone; access is not granted to zones from another home.

title: Check report contrast and non-colour cues
preconditions: A monthly report is available in the Android app. Android display settings allow colour correction or grayscale.
steps: Open the report and note how values or chart categories are distinguished.
Enable grayscale or a colour-vision correction setting.
Review the same report.
expected: Report information remains understandable without colour alone; categories and key values have text, labels or other distinguishable cues.

title: Handle lost connection while sending an invitation
preconditions: The owner is signed in and has fewer than eight members. The Android device can switch between online and offline states.
steps: Enter a valid invitee email address.
Disable network access before sending the invitation.
Try to send, then restore network access and refresh the member list.
expected: The app reports that sending failed or remains clearly pending; it does not falsely confirm success. After reconnection, the list accurately reflects whether an invitation was sent.

title: Reject an email address with invalid syntax
preconditions: The iOS app is open on the account creation screen.
steps: Enter an email address with invalid syntax.
Complete the other required fields with valid values.
Submit the form.
expected: The app identifies the email field as invalid and does not create an account.

title: Recover pairing after cloud connection failure
preconditions: The thermostat has Wi-Fi access, but access to the Dormouse cloud is temporarily blocked. The Android app is signed in and the thermostat is in pairing mode.
steps: Start pairing in the app and provide valid Wi-Fi details.
Wait for the cloud connection stage to fail.
Restore cloud access and use the app's retry option.
expected: The thermostat displays E-110 while it cannot reach the cloud. After access is restored and pairing is retried, the thermostat is added to the app.

title: Add the maximum six daily periods
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a configured zone. The zone has no schedule for the test day.
steps: Open the test day's schedule.
Add six periods with valid, non-overlapping start times and target temperatures.
Save and reopen the day's schedule.
expected: All six periods are saved and shown with their correct times and temperatures. No extra period is required or displayed.

title: Check report after changing target temperature
preconditions: The app is signed in to a home with a monthly report and a paired thermostat. Energy reporting data can be checked over a test period.
steps: Record the current monthly report values.
Change the thermostat target temperature in the app.
Allow the test period to collect data, then reopen the report.
expected: The report remains associated with the correct month and reflects available data for the period, without attributing data to the wrong date.

title: Check sensor screen with gloves on
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and showing sensor readings. Suitable gloves are available that may reduce touch or dial dexterity.
steps: Wake the display while wearing the gloves.
Use the dial to return to the sensor screen if needed.
Read the temperature and humidity values.
Check that the display remains on long enough to read them.
