expected: The sensor readings are visible and legible while the tester wears gloves. Basic dial interaction can reach the sensor screen without accidental selection of unrelated controls.

title: Check sensor values after changing target temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and both sensors are functioning. The normal screen displays the room temperature and target temperature.
steps: Record the room temperature and humidity.
Turn the dial to change the target temperature by one step.
Return to the normal screen.
Check the sensor readings.
expected: Changing the target temperature does not alter, hide or relabel the room temperature or humidity readings.

title: Pair with a nearly expired setup code
preconditions: The thermostat is in pairing mode and displays a time-limited setup code with less than one minute remaining. The Android app is signed in and ready to add a thermostat.
steps: Begin adding the thermostat in the app.
Enter the displayed setup code just before it expires.
Submit the code and follow any next prompt.
Check the app's result.
expected: The app either accepts a still-valid code and proceeds with pairing, or clearly states that the code expired and requests a fresh code. It does not show a false pairing success.

title: Check schedule period heating target
preconditions: A schedule is enabled for the zone and contains a period active now. The thermostat is online and the dashboard can edit schedules.
steps: Open the zone schedule.
Select the period active now.
Set its target to 20 degrees and save.
Check the active target on the dashboard.
expected: The schedule period is saved with a 20-degree target. The active zone target reflects the period's setting.

title: Open zone controls with TalkBack
preconditions: TalkBack is enabled on the Android device. At least one zone with an online thermostat exists.
steps: Open the Dormouse app and navigate to Zones using TalkBack.
Focus the zone name, target control, and heating mode control in turn.
Listen to each control's spoken label and current value.
expected: Each zone and control has a meaningful spoken label, and the target and mode values are announced. Focus moves through the controls in a logical order.

title: Copy a schedule to another zone
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in with permission to manage schedules. The home has two zones and one zone has a saved schedule.
steps: Open the source zone's schedule options.
Choose the option to copy or apply the schedule to the second zone.
Confirm and open the second zone's schedule.
expected: The destination zone shows the copied schedule. The source zone's schedule remains unchanged.

title: Verify E-401 code is readable
preconditions: A test unit or approved diagnostic setup can safely produce the low-backup-battery condition.
steps: Cause the backup batteries to enter the low condition using the approved setup.
Observe the display and locate the error code.
Check that other essential screen information remains readable.
expected: The display shows E-401 clearly and identifies the low backup battery condition without hiding the code.

title: Validate email address during registration
preconditions: The tester is signed out of the Android app and can access the account creation form.
steps: Enter a malformed email address and an otherwise valid password.
Submit the form.
expected: The app rejects the email address and explains that a valid email is required. No account is created.

title: Check report period at a month boundary
preconditions: The user can view reports for two consecutive months. The dashboard allows selection of each month.
steps: Open the report for the first month.
Record the period shown.
Select the following month and inspect its period.
expected: Each report is labelled with the correct month and year, including when the month or year changes at the boundary.

title: Check case-sensitive Wi-Fi password entry
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A 2.4 GHz network password contains both upper-case and lower-case letters.
steps: Select the network and open password entry.
Enter the password with the specified letter cases.
Submit it and wait for the result.
expected: The thermostat preserves letter case and connects using the exact password. Pairing completes without a credential error.

title: Receive a notification when cloud access is lost
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe test setup can interrupt cloud access for a paired thermostat without interrupting household internet access for the phone.
steps: Interrupt the thermostat's access to the Dormouse cloud.
Wait for the status to be reported.
Check the Android notification shade.
expected: A notification reports that the thermostat cannot reach the Dormouse cloud. It does not state that the phone has lost internet access.

title: Check sensor screen contrast for low vision
preconditions: The thermostat is installed at a normal viewing position. A tester with low vision or an agreed low-vision assessment method is available.
steps: View the temperature and humidity readings from the usual standing position.
View them from a modest distance away.
Check whether the digits can be distinguished from their background.
Confirm that labels and values can be told apart.
expected: Temperature and humidity digits have sufficient contrast and are distinguishable from each other and their labels. No value relies on colour alone for identification.

title: Recover from failed firmware update
preconditions: The thermostat can be made to report firmware update failure E-510. The Android app is signed in and online.
steps: Trigger or simulate a failed firmware update.
Open the thermostat status in the Android app.
Check the error details and available recovery action.
expected: The app reports the update failure and identifies E-510. The thermostat remains available for safe heating control, and the app offers a retry or clear next step without claiming the update succeeded.

title: Read schedule controls with VoiceOver
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and a schedule is available. VoiceOver is enabled on the iPhone.
steps: Navigate to the schedule using VoiceOver.
Move focus across a period, its time and its target.
Open a period and navigate its editing controls.
expected: VoiceOver announces meaningful labels and values for schedule periods and controls. Focus moves in a logical order, and the user can identify and operate the edit and save actions.

title: Handle a 5 GHz-only Wi-Fi network
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The iPhone is connected only to a 5 GHz Wi-Fi network, and the thermostat is ready to pair.
steps: Choose to add a thermostat.
Continue to the Wi-Fi network selection step.
Attempt to select or use the 5 GHz network.
Review the guidance shown by the app.
expected: The app clearly indicates that pairing requires a 2.4 GHz network and does not claim that pairing succeeded. The thermostat remains unpaired.

title: Invite a household member
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. The home has fewer than eight members.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Enter a valid email address and send an invitation.
Check the member list and the invitee's email.
expected: The invite is sent and the invitee appears as pending. The invitation email identifies the home and provides a working way to accept.

title: Prevent an invalid schedule temperature
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and a paired thermostat is available for schedule editing.
steps: Open a schedule period's temperature control.
Attempt to enter a temperature below 5 degrees or above 30 degrees.
expected: The app prevents saving an out-of-range temperature and identifies the valid range as 5 to 30 degrees.

title: Pair thermostat to a 5 GHz-only network
preconditions: The Android phone is connected to a 5 GHz-only Wi-Fi network. The thermostat is in pairing mode and a 2.4 GHz network is available nearby.
steps: Open the Android app and start adding a thermostat.
Choose the available 2.4 GHz network and enter its password.
Complete the on-screen pairing instructions.
expected: The thermostat joins the 2.4 GHz network and appears in the app. The phone's 5 GHz connection does not prevent pairing.

title: E-104 appears when Wi-Fi pairing times out
preconditions: A thermostat reset to factory settings, and a phone that is not running the Dormouse app.
steps: Hold the dial for five seconds to start pairing.
Do nothing for three minutes.
Read the display.
expected: After three minutes the display shows E-104 and returns to its pairing screen, ready to try again.

title: Check display response to dial press from home
preconditions: The thermostat is on its home screen with no alert or menu open.
steps: Press the dial once.
Observe the display response.
Press the dial again to return if needed.
expected: The press opens the intended main control view without changing the target temperature or causing an unintended selection.

title: Handle boiler fault report
preconditions: The thermostat is online and the iOS app is signed in. A boiler fault can be simulated using the approved test setup.
steps: Request heating by setting a target above the measured temperature.
Cause the boiler to report a fault using the approved test setup.
Check the thermostat display and iOS app.
expected: The thermostat displays E-312 and the app reports a boiler fault. The fault is not presented as successful heating.

title: Pair after iOS denies access to the selected Wi-Fi network
preconditions: The thermostat is in pairing mode, and a working 2.4 GHz network is available. The iPhone's app-specific Wi-Fi access is disabled if that setting is available on the iOS version under test.
steps: Start pairing and select the available network in the app.
Continue setup and observe any access prompt or error.
Use the app's guidance to open the relevant iOS setting, enable access, return to the app, and retry.
expected: The app explains that iOS Wi-Fi access is needed and provides a clear route to the setting where available. After access is enabled, setup can continue and pairing completes without restarting the entire flow.

title: Check a zone after mains power interruption
preconditions: A zone thermostat can be safely disconnected from mains power. The Android app is signed in to the home.
steps: Interrupt mains power to the thermostat.
Open the zone in the Android app and check its status.
Restore power and check the zone again.
expected: The app identifies the affected thermostat or zone as having a power interruption, and the thermostat displays E-402. After power is restored, the zone status updates without changing other zones.

title: View a previous month's energy report
preconditions: The signed-in user's home has report data for at least two completed months. The user can access that home's reports.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Select a completed month from the period control.
expected: The dashboard shows the selected month's report, and the displayed period matches the selected month.

title: Prevent owner from leaving without transferring ownership
preconditions: The test account is the household owner. At least one other member is in the household.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Choose the option to leave or close the household.
Review the app response.
expected: The app does not leave the household ownerless. It explains that ownership must be transferred or the household closed before the owner can leave.

title: Apply heating change while app reconnects
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and controlling the boiler. The Android phone has Wi-Fi and mobile data available.
steps: Open heating controls and set a new target temperature.
Temporarily disable the phone's network connection, then restore it.
Check the app and thermostat after reconnection.
expected: The app clearly indicates when it cannot communicate and does not falsely confirm an unapplied change. After reconnection, the app and thermostat show the same applied target.

title: Control heating in a single zone
preconditions: A thermostat is paired to the home and assigned to one zone. The boiler and thermostat have power and are online.
steps: Turn the dial to raise the target temperature by one half-degree.
Press the dial to confirm the target.
Check the thermostat display and listen for the boiler to respond.
expected: The display shows the new target temperature in the selected zone. The boiler starts if the measured temperature is below that target.

title: Identify the zone on the thermostat display
preconditions: The thermostat is assigned to a named zone in a home with at least one other zone.
steps: Wake the thermostat display.
Read the zone name or identifier shown.
Navigate away and return to the zone overview.
expected: The display identifies the thermostat's assigned zone clearly enough to distinguish it from other zones. The same zone is shown when returning to the overview.

title: Prevent creation of a fifth zone
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. The home already has four zones.
steps: Open the zones page.
Attempt to create another zone.
Review the dashboard response.
expected: The dashboard does not create a fifth zone. It clearly indicates that the maximum of four zones has been reached.

title: Set the away temperature
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and away mode settings are available for a paired home.
steps: Open away mode settings.
Set the away target to 17 degrees and save.
Read the target shown in the app.
expected: The saved away target is 17 degrees and remains displayed after leaving and reopening the settings.

title: Invite across different email casing
preconditions: A member has an account using a known email address. The owner is signed in and the address can be entered with different letter casing.
steps: Invite the member using the same address with different letter casing.
Check the response and household list.
expected: The dashboard handles the address consistently with the existing account and does not create duplicate membership. Any invitation or duplicate warning clearly states the outcome.

title: Check schedule accessibility with a screen reader
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard with a screen reader enabled. A zone has an existing schedule.
steps: Navigate to the schedule using screen reader controls.
Read the day headings, period times, temperatures and available actions.
Edit and save one period using the screen reader.
expected: Day, time, temperature and action controls have meaningful accessible names and are read in a logical order. The screen reader can identify the save result and any validation message.

title: Check no heating demand above target
preconditions: The thermostat is online, the boiler is responsive, and the room temperature is above the selected target. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open heating controls and note the room temperature and target.
Set a target below the room temperature.
Check heating status in the app and the boiler.
expected: The thermostat does not request heat while the room is above target. The app shows the selected target and no active heating demand.

title: Prevent overlapping schedule periods
preconditions: The zone has an editable schedule. The dashboard schedule editor allows period times to be changed.
steps: Open a day's schedule.
Set two periods to overlapping times.
Attempt to save the schedule.
Review the validation feedback and saved schedule.
expected: The dashboard blocks the overlapping schedule and explains the time conflict. The invalid periods are not applied to the thermostat.

title: Check display response to rapid dial turns
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and the target is near the middle of its range.
steps: Turn the dial quickly clockwise for several clicks.
Wait two seconds and read the target.
Turn it quickly anticlockwise for the same number of clicks.
Read the target again.
expected: The display responds without freezing or skipping unpredictably. The final target reflects the registered dial turns and remains within the allowed range.

title: Receive an overnight firmware update
preconditions: The thermostat is online, paired with the iOS app and connected to mains power. An update is available and the thermostat is idle before its configured overnight update window.
steps: Open the iOS app and confirm the update is available.
Leave the thermostat powered and online during the update window.
Check the app and thermostat after the update completes.
expected: The update installs during the overnight window. The app and thermostat show the new firmware version, and heating settings remain intact.

title: Set target to the maximum temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and showing the target temperature control. The boiler is operating normally.
steps: Turn the dial clockwise until the target reaches 30 degrees.
Try turning the dial clockwise once more.
expected: The target remains at 30 degrees and cannot be raised further. The display remains responsive and shows no unexpected error.

title: Handle thermostat cloud loss during update
preconditions: An update is available and the thermostat is online. The test environment can interrupt access from the thermostat to the Dormouse cloud during the update window.
steps: Interrupt the thermostat's cloud access during the update window.
Observe the iOS app and thermostat display.
Restore cloud access and refresh the app.
expected: The app reports the connection or update status accurately and does not show an unconfirmed success. When cloud access returns, the app reflects the thermostat's actual firmware version and update outcome.

title: Check pairing with a press-and-hold dial action
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired and pairing is open at a screen with a selectable option.
steps: Press and hold the dial briefly without intending to confirm.
Release the dial and observe the selection.
Use a normal press to choose the intended option.
expected: A brief hold does not trigger repeated or unintended selections. A normal press selects the highlighted option once.

title: Create a schedule with six daily periods
preconditions: The Android app is signed in to an owner account. A paired thermostat is online and has no schedule for the selected day.
steps: Open the thermostat's schedule editor.
Add six periods with distinct start times and temperatures.
Save the schedule and reopen that day's schedule.
expected: All six periods are saved and shown with their selected times and temperatures. No extra period is created.

title: Preserve boost after update
preconditions: The thermostat is online and an update is available. A one-hour boost can be scheduled to overlap the update window.
steps: Start a one-hour boost in the iOS app before the update window.
Allow the update window to begin and observe the app.
Check the boost status after the thermostat reconnects.
expected: The app clearly shows whether the boost was retained or ended during the update. The thermostat does not extend the boost beyond one hour, and heating follows the displayed status.

title: Update with an active heating call
preconditions: The thermostat is online, an update is available and the room is below its target temperature. The boiler is responding and heating is active.
steps: Confirm in the iOS app that the thermostat is calling for heat.
Allow the overnight update window to begin.
Observe the heating state and update status in the app.
expected: The update does not cause unsafe or unexpected boiler operation. Heating resumes according to the existing target and schedule after installation, and the app reports the final update status.

title: Pair as a household member
preconditions: The user is signed in as a household member with permission to add devices. The thermostat is unpaired and ready on a suitable 2.4 GHz network.
steps: Start adding a thermostat from the member account.
Complete the Wi-Fi and pairing prompts.
Check the household device list.
expected: If the member has permission, pairing completes and the thermostat appears in the shared home. If permission is insufficient, the app explains the restriction and does not pair the device.

title: Check sensor status after successful pairing
preconditions: The thermostat is unpaired, its temperature and humidity sensors are connected, and a known 2.4 GHz network with a valid password is available.
steps: Pair the thermostat with the available network using its controls.
Wait for the connection confirmation.
Check the displayed temperature and humidity readings.
expected: Pairing completes successfully and both sensor readings remain available. Neither E-217 nor E-221 appears.

title: Prevent duplicate pending invitations
preconditions: A pending invitation already exists for an email address in this home. The owner is signed in to the iOS app.
steps: Open the home's household sharing screen.
Invite the same email address again.
Check the app response and invitation list.
expected: The app prevents a duplicate pending invitation or offers a clear resend action; it does not create multiple active invitations for the same address.

title: Check firmware status for an up-to-date thermostat
preconditions: The thermostat is online and already running the latest firmware. The Android app is signed in to its home.
steps: Open the thermostat details in the app.
Open the firmware or device update status.
expected: The app reports that the thermostat is up to date. No update action is offered as available.

title: Check large text and display scaling
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the Android app. Android font size and display size can be increased in system settings.
steps: Increase Android font size and display size.
Open household sharing and inspect the member list and invite flow.
Open any removal or withdrawal confirmation.
expected: Names, email addresses, actions, and confirmation text remain readable without being clipped or overlapping. Essential controls remain visible and usable.

title: Cancel schedule edits
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and a saved schedule exists. The app provides a cancel or discard option.
steps: Open a schedule period and change its target.
Choose cancel or discard without saving.
Reopen the period.
expected: The unsaved target change is discarded. The period still shows its original saved target.

title: Pair after restarting the thermostat
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The thermostat is unpaired and connected to a suitable 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.
steps: Power the thermostat off and back on.
Wait for it to finish starting.
Start pairing from the iOS app.
Complete the pairing prompts.
expected: The thermostat becomes available for pairing after restart and is added to the app once the flow completes. No stale pairing state blocks setup.

title: Update while frost protection is enabled
preconditions: The thermostat is online, an update is available, and frost protection is enabled at 5 degrees.
steps: Confirm frost protection is active on the display.
Start the firmware update from the thermostat.
After restart, check the displayed mode and target.
expected: The update completes and frost protection remains enabled at 5 degrees, or the thermostat clearly reports that the mode must be restored. It does not silently select a higher target.

title: Reject a target above the supported range
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a configured zone.
steps: Add or edit a schedule period.
Try to enter a target above 30 degrees.
Attempt to save the period.
expected: The dashboard does not save an out-of-range target and identifies the permitted range of 5 to 30 degrees. No invalid value is applied to the schedule.

title: Receive a low-battery notification
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. The thermostat is configured for backup batteries, and a safe test setup can simulate a low-battery report.
steps: Simulate the thermostat reporting low backup batteries.
Wait for the app to receive the status.
Check the Android notification shade.
expected: A notification says the thermostat backup batteries are low and identifies the affected thermostat. It does not say that mains power has been interrupted.

title: Leave a household as a member
preconditions: The test account is an accepted member of a household and is signed in to the Android app.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Choose to leave the household.
Confirm the action.
expected: The account leaves the household and loses access to its shared devices and information. The owner sees the account removed from the member list.

title: Handle leading and trailing email spaces
preconditions: A verified Dormouse account exists and the tester is signed out. The tester knows the exact email address and password.
steps: Enter the account email address with spaces before and after it.
Enter the correct password and submit the form.
expected: The app trims harmless surrounding spaces and signs in to the correct account, or clearly requests a valid email without crashing.

title: Verify VoiceOver reads notification content
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. VoiceOver is enabled and a paired thermostat can generate a test notification.
steps: Generate a test notification.
Navigate to it with VoiceOver.
Listen to the notification content and activate it.
expected: VoiceOver announces the app and the meaningful notification text in a logical order. The notification can be activated using VoiceOver.

title: Check menu text fits display
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and menus contain their normal entries.
steps: Open each available top-level menu in turn.
Inspect the labels and highlighted item on each screen.
Navigate through any longer menu labels.
expected: Menu text and selection indicators remain visible and legible, with no clipped labels or overlapping content.

title: Exit pairing after entering network details
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. Pairing is open and network details have been entered but not submitted.
steps: Enter a network name or select a network.
Enter part of the password.
Use the back or cancel control to leave pairing.
expected: The thermostat exits the flow without attempting to connect. Incomplete credentials are not shown as a successful pairing.

title: Check readings recover after sensor conditions normalise
preconditions: The thermostat and both sensors are operating normally. A temporary, safe change in temperature or humidity can be made near the thermostat.
steps: Record both displayed readings.
Temporarily change one local condition without touching the thermostat.
Restore the original room conditions.
Wait for the readings to settle.
expected: Both readings continue to be displayed and move back towards their original values as the room conditions recover. No persistent sensor fault is shown.

title: Handle thermostat offline at update time
preconditions: An update is available and scheduled. The thermostat can be disconnected from Wi-Fi for the test, and the Android app is signed in.
steps: Disconnect the thermostat from Wi-Fi before 02:00.
Check firmware status in the app during the update window.
Reconnect the thermostat to Wi-Fi and refresh its status.
expected: The app reports that the update is pending or could not proceed because the thermostat is offline, without claiming success. After reconnection, the thermostat can retry or report the next available update opportunity.

title: Check cloud loss does not mix zone controls
preconditions: At least two zones are configured. The selected thermostat is online before the test and can be isolated from the Dormouse cloud without removing local power.
steps: Interrupt access to the Dormouse cloud while leaving the thermostat powered.
Check the display for E-110 or a clear cloud connection status.
Restore cloud access and check the selected zone again.
expected: The thermostat reports the cloud connection issue as E-110 or clear status and does not apply changes to another zone. Once access returns, the selected zone recovers without losing its local identity.

title: Check large report values remain readable
preconditions: A report is available with a high energy value or a value near the largest supported display size. The user can access it.
steps: Open the report containing the large value.
Inspect the value, label and surrounding layout.
expected: The full value and unit are visible, legible and associated with the correct label. The value does not overlap other report content.

title: Allow an invitation when one place remains
preconditions: The home has an owner and seven members. The owner is signed in to the iOS app and a valid new email address is available.
steps: Open household sharing for the home.
Invite the new email address.
Check the invitation list.
expected: The invitation is sent and shown as pending; the home does not exceed its limit of eight members.

title: Reload the dashboard on an energy report
preconditions: The user is signed in and viewing a report with data. The browser reload function is available.
steps: Open an energy report.
Reload the browser page.
expected: The report reloads without an error and continues to show the correct report period and home.

title: Pair after cancelling the setup flow
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The thermostat is unpaired and ready to pair on a suitable 2.4 GHz network.
steps: Start adding the thermostat.
Cancel before submitting network details.
Confirm cancellation if asked.
Start the add-thermostat flow again and pair.
expected: Cancellation exits the flow without adding a thermostat or leaving it in a misleading paired state. A new flow can pair the thermostat successfully.

title: Verify humidity reading after a brief damp-air change
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live sensor readings. A small source of damp air can be introduced nearby without wetting the thermostat.
steps: Record the displayed humidity.
Briefly introduce damp air near the thermostat without touching or covering it.
Remove the source and observe the display for two minutes.
expected: The displayed humidity responds to the local change and trends back towards the room level after the source is removed.

title: Check notification after app is force-closed
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, notifications are allowed, and a paired thermostat can generate a test notification. Force-close the app before the test.
steps: Force-close the iOS app.
Generate a test notification from the thermostat or test setup.
Check the iPhone notification centre.
Tap the notification.
expected: The notification is delivered while the app is closed. Tapping it launches the app and opens the relevant screen or a safe sign-in flow.

title: Check heating demand below target
preconditions: The thermostat is online, the boiler is responsive, and the room temperature is below the selected target. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open heating controls and note the room temperature and target.
Set a target above the room temperature.
Check the heating status in the app and listen or observe for the boiler to respond.
expected: The thermostat indicates a demand for heat and requests heat from the boiler. The app shows the new target and current heating status.

title: Check humidity response to drier room air
preconditions: The thermostat is in a stable room and its displayed humidity has settled. A safe way to lower room humidity gradually is available.
steps: Record the displayed humidity.
Gradually introduce drier room air without directing airflow at the sensor.
Observe the displayed humidity at intervals.
Stop when the room conditions stabilise.
expected: The displayed humidity trends down as the room becomes drier, without implausible abrupt changes. The reading settles as the room conditions stabilise.

title: Handle a delayed two-step verification code
preconditions: An account with two-step verification enabled is available, and the iOS device can receive its verification codes.
steps: Sign in with the account's valid credentials.
Wait until the verification code expires without submitting it.
Enter the expired code and submit it.
Enter the newly issued valid code, if prompted, and submit it.
expected: The expired code is not accepted and the app explains that it is no longer valid. A current valid code completes verification and opens the account.

title: Use dial-only pairing with spoken prompts
preconditions: The thermostat is unpaired and a known 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network with a valid password is available. The tester can use the dial without relying on touch controls and can hear the thermostat's spoken prompts, if supported.
steps: Start pairing using the dial and listen for each prompt.
Select the network and enter its password using only the dial.
Confirm the details using the dial.
Wait for pairing to finish and listen for the completion prompt.
expected: All pairing actions can be completed using the dial without requiring touch input. Spoken prompts, if provided, identify the current action and completion clearly; the display confirms successful pairing.

title: Handle an expired dashboard session
preconditions: A signed-in dashboard session can be expired using an approved test method. The account has notifications available.
steps: Expire the dashboard session.
Attempt to open the notifications view.
Sign in again when prompted.
expected: The dashboard does not expose notifications before authentication is restored. After sign-in, the notifications view loads for the authenticated account.

title: Check schedule display after firmware update
preconditions: A thermostat has a saved schedule and the Android app is signed in. A firmware update has completed successfully.
steps: Open the thermostat schedule after the update.
Check several saved periods and temperatures.
Edit and save one period.
expected: The existing schedule remains intact after the update. Its values are displayed correctly, and a new edit can be saved successfully.

title: Update while the app is closed
preconditions: The thermostat is online, an update is available and the iOS app is installed and signed in. The update window is imminent.
steps: Force-close the iOS app before the update window.
Allow the thermostat to remain powered and online through the window.
Open the app and check firmware status.
expected: The thermostat can complete its scheduled update without the app remaining open. On reopening, the app displays the current firmware version and accurate update status.

title: Check password field masking control
preconditions: The tester is signed out and the registration page is open.
steps: Enter a password in the password field.
Use the show or hide password control, if provided.
Check the field after each activation.
expected: The password is masked by default. The control toggles visibility without changing the entered value.

title: Adjust a zone without changing another
preconditions: Two zones are active and have different target temperatures. Both thermostats are online.
steps: On the first thermostat, raise its target by one half-degree using the dial.
Check the target on the second thermostat.
Check the target on the first thermostat again.
expected: Only the first zone's target changes. The second zone retains its original target.

title: Reflect sharing changes after refresh
preconditions: The owner and one accepted member can use separate iPhones. Both are signed in, and the member can see the shared home.
steps: On the owner's iPhone, remove the member from the home.
On the member's iPhone, refresh the app or reopen the home list.
Check whether the shared home is still accessible.
expected: The member's app reflects the removal after refresh and no longer grants access to the home.

title: Receive a mains power interruption alert
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe test setup can simulate a thermostat mains-power interruption.
steps: Simulate a mains-power interruption at the thermostat.
Wait for the app to receive the status.
Check the Android notification shade.
expected: A notification reports the mains-power interruption and identifies the affected thermostat. It does not present the event as a low-battery warning.

title: Handle invitation service failure
preconditions: An owner is signed in. The test environment can make the invitation service return an error.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Enter a valid email address.
Submit while the invitation service is unavailable.
Restore the service and check the pending invitation list.
expected: The dashboard shows a clear failure message and does not falsely report success. It does not create a misleading pending entry, and the owner can retry after service recovery.

title: Check report values are formatted consistently
preconditions: The user can view an energy report containing multiple non-zero values. The dashboard supports the user's browser locale.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Inspect the formatting of several displayed energy values.
expected: Values use consistent number formatting and clearly distinguish whole values from fractional values. No value is truncated or rendered as an invalid number.

title: Handle a cloud error while loading members
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the iOS app. A test environment or network control can make the Dormouse cloud unavailable temporarily.
steps: Make the Dormouse cloud unavailable.
Open household sharing for the home.
Check the displayed status and available actions.
Restore cloud access and retry loading the screen.
expected: The app shows a clear loading or connection error rather than incorrect member data; after access is restored, the current member list loads.

title: Check away mode after scheduled period changes
preconditions: A schedule has a period change during the test, and away mode is on. The Android app is connected.
steps: Note the thermostat's away target.
Wait for or simulate the next scheduled period change.
Check the thermostat and app.
expected: Away mode remains active and the away target remains in effect. The schedule change does not silently cancel away mode.

title: Check screen response to sensor value limits
preconditions: A controlled test environment can supply valid low and high room conditions within the thermostat's specified sensor range. The thermostat is powered and stable.
steps: Expose the thermostat to a valid low condition within its specified sensing range.
Check the displayed room reading.
Expose it to a valid high condition within the specified range.
Check the displayed room reading again.
expected: The display presents valid readings at both ends of the supported sensing range without blanking, clipping or showing an error. Values remain clearly associated with room temperature.

title: Check zone status when cloud is unreachable
preconditions: A paired thermostat is assigned to a zone. Network access to the Dormouse cloud can be interrupted.
steps: Block the network connection to the Dormouse cloud.
Open the affected zone in the Android app.
Restore cloud access and refresh the zone.
expected: The app reports that current zone information is unavailable while the cloud cannot be reached. It refreshes to the current status after cloud access returns.

title: Prevent a member from joining a different home via link
preconditions: A valid invitation link belongs to one home. The invitee is signed in to an account that already belongs to a different home.
steps: Open the invitation link on the invitee's iPhone.
Review the home name and invitation details before accepting.
Accept the invitation.
Check the invitee's home list.
expected: The app clearly identifies the home being joined and adds access only to that home; existing home membership remains unchanged.

title: Prevent pairing a fifth thermostat in a home
preconditions: The home already has four paired thermostats. A fifth thermostat is in pairing mode, and the Android app is signed in as the owner.
steps: Start adding another thermostat from the home screen.
Attempt to proceed with pairing the fifth device.
Review the app message and existing device list.
expected: The app explains that the home has reached its four-thermostat limit and does not add the fifth device. The four existing devices remain unchanged.

title: Check pairing timeout presentation E-104
preconditions: The thermostat is unpaired or pairing can be safely restarted. No suitable pairing network is made available during the test.
steps: Start the thermostat pairing flow using its on-device controls.
Leave the thermostat without completing pairing until the flow times out.
Observe the final display.
expected: The pairing flow ends with error code E-104 and a clear timeout indication; the display remains responsive to dial and button input.

title: Use sharing controls with keyboard only
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard using a keyboard and a supported browser.
steps: Navigate to household sharing using Tab and Shift+Tab.
Open the invite form and enter a valid email address.
Submit the invitation using the keyboard.
Navigate to the pending invitation controls.
expected: All sharing controls can be reached and operated by keyboard, with a visible focus indicator. The invitation is sent and its status and available actions are keyboard-accessible.

title: Reject target temperature between allowed steps
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and online. The Android app is signed in and provides a target temperature entry field.
steps: Open the target temperature entry field.
Enter a value that is not on a 0.5-degree step, such as 20.2 degrees.
Submit the value.
expected: The app does not apply an invalid target. It shows a clear validation message or adjusts the value to a valid half-degree step.

title: Change temperature by half a degree
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone has an online thermostat.
steps: Open the zone controls.
Change the target from 20 degrees to 20.5 degrees.
Save the setting.
expected: The dashboard accepts 20.5 degrees and shows it as the zone target. No rounding to a whole degree occurs.

title: Activate and verify one-hour boost
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and boost is not currently active.
steps: Press the boost button once.
Read the display for boost status and duration.
Wait briefly and check that the boost remains active.
expected: The display indicates that boost is active for one hour. The control does not start multiple boosts from one press.

title: Check temperature reading with frost protection selected
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and its temperature sensor is functioning. Frost protection can be selected on the thermostat.
steps: Record the current room temperature.
Select frost protection on the thermostat.
Check the displayed room temperature.
expected: The thermostat indicates frost protection and continues to display the measured room temperature separately from the 5 degrees protection target.

title: Handle an invalid invitation email
preconditions: The owner is signed in and can invite household members.
steps: Open the invite-member form.
Enter an incorrectly formatted email address.
Try to send the invitation.
expected: The app identifies the email address as invalid and does not send an invitation. The user can correct the entry without losing other form data.

title: Handle low battery warning during update readiness
preconditions: The thermostat can report E-401 low backup batteries, and an update is available. The Android app is online.
steps: Cause the thermostat to report E-401 before the update window.
Check the firmware status and warning in the app.
Review any guidance about proceeding or replacing batteries.
expected: The app displays the low-battery warning and does not misreport firmware status. It communicates any update limitation or recommended action clearly.

title: Pair a new thermostat over Wi-Fi from the app
preconditions: A thermostat reset to factory settings and a phone on the same 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network.
steps: In the app, choose Add a thermostat.
Hold the thermostat's dial for five seconds until it shows a pairing code.
Enter the code in the app and choose the home Wi-Fi network.
expected: Within two minutes the thermostat appears in the app, shows the current room temperature and accepts a new target temperature.

title: Check zero energy is shown clearly
preconditions: A report is available for a period in which the recorded energy value is zero. The user can access that report.
steps: Open the report for the period with zero energy.
Inspect the energy value and its label.
expected: The report displays zero as a valid value with its unit, rather than treating it as missing or replacing it with unrelated data.

title: Remove a household member as owner
preconditions: The owner is signed in and at least one member has accepted the household invitation.
steps: Open the household member list.
Select a member and choose to remove them.
Confirm the removal.
expected: The member is removed from the household and no longer has access to its shared devices or information. The owner sees the updated member list.

title: Manual update from thermostat settings
preconditions: The thermostat is online, idle, and has an update available. Its current schedule is saved.
steps: Open the thermostat's settings using the dial.
Select firmware update and confirm installation.
Wait for installation to finish, then inspect the version and schedule.
expected: The update installs and the thermostat displays the new firmware version. The saved schedule remains available and active.

title: Display schedule during cloud outage
preconditions: A schedule is saved and the thermostat has Wi-Fi access. The Dormouse cloud can be made unavailable while local thermostat power remains on.
steps: Make the Dormouse cloud unavailable to the thermostat.
Open Schedules on the thermostat.
Review the schedule and note any displayed error code.
Restore cloud access and reopen the schedule.
expected: The local schedule remains viewable during the cloud outage, with E-110 shown if the thermostat reports that it cannot reach the cloud. The schedule remains intact after service returns.

title: Check display readings after thermostat restart
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and both sensors are functioning. The current temperature and humidity readings are visible.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Restart the thermostat using its normal restart control.
Wait for the normal screen to appear.
expected: The normal screen returns with numeric temperature and humidity readings. No sensor fault is shown solely because of the restart.

title: Check VoiceOver labels in household sharing
preconditions: An iPhone with VoiceOver enabled is signed in to the Dormouse app as the home owner. The home has a member or pending invitation listed.
steps: Open household sharing with VoiceOver enabled.
Move focus through the member list and sharing controls.
Listen to the announced labels and states.
Activate the invite control using VoiceOver.
expected: VoiceOver announces meaningful labels, member or invitation status, and actionable controls; the invite control can be reached and activated.

title: Keep schedule edits after app restart
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and paired with an online thermostat. A schedule period can be edited.
steps: Change a period's target to a valid different value and save.
Close the app fully.
Reopen the app and inspect the period.
expected: The saved target remains visible after restarting the app. The app does not restore the previous value or create a duplicate period.

title: Keep membership after page refresh
preconditions: A member has accepted an invitation and can access the shared home in the web dashboard.
steps: Open household sharing or the home dashboard as the owner and confirm the member is listed.
Refresh the page.
Sign in as the member in a separate browser session and open the home.
expected: The member remains listed after refresh and can still access the home. Membership is not lost or duplicated by reloading the dashboard.

title: Check display in bright ambient light
preconditions: The thermostat is operating normally in a brightly lit room, without direct sunlight on the display.
steps: Place the thermostat in the bright room lighting.
Inspect the home screen readings and icons.
Open a menu and inspect its text.
expected: The display remains readable in bright ambient light, and essential values and menu labels are not washed out.

title: Pair when phone and thermostat use different bands
preconditions: A dual-band router provides 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz Wi-Fi under the same network name. The Android phone is connected on 5 GHz and the thermostat is in pairing mode.
steps: Start adding a thermostat in the app.
Select the shared network name and enter its password.
Follow the instructions until pairing finishes.
expected: The app completes pairing and the thermostat connects over 2.4 GHz. The app shows the thermostat as online.

title: Set a half-degree target
preconditions: The thermostat is online and controllable from the dashboard. The current target is not 20.5 degrees.
steps: Open the target temperature control.
Set the target to 20.5 degrees.
Save the change.
Check the dashboard and thermostat display.
expected: The target is shown as 20.5 degrees in both places. The value is not rounded to a whole degree.

title: Set away temperature in half-degree steps
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and away mode settings are available.
steps: Open away mode settings.
Set the target to 18.5 degrees.
Save and reopen the setting.
expected: The app accepts and retains 18.5 degrees as the away target.

title: Install a scheduled overnight firmware update
preconditions: The thermostat is paired, online and below the latest available firmware version. The Android app is signed in as the home owner.
steps: Open the thermostat in the Android app and check its firmware status.
Leave the thermostat powered and connected to Wi-Fi overnight.
After 04:00, refresh the firmware status in the app.
expected: The update installs between 02:00 and 04:00. The app shows the new firmware version and the thermostat remains paired and controllable.

title: Handle low backup batteries
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and paired. The iOS app is signed in, and low backup battery status can be safely simulated.
steps: Simulate low backup battery status using the approved test setup.
Check the thermostat display.
Check the iOS app for the thermostat status or notification.
expected: The thermostat displays E-401 and the app reports the low backup battery condition.

title: Announce sign-in errors to assistive technology
preconditions: A screen reader is available, and the dashboard sign-in page is open with no active session.
steps: Focus the email field and enter a registered email address.
Enter an incorrect password and submit the form.
Use the screen reader to inspect the resulting error announcement.
expected: The sign-in error is announced to the screen reader and is programmatically associated with the form or relevant field. The error is understandable without relying on colour alone.

title: Set the zone target to the minimum
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone has an online thermostat.
steps: Open the zone controls.
Set the target to 5 degrees.
Save the setting.
expected: The dashboard accepts 5 degrees and shows the zone target as 5 degrees. It does not allow the target to fall below 5 degrees.

title: Handle low backup battery alert
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and online with backup batteries that can be safely set to a low level. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Set the backup batteries to a low level.
Open heating controls in the app.
Check the thermostat display and app alerts.
expected: The thermostat displays E-401. The app reports low backup batteries without changing the user's target temperature.

title: Verify target step size at upper limit
preconditions: The thermostat is online and the iOS app is signed in. Its target is 29.5 degrees.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Increase the target once.
Check the displayed target.
expected: The target becomes 30 degrees, with no value beyond the supported maximum.

title: Check display contrast in a dark room
preconditions: The thermostat is operating normally in a room that can be made dim or dark.
steps: Dim the room lighting.
Inspect the home screen and its key values.
Open a menu and inspect its text and selection indicator.
expected: Essential readings and controls remain discernible in low ambient light without glare obscuring the information.

title: Recover from cloud connection error
preconditions: The Android app is signed in. The thermostat or app cannot reach the Dormouse cloud and the app shows an offline or connection error.
steps: Attempt to change away mode.
Restore access to the Dormouse cloud.
Refresh the home controls.
expected: The app shows the connection problem without losing the user's action where it can be safely retried. After recovery, it displays the confirmed away mode state.

title: Check heating controls in dark appearance
preconditions: Dark appearance is enabled on the iOS device. The app is signed in and a thermostat is online.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Check the target, heating status and boost state.
Change the target by one half-degree.
expected: Heating controls, statuses and values remain legible in dark appearance, and the target change is applied correctly.

title: Recover pairing after an app update
preconditions: An Android app update is available. The thermostat is in pairing mode, and a 2.4 GHz network is available.
steps: Update the app from the approved test build or store.
Open the updated app and sign in if required.
Start pairing and complete setup with valid network details.
expected: The updated app retains access to the account and pairing flow. The thermostat pairs successfully without requiring an unsupported workaround.

title: View the selected zone schedule
preconditions: A schedule with at least two periods is configured for the thermostat's zone. The thermostat is online or has the schedule stored locally.
steps: Open the schedule view on the thermostat.
Navigate through the day's periods.
Check the displayed times and targets for the selected zone.
expected: The thermostat shows the configured periods and targets for the selected zone. It does not display another zone's schedule as its own.

title: Check notification privacy on lock screen
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed. The iPhone notification preview setting is set to hide previews when locked, and a paired thermostat can generate a test notification.
steps: Lock the iPhone.
Generate a test notification containing account or home context.
Inspect the lock screen without unlocking the phone.
expected: The notification follows the iOS preview privacy setting and does not reveal protected details while the phone is locked. Its visible text is still sufficient to identify the app.

title: Navigate schedule menu by dial rotation
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and the schedule menu is available. The dial turns and presses normally.
steps: Press the dial to open the menu.
Turn the dial through schedule menu items in both directions.
Stop on Schedules and press the dial.
Return to the previous menu.
expected: Dial rotation moves the selection predictably in both directions, and pressing the dial opens the selected menu item.

title: Check geofencing disabled while away is active
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and away mode is active. Location permission is available.
steps: Disable the app's location permission in iOS settings.
Return to the app and refresh away settings.
Check the mode status and any location warning.
expected: The app retains the confirmed away mode status and clearly reports that location-based updates are unavailable. It does not silently change the heating target.

title: Verify displayed humidity is distinguishable
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and humidity readings are available on its display.
steps: Navigate to the screen showing humidity, if needed.
Record the displayed humidity value and unit.
Return to the home screen.
expected: Humidity is clearly identified as humidity, with its value distinguishable from the temperature and target.

title: Update with the dial pressed during download
preconditions: The thermostat is online, an update is available, and its display shows update progress.
steps: Start the update and wait until progress is visible.
Press the dial once during the download.
Observe the display and wait for the update to finish.
expected: The dial press does not cancel or damage the update. The display continues to show a meaningful update status and the installation completes.

title: Invite a household member by email
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in as the home owner. The home has fewer than eight members and internet access is available.
steps: Open household sharing for the home.
Choose the option to invite a member.
Enter a valid email address and send the invitation.
Check the member list and invitation status.
expected: The invitation is sent to the entered address and appears in the member list as pending.

title: Detect mismatched password confirmation
preconditions: The iOS app is open on the account creation screen with password confirmation fields available.
steps: Enter valid account details and a valid password.
Enter a different value in the confirmation field.
Submit the form.
expected: The app reports that the password entries do not match and does not create the account.

title: Check dial navigation through network list
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. Several visible 2.4 GHz networks are available for selection.
steps: Open the network list.
Turn the dial through the list in both directions.
Press the dial to select a network, then return to the list if possible.
expected: Each dial movement changes the highlighted item predictably, and pressing the dial selects only the highlighted network. The list does not skip or select items unexpectedly.

title: Use account screens with VoiceOver
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and signed out. VoiceOver is enabled in iOS settings.
steps: Open the app and navigate to the sign-in screen using VoiceOver.
Move through the email and password fields, sign-in button, and account-recovery links.
Open the two-step verification screen using a test account, then navigate its controls.
expected: VoiceOver announces each control with a useful name and role, and communicates relevant validation or status messages. The account flow can be navigated and operated without relying on sight.

title: Use frost protection in one zone
preconditions: Two zones with online thermostats exist. The Android app is signed in to the home.
steps: Open the first zone's heating controls.
Select Frost protection.
Check the first zone and its thermostat, then check the second zone.
expected: The first zone shows frost protection with a 5-degree target. The second zone's mode and target remain unchanged.

title: Heating follows active schedule
preconditions: The thermostat is online and has a schedule with a period active now. The iOS app is signed in.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Check the active schedule period and its target.
Confirm the heating status against the measured temperature and target.
expected: The app shows the target for the active schedule period. Heating is requested when the measured temperature is below that target.

title: Handle Wi-Fi signal loss during network scan
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A 2.4 GHz access point can be moved out of range or switched off during scanning.
steps: Open the network scan screen.
Switch off the access point or move it out of range.
Observe the network list and displayed status.
Restore the signal and rescan.
expected: The unavailable network is not presented as currently connectable. After signal is restored and a rescan is performed, the network can be selected.

title: Set frost protection target
preconditions: The thermostat is online and frost protection can be selected from the dashboard. The current target is above 5 degrees.
steps: Open the zone's heating mode controls.
Select frost protection.
Check the target shown on the dashboard.
Check the thermostat display.
expected: Frost protection is shown as active with a 5-degree target. The thermostat display also shows the frost-protection target or mode.

title: Check sensor readings after a sustained humidity change
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live readings. A controlled, safe method can change room humidity gradually without exposing the thermostat to moisture.
steps: Record the displayed humidity and temperature.
Change room humidity gradually and hold the new condition for ten minutes.
Restore the original condition and observe both readings.
expected: The humidity reading remains available through the sustained change and trends back after restoration; the temperature reading also remains visible and functional.

title: Factory resetting the thermostat clears its Wi-Fi settings
preconditions: A paired thermostat connected to Wi-Fi.
steps: Open Settings on the thermostat and choose Factory reset.
Confirm by holding the dial for ten seconds.
Wait for the restart, then open the network screen.
expected: The thermostat restarts on the welcome screen with no saved Wi-Fi networks, and it no longer appears in the owner's app.

title: Check sensor readings using dial-only interaction
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live readings. The dial can be used without pressing the boost button.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Use only dial turns and presses to navigate away from the sensor view.
Use only the dial to return to the sensor view.
expected: The dial-only flow allows the user to reach and read both sensor values without requiring another control.

title: Receive a boiler fault alert
preconditions: A user account is signed in and boiler alerts are enabled. A test boiler or approved simulator can report a fault.
steps: Trigger a boiler fault using the approved test method.
Open the dashboard notifications view.
Inspect the new alert.
expected: A notification reports that the boiler has a fault and identifies the affected home or zone. The alert does not claim the boiler is operating normally.

title: Test temperature limits in schedule editor
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and a scheduled period is open in the editor. The temperature control can be adjusted by turning the dial.
steps: Set the target to 5 degrees and try to decrease it one step.
Set the target to 30 degrees and try to increase it one step.
Save the period.
expected: The target cannot be set below 5 degrees or above 30 degrees. The saved value remains within the supported range.

title: View current monthly energy report
preconditions: The Android app is installed and signed in to an account with a paired thermostat. The home has energy data for the current month.
steps: Open the app and select the home's energy reports.
Open the current month's report.
Review the displayed energy summary and chart.
expected: The report opens for the current month and shows the available energy data with clearly labelled values and time period.

title: Create account with valid details
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the tester has an email address not already registered with Dormouse.
steps: Open the app and choose to create an account.
Enter valid account details and a password meeting the displayed rules.
Submit the form and complete any requested verification.
expected: The account is created and the app confirms success or opens the signed-in home screen.

title: Check temperature reading remains visible
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and the temperature sensor is connected. No error is present.
steps: View the home screen without touching the controls.
Read the room temperature shown on the display.
expected: The display shows a room temperature reading and remains on the home screen without an error.

title: Check app notification preference is respected
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled in Android settings. An app-level notification preference can be disabled, and a safe test alert is available.
steps: Disable the relevant alert type in the app's settings.
Generate that type of test alert.
Check the Android notification shade.
Review the alert status in the app.
expected: No Android notification is posted for the disabled alert type. The app still shows the current thermostat status and does not hide the fault itself.

title: Show an empty notification list
preconditions: A user account is signed in to a home with no notifications in the selected view or filter.
steps: Open the notifications view.
Apply the selected view or filter with no matching notifications.
expected: A clear empty-state message is shown instead of a blank or broken page. No unrelated notification is displayed.

title: Sign in with email case variation
preconditions: A verified account exists and the tester is signed out.
steps: Enter the registered email using different letter casing and the correct password.
Submit the sign-in form.
Review the result.
expected: Email casing is handled consistently with the account policy and does not cause an unintended duplicate identity. The outcome is clearly reported.

title: Request another two-step verification code
preconditions: A verified account has two-step verification enabled and the app is at code entry.
steps: Choose the option to resend the verification code.
Wait for the resend confirmation or new code.
Enter the newest code and submit it.
expected: The app confirms the resend request and accepts the newest valid code; an older code is not treated as the newest one.

title: Change a scheduled target temperature
preconditions: A schedule with at least one period is saved on the thermostat. The thermostat is connected to a working boiler.
steps: Open Schedules using the dial.
Select a day and choose an existing period.
Change its target temperature by one half-degree step.
Save the change and reopen the period.
expected: The period shows the revised target temperature, exactly one half-degree step above its previous value.

title: Check dial press does not repeat unexpectedly
preconditions: A menu with a single selectable option is open. The thermostat is stable and responsive.
steps: Press the dial once to activate the highlighted option.
Keep hands away from the dial and observe the result for several seconds.
Check that no further action occurs.
expected: The option activates once. The thermostat does not register a phantom second press or repeat the action without another deliberate input.

title: Accept a household invitation
preconditions: The owner has sent an invitation to an email address that can be accessed on an iPhone. The invitee has the Dormouse iOS app installed.
steps: Open the invitation email on the iPhone.
Follow the invitation link.
Sign in or create an account using the invited email address.
Open the home in the app.
expected: The invitation is accepted and the home appears in the invitee's app with member access.

title: Update several thermostats in one home
preconditions: The home has at least two thermostats with the same available firmware update. The Android app is signed in as the owner.
steps: Review firmware status for each thermostat in the home.
Allow each eligible thermostat to update overnight.
Refresh the status for every thermostat after 04:00.
expected: Each eligible thermostat reports its own accurate update result and firmware version. A failure on one thermostat does not incorrectly mark another thermostat as failed or updated.

title: Recover from a pairing timeout
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The thermostat and iPhone are on a suitable 2.4 GHz network, but the pairing flow can be left idle until it times out.
steps: Start adding the thermostat and begin pairing.
Leave the app idle until the pairing attempt times out.
Review the error on the thermostat and in the app.
Restart pairing and complete the prompts promptly.
expected: The first attempt ends without pairing and the thermostat shows E-104. Restarting the flow allows pairing to complete without creating a duplicate thermostat.

title: Check schedule after thermostat restart
preconditions: A schedule is saved on the thermostat. Power can be safely cycled using the approved method.
steps: Record the selected day's periods and targets.
Restart the thermostat using the approved method.
Wait for the display to become ready.
Open Schedules and compare the saved values.
expected: All recorded schedule periods and targets are retained after restart, with no unintended changes.

title: Check E-221 humidity fault on the display
preconditions: A safe, approved test setup can simulate a humidity sensor fault.
steps: Use the approved setup to simulate a humidity sensor fault.
Observe the displayed error and any remaining temperature information.
Restore the sensor and check the display.
expected: The display shows E-221 for the humidity sensor fault. Temperature information remains available if supported, and the error updates after restoration.

title: Pair with special characters in Wi-Fi password
preconditions: A 2.4 GHz network has a password containing symbols and mixed-case letters. The thermostat is in pairing mode.
steps: Start pairing and select the network.
Enter the password exactly, including its symbols and letter case.
Submit the details and wait for connection.
expected: The password field accepts the required characters accurately, and pairing succeeds with valid credentials. The app does not alter the password unexpectedly.

title: Reject matching current and new passwords
preconditions: The tester is signed in and can access password change settings.
steps: Enter the correct current password.
Enter the same value as the new password and confirmation.
Submit the change.
expected: The dashboard rejects reuse if prohibited by its password policy and explains the requirement. It does not report success unless the change is genuinely applied.

title: Check mains interruption indication
preconditions: An approved test setup can safely interrupt mains power while backup power is available.
steps: Interrupt mains power using the approved setup.
Observe the display while the thermostat is on backup power.
Restore mains power and check the display.
expected: The thermostat displays E-402 while mains power is interrupted. It returns to the appropriate normal status after mains power is restored.

title: Check a zone after low backup battery warning
preconditions: A zone thermostat can be put into a low backup battery state. The app is signed in to the home.
steps: Cause the thermostat to report low backup batteries.
Open the zone in the Android app.
Check the zone status and any alert details.
expected: The affected zone shows a clear low-battery warning associated with its thermostat. The thermostat displays E-401, and unrelated zones are not labelled as having low batteries.

title: Lose cloud access during update download
preconditions: An update is available and downloading. The network can block internet access while keeping local Wi-Fi connected.
steps: Start downloading the update on the thermostat.
Block internet access while keeping the thermostat connected to Wi-Fi.
Restore internet access and inspect the update status.
expected: The thermostat does not install an incomplete or unverified update. It gives a clear status and can safely retry after cloud access returns.

title: Pair with Voice Control
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. Voice Control is enabled, and the thermostat is ready to pair on a suitable network.
steps: Open the add-thermostat flow using voice commands.
Choose the network and enter credentials using available voice controls.
Start pairing using a voice command.
Follow the app prompts until pairing finishes.
expected: Pairing controls have usable names for Voice Control and can be selected by voice. The user can complete pairing without relying on unlabeled controls.

title: Verify update status after sensor fault
preconditions: The thermostat can report E-217 or E-221 while remaining accessible to the app. An update is available.
steps: Cause a temperature or humidity sensor fault.
Check firmware status and the sensor error in the Android app.
Restore the sensor connection or condition and refresh the status.
expected: The app keeps sensor and firmware states distinct and displays the relevant sensor error. It does not claim a firmware update failed solely because a sensor fault is present.

title: Check away mode state after app restart
preconditions: Away mode is on and the Android app is signed in.
steps: Close the Dormouse app completely.
Reopen the app.
Open the home controls.
expected: The app shows away mode as on, matching the thermostat's confirmed state.

title: Open a thermostat alert from the notification
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. At least one thermostat is paired and a safe test alert can be generated.
steps: Generate a thermostat alert.
Tap its notification.
Check the screen opened in the app.
expected: The app opens the relevant thermostat or alert detail and shows the alert's current status. It does not open an unrelated home or thermostat.

title: Handle overlapping schedule periods
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and a schedule editor is open for a day with at least one period.
steps: Set a period's start time to overlap another period.
Attempt to save the schedule.
expected: The app prevents conflicting periods from being saved and explains that their times overlap. The schedule remains in its last valid state.

title: Handle loss of network while loading a report
preconditions: The user is signed in and can view the web dashboard. Network access can be disabled and restored during the test.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Disable network access while a report is loading.
Restore network access and retry the report.
expected: The dashboard indicates that the report could not be loaded while offline. After network access is restored and the report is retried, the report loads or a clear service error is shown.

title: Check sensor display after an update failure
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and an approved test setup can safely cause a firmware update to fail.
steps: Start a firmware update using the approved procedure.
Cause the update to fail using the test setup.
Check the displayed error and sensor view.
expected: The thermostat indicates E-510 for the failed update. The device remains usable, and its sensor readings are available if the normal sensor view can be opened.

title: Check E-217 sensor error on the display
preconditions: A safe, approved test setup can disconnect the temperature sensor without damaging the thermostat.
steps: Disconnect the temperature sensor using the approved test setup.
Observe the thermostat display.
Reconnect the sensor and observe the display.
expected: The thermostat displays E-217 while the temperature sensor is disconnected. The error clears or updates appropriately after the sensor is restored.

title: Check boost ends after one hour
preconditions: The thermostat is online and the boiler is responsive. The Android app can display the active boost status.
steps: Start boost from the Android app.
Check that boost is active.
After one hour, refresh the app and check boost status.
expected: Boost ends at the end of its one-hour duration without requiring another action. The thermostat then follows its applicable target or schedule.

title: Member pairing permission follows account role
preconditions: The Android app is signed in as a household member rather than the home owner. The home already contains a paired thermostat, and a second thermostat is in pairing mode.
steps: Open the home and try to start adding the second thermostat.
Review whether the app permits the pairing action or requests owner authorisation.
If permitted by the app, follow the displayed authorisation flow.
expected: The app enforces the configured role permissions consistently and clearly identifies any required owner action. No thermostat is added without the necessary authorisation.

title: Check sharing across multiple zones
preconditions: The shared home has at least two zones with thermostats, and a member has accepted an invitation.
steps: Sign in as the member and open the home.
View each zone and its thermostat status.
Change the target in one zone.
Check the other zone.
expected: The member can see the home's available zones. The change applies only to the selected zone and does not alter the other zone's target.

title: Check update screen with high contrast
preconditions: An iOS accessibility contrast setting is enabled, such as Increase Contrast. The app is signed in and a thermostat's firmware status is available.
steps: Open the firmware status screen.
Check status indicators, text and buttons.
Review the screen with an update error or warning if available.
expected: Text, controls and update states remain distinguishable with the enabled contrast setting. Status is communicated by text as well as colour.

title: Verify displayed room temperature updates
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and its temperature sensor is connected. A safe way to cause a small room-temperature change is available.
steps: Record the displayed room temperature.
Cause a small, safe change in the air around the thermostat without touching it.
Wait for the sensor display to refresh and record the value.
expected: The displayed room temperature updates to reflect the sensor reading and remains separate from the target temperature.

title: Check away mode near a geofence boundary
preconditions: Geofencing is enabled in the Android app, location permission is granted, and a home geofence is configured. Away mode is currently off.
steps: Move the phone to just outside the configured home geofence.
Wait for the app to process the location change.
Check the away mode state in the app.
expected: Away mode turns on only after the phone is recognised as outside the configured geofence; the app does not repeatedly toggle the state while the phone remains there.

title: Verify target step size at lower limit
preconditions: The thermostat is online and the iOS app is signed in. Its target is 5.5 degrees.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Decrease the target once.
Check the displayed target.
expected: The target becomes 5 degrees, with no value below the supported minimum.

title: Keep me signed in after restarting the app
