preconditions: The iOS app is installed, and an account with two-step verification disabled is available. The user is signed in and has enabled any offered stay-signed-in option.
steps: Force-quit the Dormouse app.
Reopen the app.
Open the account area.
expected: The user remains signed in and can view account content without entering credentials again.

title: Keep heating controllable during update
preconditions: The thermostat has an update scheduled or in progress, and heating demand can be checked safely. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Set a valid target temperature in the app before the update window.
Check the target and heating status while the update is in progress.
Check the target and heating status after the update completes.
expected: The target temperature is not silently changed by the update. Heating control returns after installation, and the app shows the current target and status accurately.

title: Handle boiler not responding error
preconditions: The thermostat is online and paired. The boiler can be made not to respond, and the Android app is signed in.
steps: Make the boiler unresponsive.
Set a target above the room temperature in the app.
Check the app and thermostat for the resulting error.
expected: The thermostat displays E-305. The app reports that the boiler is not responding and does not claim that heating is operating normally.

title: Check the four-zone limit
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in as the home owner. Four thermostats are already assigned to the home, and a fifth unassigned thermostat is available.
steps: Open the option to add a zone.
Attempt to pair and assign the fifth thermostat.
Review the message and the zone list.
expected: The app prevents a fifth zone from being added and explains that the home has reached its zone limit. The existing four zones remain unchanged.

title: Reject a target with unsupported precision
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a configured zone.
steps: Add or edit a schedule period.
Enter a target with a quarter-degree increment, such as 19.25 degrees.
Attempt to save the period.
expected: The dashboard rejects the unsupported precision or guides the user to a valid half-degree value. It does not silently save a different temperature.

title: Delete a schedule period
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the selected day has at least two saved periods. The thermostat is online.
steps: Open the selected day's schedule.
Delete one period and confirm if prompted.
Reopen the schedule.
expected: The selected period is removed and the other periods remain unchanged. The app and thermostat reflect the updated schedule.

title: Keep notification state after sign-in
preconditions: A user account is signed in and has a notification marked as read.
steps: Sign out of the dashboard.
Sign in again with the same account.
Open the notifications view.
expected: The previously read notification remains marked as read. Its message and timestamp are still available.

title: Reject away temperature above maximum
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and paired with an online thermostat. Away mode settings allow temperature entry.
steps: Open away mode settings.
Try to enter a temperature above 30 degrees.
Save or confirm the entry.
expected: The app does not accept a temperature above 30 degrees and clearly indicates the allowed range.

title: Check sensor readings when boiler does not respond
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live readings. A safe test setup can prevent the boiler from responding to a heat request.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Request heat using the dial.
Check the display after the boiler fails to respond.
expected: The thermostat indicates E-305 for the boiler response failure; sensor readings remain available when the sensor view is shown.

title: Enable frost protection for a zone
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone has an online thermostat.
steps: Open the zone controls.
Enable frost protection.
Review the displayed target and zone status.
expected: Frost protection is shown as active for the selected zone with a 5 degrees target. No other zone's frost protection status changes.

title: Check report while signed out
preconditions: A report is available in an iOS app session that can be signed out of.
steps: Sign out of the iOS app.
Attempt to open Energy reports using any remaining app navigation or a report link.
expected: The app requires sign-in before showing private report data. No household energy values remain accessible after sign-out.

title: Owner leaves the household
preconditions: The owner is signed in and at least one other member is in the home.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Try to leave or remove the owner's own account.
Review the confirmation and available options.
expected: The owner is not silently removed or left with an ownerless home. The dashboard clearly requires a supported ownership transfer or other valid resolution.

title: Check target limits and step size
preconditions: A zone with an online thermostat exists. The Android app is signed in to the home.
steps: Open the zone's temperature control.
Try to decrease the target below 5 degrees.
Increase the target from 5 degrees in repeated single steps until it reaches 30 degrees.
Try to increase the target above 30 degrees.
expected: The control cannot set a target below 5 or above 30 degrees. Each available increment is exactly 0.5 degrees.

title: Check screen reader labels for sharing
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard with a screen reader enabled.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Navigate through the member list and invitation controls.
Open the invite form and move through its fields and buttons.
Submit a valid invitation.
expected: The screen reader announces meaningful names, roles, statuses and instructions for sharing controls. Submission feedback is announced and the pending invitation is identifiable.

title: Handle app network loss during update
preconditions: An update is in progress and the iOS device can be disconnected from the internet without disconnecting the thermostat from Wi-Fi.
steps: Disconnect the iOS device from the internet during the update.
Wait briefly, then restore the device's internet connection.
Refresh the update status in the app.
expected: The app indicates that status is temporarily unavailable while offline. After reconnection it reports the thermostat's actual update result and does not falsely claim success or failure.

title: Check keyboard and switch navigation
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the Android app. A Bluetooth keyboard or Android Switch Access is available.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Navigate through the screen using keyboard or Switch Access controls.
Open the invitation form and move between its fields and actions.
expected: All essential sharing controls can be reached and activated without touch. Focus is visible and follows a logical order.

title: Check sensor display while seated
preconditions: The thermostat is installed at its normal height. The tester can view and operate the unit from a seated position.
steps: View the display from the seated position.
Wake the display if needed using the dial or button.
Read both sensor values without standing.
Check that the values are not hidden by the viewing angle.
expected: Temperature and humidity readings can be seen and distinguished from a seated position. The display does not hide either value at the expected viewing angle.

title: Check report data after app relaunch
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and a monthly report is available.
steps: Open a report and select a month and zone.
Force-close the app.
Relaunch the app and return to Energy reports.
expected: The app remains stable and loads a valid report. Any restored month or zone selection is accurate and clearly indicated.

title: Prevent overlapping schedule periods
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the selected day has at least one saved period.
steps: Edit or add a period so its start time conflicts with an existing period.
Attempt to save the schedule.
Review the validation message and saved schedule.
expected: The app does not save overlapping periods and explains the conflict. Existing valid periods remain unchanged.

title: Check Low Power Mode location messaging
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, location permission is available, and the iPhone supports Low Power Mode.
steps: Enable Low Power Mode in iOS settings.
Open the app's away settings.
Check any geofencing availability or status message.
expected: The app does not claim a location transition has occurred without confirmation. Any limitation or delay is communicated clearly, and the current confirmed away status remains visible.

title: Check boost expiry in a zone
preconditions: A one-hour boost is active for the thermostat's zone. The thermostat remains powered throughout the test.
steps: Note the time that boost starts.
Wait one hour without changing the zone controls.
Check boost status and the zone's heating control.
expected: Boost ends after one hour and the display no longer shows it as active. The zone resumes its normal control state.

title: Pair with a long Wi-Fi network name
preconditions: A 2.4 GHz network with a long network name is available. The thermostat is in pairing mode and the network password is known.
steps: Start pairing and locate the long network name in the app.
Select it and confirm the selected name is correct.
Enter the password and complete setup.
expected: The app displays or otherwise identifies the full selected network unambiguously. The thermostat connects to that network and is added to the app.

title: Check screen updates after target change from schedule
preconditions: A schedule is configured with a known upcoming period and the thermostat is on its home screen.
steps: Wait for the scheduled period to begin or use a test schedule set to begin shortly.
Observe the displayed active target when the period changes.
Check that the screen updates without manual input.
expected: The displayed target updates to the scheduled period's value at the correct transition, with no stale previous target remaining.

title: Create a zone and add a thermostat
preconditions: The Android app is signed in as the home owner. One unassigned, paired thermostat is available.
steps: Open the home and select Zones.
Choose Add zone and enter a unique zone name.
Select the available thermostat and save the zone.
expected: The zone appears in the home with its name and assigned thermostat. The thermostat is no longer shown as unassigned.

title: Request a password reset for a registered email
preconditions: A Dormouse account exists for an email address the tester can access, and the tester is signed out.
steps: Open the password reset flow from the sign-in screen.
Enter the registered email address.
Submit the request and check the available confirmation.
expected: The app confirms the request without exposing sensitive account details, and the reset message arrives through the configured channel.

title: Save the maximum number of daily periods
preconditions: The selected zone has an editable schedule and fewer than six periods for the chosen day. The thermostat is online.
steps: Open the schedule for one day.
Add periods until there are six.
Set valid times and targets for all six periods.
Save and reopen the schedule.
expected: The schedule saves and displays all six periods with their times and targets. No seventh period can be added for that day.

title: Handle an expired password during sign-in
preconditions: A verified Dormouse account is configured to require a password change at next sign-in. The Android app is installed and signed out.
steps: Open the app's sign-in screen.
Enter the account email and current password.
Submit the sign-in form.
Follow the prompt to set a new password and submit it.
expected: The app explains that the password must be changed and provides a way to set one. After the change succeeds, the user can proceed without an unexplained error.

title: Save six periods in a zone schedule
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone has an online thermostat and its schedule is editable.
steps: Open the zone schedule.
Add six periods for one day with valid times and temperatures.
Save and reopen the schedule.
expected: All six periods are saved and displayed in the correct order. The dashboard does not drop or duplicate a period.

title: Receive target temperature change notification
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and notifications are allowed in iOS Settings. A paired thermostat is online and notifications for temperature changes are enabled, if that setting is available.
steps: Change the thermostat target temperature in the app.
Wait for the change to reach the thermostat.
Check the iPhone notification centre.
expected: A notification reports the target temperature change once the thermostat has accepted it. It identifies the correct home or zone and temperature.

title: Raise target temperature by half a degree
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and online. The Android app is open to its heating controls.
steps: Note the current target temperature.
Increase the target by one available increment.
Check the displayed target in the app and on the thermostat.
expected: The target increases by exactly 0.5 degrees, and the app and thermostat show the same value.

title: Confirm heating target after Android app relaunch
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and paired with a powered Dormouse thermostat. The thermostat has a working boiler connection and a known target temperature.
steps: In the Android app, change the target to a different valid temperature.
Close the app completely.
Reopen the app and open the thermostat's heating controls.
expected: The app shows the newly selected target temperature after relaunch. The thermostat display shows the same target.

title: Handle disconnected temperature sensor
preconditions: The thermostat is online and the iOS app is signed in. The temperature sensor can be disconnected using the approved test setup.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Disconnect the temperature sensor using the approved test setup.
Check the thermostat display and heating status in the app.
expected: The thermostat displays E-217 and the app identifies the sensor problem. The app does not present a disconnected sensor reading as a valid current temperature.

title: Set the minimum scheduled temperature
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with a configured zone.
steps: Add or edit a schedule period.
Set its target to 5 degrees and save.
Reopen the period.
expected: The dashboard accepts and displays 5 degrees as the period target. No validation error appears.

title: Receive a notification for a boiler-reported fault
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A paired thermostat and safe test setup can simulate a boiler-reported fault.
steps: Simulate a boiler-reported fault.
Wait for the thermostat to report the fault.
Check the Android notification shade.
expected: A notification states that the boiler has reported a fault and advises checking the boiler or seeking appropriate assistance. It does not confuse this with a connectivity issue.

title: Reject an incorrect password
preconditions: A verified Dormouse account exists and the tester knows its email address but will enter an incorrect password. The tester is signed out.
steps: Enter the account email address and an incorrect password.
Submit the sign-in form.
expected: Sign-in is denied and the app gives a non-revealing error message. The app does not disclose whether the email address is registered.

title: Check response to humidity sensor fault
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and operating normally. A controlled method is available to induce and clear a humidity sensor fault.
steps: Induce the humidity sensor fault.
Observe the thermostat display.
Clear the fault.
expected: The thermostat displays E-221 during the fault. After the fault is cleared, the error is removed and normal display operation resumes.

title: Check temperature display unit is degrees
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying the room temperature. The current display settings are available on the thermostat.
steps: Open the temperature display settings.
Select degrees Celsius if a unit choice is offered.
Return to the normal screen.
expected: The room temperature is displayed in degrees Celsius, using a clear unit label or an unambiguous Celsius setting.

title: Two-step verification code is required on a new browser
preconditions: An account with two-step verification switched on, and a browser that has never been used with it.
steps: Open the web dashboard in the new browser.
Log in with the email address and password.
Enter the six-digit code from the email.
expected: The dashboard asks for a code before showing anything, accepts the right code, and refuses a wrong one.

title: Update with low thermostat batteries
preconditions: An update is available and the thermostat reports low backup batteries, corresponding to E-401. The iOS app is connected to the thermostat.
steps: Check the battery warning in the iOS app.
Review the update status during the overnight window.
Replace or recharge batteries as directed, then check update eligibility again.
expected: The app clearly reports the low-battery condition and does not start an update when power stability is insufficient. After the condition is resolved, the app shows whether the update is scheduled or ready.

title: Edit a schedule using Dynamic Type
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and a schedule is available. iOS text size is set to the largest supported accessibility size.
steps: Open the weekly schedule.
Open a period for editing.
Change its target and save.
Review the schedule and save confirmation.
expected: Schedule times, targets and controls remain readable and usable at the selected text size. Text does not obscure essential controls or prevent saving.

title: Resend email verification message
preconditions: A Dormouse account exists but its email address is not verified. The tester can receive email for that address.
steps: Sign in or open the verification prompt.
Choose to resend the verification email.
Check the inbox and open the newest message.
expected: The app confirms the resend request without creating another account. The new message contains a working link for the correct account.

title: Handle cloud unavailable while loading report
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and a test setup can make the Dormouse cloud unavailable to the app.
steps: Make the Dormouse cloud unavailable.
Open Energy reports.
Observe the loading and error state.
expected: The app reports that the report cannot currently be loaded and offers a usable recovery path, such as retrying. It does not present an error message as valid report data.

title: Use sign-in with large text enabled
preconditions: The iOS device has a large accessibility text size enabled and the app is on the sign-in screen.
steps: Review the screen at the configured text size.
Enter valid credentials and submit the form.
expected: Text and controls remain usable without essential content being clipped, and sign-in can be completed.

title: Check low-battery warning on the display
preconditions: The thermostat is battery-powered or has an approved way to simulate low backup batteries.
steps: Use the approved setup to simulate low backup batteries.
Observe the display for a warning or error code.
Press the dial once and check whether the warning remains accessible.
expected: The thermostat displays E-401 for low backup batteries. The warning remains visible or accessible after a control press.

title: Keep schedules separate across zones
preconditions: Two thermostats are paired as separate zones in one home. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open the schedule for the first zone and set a distinctive period.
Open the second zone's schedule.
expected: The first zone's schedule is saved only for that zone. The second zone continues to show its own schedule.

title: Invite a household member by email
preconditions: The owner is signed in to the Android app and has a paired thermostat. The owner has fewer than eight household members.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Choose to add a member and enter a valid email address.
Send the invitation.
expected: The app confirms that the invitation was sent and shows the invitee as pending. The invitee receives an invitation for the correct household.

title: Change one zone without affecting another
preconditions: Two zones each have an online thermostat and different target temperatures. The Android app is signed in to the home.
steps: Record both zone targets.
Change the first zone target by 0.5 degrees.
Reopen both zone controls.
expected: Only the first zone's target changes. The second zone retains its original target.

title: Check warning presentation for E-101
preconditions: The thermostat can be made to lose its configured 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network. An appropriate test network is available.
steps: Make the configured Wi-Fi network unavailable.
Observe the thermostat display.
Restore the network after noting the displayed status.
expected: The display presents error code E-101 with a clear network-not-found indication, without obscuring the code.

title: Lose Wi-Fi during update download
preconditions: An update is available and downloading. A way to disable the paired Wi-Fi access point is available.
steps: Start downloading the update on the thermostat.
Disable the access point while download progress is visible.
Restore Wi-Fi and inspect the update status.
expected: The thermostat reports a connection problem or pauses the download without applying an incomplete image. Once Wi-Fi returns, it can safely resume or restart the download.

title: Confirm schedule change from a household member
preconditions: A household member account has permission to control the home. A thermostat is paired and the member is signed in to the Android app.
steps: Open the thermostat schedule as the household member.
Change a period and save.
Reopen the schedule.
expected: If the member has schedule-edit permission, the change is saved and displayed. If not, editing is unavailable or clearly denied, and the saved schedule is unchanged.

title: Verify invitation belongs to the correct household
preconditions: Two separate households exist, each with a different owner and thermostat. An invitation is pending for one of them.
steps: Open the invitation on the invitee's Android device.
Review the household identity shown before acceptance.
Accept the invitation and open the household view.
expected: The invitee joins only the household that sent the invitation. The other household and its thermostat are not exposed.

title: Show progress during an overnight update
preconditions: An update is available and scheduled to start during the overnight update window. The Android app is signed in and can reach the thermostat.
steps: Open the thermostat's firmware status shortly before 02:00.
Refresh the status after the update begins.
Check the displayed status and progress.
expected: The app changes from scheduled or pending to updating when installation starts. Any progress shown advances without reporting a false failure.

title: Check sensor display while cloud access is unavailable
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and showing live readings. The network can be configured to block access to the Dormouse cloud while keeping the thermostat powered.
steps: Record both sensor readings.
Block cloud access using the approved network test setup.
Check the display and open the sensor view if necessary.
expected: The thermostat indicates E-110 when cloud access cannot be reached, and both local sensor readings remain available on the sensor view.

title: Update when storage is unavailable
preconditions: An update is available and the test environment can simulate insufficient or unavailable update storage. The thermostat is connected to the iOS app.
steps: Start or schedule the update in the test environment.
Check the app's update status and any error details.
Restore storage availability and check the next update attempt.
expected: The app reports that the update cannot proceed and does not show a new version as installed. Once storage is available, the thermostat can retry in line with the overnight update rules.

title: Use firmware status with large text enabled
preconditions: Android system font size is set to the largest practical setting. The app is signed in and a firmware status is available.
steps: Open the thermostat firmware status screen.
Read the version, status and any error text.
Check all buttons and actions on the screen.
expected: Text remains readable and important status and actions are not clipped or overlapped. The user can identify the update state and reach available controls.

title: Create an account with valid details
preconditions: The tester has a valid email address not already registered. The web dashboard is open on its account creation page.
steps: Enter a valid email address and a compliant password.
Complete any required verification or consent fields.
Submit the registration form.
Open the dashboard after registration completes.
expected: The account is created and the dashboard shows the signed-in account. No validation or server error is displayed.

title: Check VoiceOver update status
preconditions: VoiceOver is enabled on the iOS device and the app is signed in. A thermostat is paired and its firmware status screen is available.
steps: Navigate to the thermostat's firmware status using VoiceOver.
Swipe through the status, version and available actions.
Activate the update status or action control.
expected: VoiceOver announces the thermostat identity, firmware version, update state and control labels meaningfully. Focus order is logical and controls can be activated without relying on sight.

title: Reject a seventh daily schedule period
preconditions: The Android app is signed in, and a schedule with six periods exists for the selected day.
steps: Open the selected day's schedule editor.
Attempt to add another period.
expected: The app does not add a seventh period and explains that six periods is the daily limit. The existing six periods remain unchanged.

title: Check schedule limit of six periods
preconditions: The selected zone has six schedule periods for the current day. Schedule editing is available on the thermostat.
steps: Open the schedule editor for the selected zone.
Attempt to add a seventh period.
Review the schedule after the attempt.
expected: The thermostat does not add a seventh period. The six existing periods remain intact and usable.

title: Receive a low temperature alert
preconditions: A user account is signed in and temperature alerts are enabled. A test condition or approved simulator can trigger a low temperature alert for the home.
steps: Trigger the low temperature alert condition.
Open the dashboard notifications view.
Inspect the new alert.
expected: A notification identifies the low temperature condition and the correct home or zone. The alert is visible in the dashboard without being duplicated.

title: Check password maximum length handling
preconditions: The tester is signed out and has an unused email address. A test string longer than the app's accepted password limit is available.
steps: Enter the email address and a password longer than the accepted limit.
Submit the form.
expected: The app handles the overlong password safely, either by clearly rejecting it or by accepting it if the product permits it. The app does not freeze, truncate silently, or show a misleading success.

title: Filter notifications by type
preconditions: A user account is signed in and has notifications of at least two available types.
steps: Open the notifications view.
Apply a filter for one notification type.
Compare the listed results with their displayed types.
expected: Only notifications matching the selected type are shown. Clearing the filter restores the full list.

title: Show notifications for the correct zone
preconditions: A signed-in account has a home with at least two zones. A test condition or approved simulator can generate an alert for one zone.
steps: Trigger an alert for one zone.
Open the dashboard notifications view.
Check the zone named in the new notification.
expected: The notification names the zone where the event occurred. It does not identify another zone in the same home.

title: Check sensor display when Wi-Fi network is unavailable
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and displaying live readings. Its configured Wi-Fi network can be switched off safely.
steps: Record the displayed temperature and humidity.
Switch off the configured Wi-Fi network.
Check the thermostat display and sensor view.
expected: The thermostat indicates E-101 for the missing Wi-Fi network; local temperature and humidity readings remain available.

title: Recover app display after network interruption
preconditions: An update is pending or in progress and the Android device can have its internet connection interrupted independently of the thermostat.
steps: Open the firmware status in the app.
Disable internet access on the Android device briefly.
Restore internet access and refresh the status.
expected: The app indicates that status is temporarily unavailable during the interruption. Once connected, it retrieves the current device status without duplicating or restarting the update.

title: Update with mains power interrupted
preconditions: An update is available and the thermostat displays E-402. A controlled test setup can reproduce the power interruption condition.
steps: Open the firmware update option on the thermostat.
Attempt to start the update while E-402 is shown.
Restore stable power and check the update option again.
expected: The thermostat does not start an unsafe update while power is interrupted. After power is restored, it reports the condition clearly and allows a safe update attempt.

title: Check password minimum length boundary
preconditions: The tester is signed out and the account registration page states its password rules.
steps: Enter a valid email and a password one character shorter than the stated minimum.
Submit the form.
Increase the password to exactly the stated minimum and submit again.
expected: The below-minimum password is rejected with a message explaining the requirement. The password at the minimum is accepted if it meets all other displayed rules.

title: Change report month using the calendar control
preconditions: The user is signed in and can view reports for a home with data in several months. A month or date-period control is available.
steps: Open the Energy reports page.
Use the calendar control to select a different available month.
expected: The report refreshes for the chosen month without changing the selected home.

title: Verify away mode starts at the configured departure delay
preconditions: An iPhone has the Dormouse app installed and is signed in as the home owner. Geofencing is enabled with location permission set to Always, and a departure delay is configured.
steps: Leave the home geofence with the iPhone.
Wait for the configured departure delay to elapse.
Check the away status in the app and on the thermostat.
expected: Away mode activates after the configured delay, not immediately upon leaving the geofence. The app and thermostat show the same away status.

title: Create a zone and assign a thermostat
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. One unassigned thermostat is online in the home.
steps: Open the zones page.
Choose to create a zone and enter a unique zone name.
Assign the online thermostat and save the zone.
expected: The zone is created with the entered name and assigned thermostat. The zone appears in the home zone list without an error.

title: Check heating controls with large text
preconditions: Large accessibility text is enabled on the iOS device. The app is signed in and a thermostat is online.
steps: Open the thermostat controls in the iOS app.
Inspect the target and boost controls.
Change the target and check the resulting value.
expected: Heating controls and their values remain readable and usable without clipping or hiding the selected target.

title: Verify update notification
preconditions: Notifications are enabled for the Dormouse iOS app and an update can be completed in the test environment. The device is signed in and online.
steps: Allow the thermostat update to complete.
Check the iOS notification centre for an update notification.
Open the notification and inspect the destination screen.
expected: The app sends a notification that accurately describes the update outcome. Tapping it opens the relevant thermostat or update status without showing stale information.

title: Require a password during registration
preconditions: The tester is signed out of the Android app and can access the account creation form.
steps: Enter a valid, unused email address.
Leave the password blank and submit the form.
expected: The app does not create an account and identifies the password field as required.

title: Preserve away mode after firmware update
preconditions: Away mode is enabled for the home and an update is available. The Android app is signed in as the owner.
steps: Record the current away mode status and configured behaviour.
Allow the update to complete.
Check away mode status and heating behaviour in the app.
expected: Away mode remains in its documented state after the update. The app does not silently disable geofencing or change away-mode heating behaviour.

title: Stop boost before its hour ends
preconditions: A one-hour boost is active on the thermostat. The Android app is online and signed in.
steps: Open heating controls.
Stop the active boost.
Check the app and thermostat status.
expected: Boost is no longer shown as active. Heating returns to the applicable target or schedule control.

title: Verify alert does not obscure all operating status
preconditions: A test setup can trigger a non-critical on-device alert while the thermostat is operating normally.
steps: Trigger the supported non-critical alert.
Inspect the alert and the remaining visible operating status.
Dismiss or clear the alert using the supported control.
expected: The alert is prominent and readable while essential status remains available where the design permits; clearing it restores the normal screen.

title: Set the zone target to the maximum
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone has an online thermostat.
steps: Open the zone controls.
Set the target to 30 degrees.
Save the setting.
expected: The dashboard accepts 30 degrees and shows the zone target as 30 degrees. It does not allow the target to exceed 30 degrees.

title: Edit one zone schedule period
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in with permission to manage schedules. A zone has at least one saved schedule period.
steps: Open the zone schedule and select a period.
Change its time or target temperature.
Save the change.
expected: The selected period shows the updated value. Other periods in that zone remain unchanged.

title: Verify display information is not conveyed by colour alone
preconditions: A test setup can display a normal status and a warning or active boost status.
steps: Observe the normal status on the display.
Trigger the warning or boost status.
Compare the text, symbols, or other non-colour indicators between states.
expected: Each state can be distinguished using text, icons, or shape as well as colour, so the status remains identifiable without relying on colour alone.

title: Pair with location permission denied
preconditions: The app has no location permission. Android Wi-Fi scanning may require location permission on this device version; the thermostat is in pairing mode and a 2.4 GHz network is available.
steps: Start pairing and deny any location permission request.
Check whether the app can list networks or offers manual network entry.
Provide valid network details and continue if the app allows it.
expected: The app explains any permission requirement clearly or offers a supported manual-entry route. It does not silently fail or report a successful pairing before the thermostat connects.

title: Pair using a large text size
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. iOS text size is set to the largest supported accessibility size, and the thermostat is ready to pair.
steps: Open the add-thermostat flow.
Review each pairing screen at the configured text size.
Enter valid Wi-Fi details and complete pairing.
expected: Text remains readable, controls and essential instructions are not clipped or obscured, and the user can complete pairing successfully.

title: Rename an existing zone
preconditions: The Android app is signed in as the home owner. A zone with an assigned thermostat exists.
steps: Open Zones and select the zone.
Choose Edit and change its name.
Save the change and return to the zone list.
expected: The new name appears in the zone list and zone details. The assigned thermostat remains in the zone.

title: Check notification settings persist after app restart
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and has an available notification setting. Notifications are enabled in both the app and Android settings.
steps: Open the app's notification settings.
Change an available notification preference.
Close the app completely.
Reopen the app and review the setting.
expected: The selected preference remains saved after the app restarts. The app's displayed setting agrees with the saved value.

title: Verify boost button feedback when idle
preconditions: The thermostat is on and boost is inactive. The connected boiler is available.
steps: Press the boost button once.
Observe the display for a boost status change.
Wait briefly and check that the displayed status remains stable.
expected: The display clearly indicates that boost has started and shows its active status without requiring navigation away from the current screen.

title: Check update details before installation
preconditions: An update with release details is available on the thermostat. The thermostat is not currently updating.
steps: Open the update notification on the thermostat.
Use the dial to view all available update details.
Exit the details without starting installation.
expected: The update details can be read using the thermostat controls. Exiting the details leaves the current firmware unchanged.

title: Check update screen contrast and colour independence
preconditions: An update status or error is visible in the Android app. Android display colour correction or grayscale is available.
steps: View the firmware status screen in normal display mode.
Enable grayscale or colour correction.
Check status, progress and error indicators.
expected: Update state and errors remain distinguishable through text, icons or labels, not colour alone. Essential information remains legible.

title: Check display at a schedule boundary
preconditions: A schedule transition is configured to occur shortly. The thermostat is displaying its home screen.
steps: Observe the display immediately before the scheduled transition.
Observe it as the transition time passes.
Check the target and any indication of heating demand.
expected: The display changes to the new scheduled target at the configured boundary and presents a consistent heating status without a frozen or partial screen.

title: Edit one zone schedule only
preconditions: Two zones exist with different schedules. The Android app is signed in as the home owner.
steps: Record the schedules for both zones.
Edit one period in the first zone's schedule and save.
Reopen both schedules.
expected: The edited period is saved only for the first zone. The second zone's schedule remains unchanged.

title: Check display and controls with hearing impairment
preconditions: Thermostat is operating normally in a quiet environment. A tester can assess the interaction without relying on audio cues.
steps: Navigate to a setting and activate it using the dial.
Observe the display for confirmation of the action.
Trigger a non-critical status change using the controls.
Check whether the resulting state is conveyed visually.
expected: Essential control feedback and status changes are communicated on the display, not solely through sounds. The tester can confirm each action and the resulting state visually.

title: Browse reports across several months
preconditions: The home has energy reports for at least three months. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open the energy reports.
Select an older available month.
Select a newer month, then return to the current month.
Check the period heading after each selection.
expected: Each selection shows the correct month and its corresponding report without mixing data between periods.

title: Delete a scheduled period
preconditions: An owner is signed in and has an online thermostat with at least two periods on the test day.
steps: Open the test day's schedule.
Delete one period and confirm if prompted.
Reopen the schedule.
expected: The selected period is removed and the other period remains unchanged. The dashboard shows the updated schedule.

title: Verify displayed units setting
preconditions: The thermostat supports changing temperature units. It is paired and showing a known room or target temperature.
steps: Open the unit setting using the thermostat controls.
Select the other supported temperature unit.
Check the displayed target and room temperature.
Restore the original unit.
expected: Temperature values are converted consistently and labelled with the selected unit. Restoring the original unit returns the readings to their original unit without changing the underlying heating target.

title: Check password visibility toggle
preconditions: The tester is signed out and the sign-in form is open on an Android phone.
steps: Enter a password in the password field.
Toggle password visibility on and inspect the value.
Toggle visibility off.
expected: The toggle reveals the entered password only when enabled and masks it when disabled. Toggling does not alter the password value.

title: Delete an empty zone
preconditions: The Android app is signed in as the home owner. An empty zone exists.
steps: Open the empty zone's settings.
Choose Delete zone and confirm the deletion.
Return to the zone list.
expected: The deleted zone no longer appears in the home. No thermostat is removed or changed.

title: Check account sign-in with password manager paste
preconditions: A verified account exists and its password is available in an Android password manager. The tester is signed out.
steps: Copy the password from the password manager.
Paste it into the password field and enter the account email.
Submit the form.
expected: Pasting is supported and preserves the full password accurately. Sign-in succeeds with the correct credentials.

title: Check location permission set to While Using
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and iOS location permission is set to While Using the App, not Always.
steps: Open away mode settings.
Review the location permission status.
Leave the app and check whether it reports background location as available.
expected: The app accurately indicates that background geofencing may be limited by the current permission. It does not claim reliable background location monitoring with While Using permission.

title: Check away mode for a zone with a fault
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to a two-zone home. One thermostat is reporting a boiler or sensor fault and the other is operating normally.
steps: Enable away mode for the home.
Open each zone's status.
Check the faulted zone's status and the working zone's target.
expected: The app indicates the fault for the affected zone and does not claim its heating change succeeded. The working zone applies its away target.

title: Handle boiler not responding error
preconditions: The thermostat is online and a test setup can make the boiler unresponsive. The user can view the zone on the dashboard.
steps: Set a target above the current room temperature.
Cause the boiler not to respond.
Refresh the dashboard and check zone status and notifications.
Restore the boiler and retry heating.
expected: The dashboard reports that heating was not delivered and presents the thermostat's E-305 status where available. After the boiler responds again, the heating request can succeed and the error clears or is marked resolved.

title: Monthly energy report matches the heating hours
preconditions: A test account with a month of recorded heating history.
steps: Open Energy on the web dashboard and choose last month.
Add up the daily heating hours in the chart.
Compare the total with the heating log export.
expected: The report's total heating hours match the log export to within one hour.

title: Assign a schedule to one zone
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in with permission to manage schedules. The home has at least two zones.
steps: Open one zone's schedule settings.
Set a period with a valid time and temperature.
Save the schedule and view the other zone.
expected: The schedule is saved for the selected zone. The other zone's schedule is not changed.

title: Pair using Android switch access
preconditions: Android Switch Access is enabled and configured, and the app is signed in to an owner account. A thermostat is in pairing mode, and a usable 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network is available.
steps: Navigate the add-thermostat flow using Switch Access only.
Select the Wi-Fi network and enter its password using the available switch-access controls.
Move through the setup prompts and submit the pairing request.
Wait for the completion status.
expected: Every pairing control and status can be reached and operated with Switch Access, with a clear focus indicator. Pairing completes and the app announces or presents its success status accessibly.

title: Recover away settings after cloud reconnect
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the home is configured. Internet access can be interrupted and restored.
steps: Disconnect the iPhone from the internet.
Open away settings and note the offline state.
Restore internet access and refresh the home controls.
expected: The app reconnects and displays the home's confirmed away status and target. It does not apply an unconfirmed offline edit without an explicit successful save.

title: Prevent password disclosure in browser history
preconditions: A browser with password saving disabled is available. The dashboard sign-in page is open.
steps: Enter an email address and password, then submit the form.
Use the browser back button to return to the sign-in page.
Inspect the password field and browser page source or saved form history.
expected: The password is not displayed in the field or exposed in browser history or page source after navigation. The user must re-enter it to sign in again.

title: Check humidity display near saturation
preconditions: The thermostat is in a controlled environment where humidity can be raised safely without wetting the unit or creating condensation. The displayed humidity has settled at a lower level.
steps: Record the displayed humidity.
Gradually raise the environment's humidity towards saturation.
Observe the displayed value as it approaches 100 percent.
Stop before condensation forms.
expected: The displayed humidity remains a valid value and does not exceed 100 percent. No sensor fault appears and no condensation reaches the thermostat.

title: Select a half-degree schedule target
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and an editable schedule period is available. The thermostat is online.
steps: Edit the period's target temperature.
Set the target to 19.5 degrees.
Save and reopen the period.
expected: The app saves and displays 19.5 degrees without rounding it. The thermostat receives the same target.

title: Check dial operation after a long press
preconditions: Thermostat is on its home screen and heating settings are available.
steps: Press and hold the dial for five seconds.
Release the dial and inspect the display.
Check that the target and menu state have not changed unexpectedly.
expected: The dial performs only its documented long-press behaviour, if any. It does not cause repeated selections or an unintended change to the heating target.

title: Check dial operation with gloves
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on and the target temperature control is available. The tester has gloves suitable for ordinary household use.
steps: Wear the gloves and turn the dial to change the target.
Press the dial to confirm the target.
Check the displayed value.
expected: The dial turns and presses reliably while wearing gloves. The display shows the selected target and confirms the action without requiring repeated attempts.

title: Show schedule save failure clearly
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and a schedule exists. The thermostat or cloud can be made unavailable during the test.
steps: Make a valid schedule change.
Make the thermostat or cloud unavailable before saving.
Save the change and observe the app response.
Restore service and inspect the saved schedule.
expected: The app reports that the change was not confirmed and does not present it as successfully applied. After service is restored, the displayed schedule accurately reflects whether the change was saved.

title: Check zone controls with large text
preconditions: An online zone exists. Android display text size is set to the largest supported setting.
steps: Open Zones in the Android app.
Open a zone and inspect its name, target, and mode controls.
Change the target by 0.5 degrees and inspect the updated screen.
expected: Zone details and controls remain readable and usable without clipped text or overlapping controls. The updated target is visible and can be operated.

title: Check zone frost protection
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in with permission to control the home. The home has an online zone.
steps: Open the zone's heating settings.
Enable frost protection for that zone.
Review the displayed target or mode.
expected: Frost protection is enabled for the selected zone and uses a 5 degree target. The app identifies the mode as frost protection.

title: Check tactile operation of boost button
preconditions: The thermostat is mounted in its intended position and boost is inactive.
steps: Locate the boost button by touch without looking directly at it.
Press it once deliberately.
Check the display for the resulting status.
expected: The boost button is distinguishable by touch from the dial, registers one deliberate press, and the display confirms the action.

title: Refresh a report after returning to the page
preconditions: The user can access a report page and the browser can reload pages. Report data is available for the selected period.
steps: Open an energy report and note its selected period and home.
Navigate to another dashboard page.
Return to the Energy reports page.
expected: The report page loads successfully and shows a valid report for the selected or default period and home, without stale or duplicated content.

title: Set target temperature by turning the dial
preconditions: The thermostat is powered on, connected to a working boiler and showing the home screen. Heating is available.
steps: Turn the dial clockwise to raise the target temperature.
Press the dial to confirm the target.
expected: The display shows the selected target temperature, and the boiler is requested to heat if the room is below that target.

title: Check large text accessibility in report
preconditions: The Android device has a monthly report available and supports system font scaling.
steps: Increase the Android font size to the largest supported setting.
Open the monthly energy report.
Review headings, values, controls and any explanatory text.
expected: Report text remains readable and controls remain usable. Essential labels and values are not clipped or obscured.

title: Edit a scheduled start time
preconditions: A schedule with at least one period is saved on the thermostat. The selected period has a start time that can be changed without overlapping another period.
steps: Open the selected day's schedule.
Choose a period and edit its start time.
Set the time five minutes later and save.
Reopen the period to check the saved time.
expected: The thermostat displays the new start time, five minutes later than before, and retains the period's other settings.

title: Keep sign-in safe after app backgrounding
preconditions: A Dormouse account has two-step verification enabled. The tester is at the verification-code entry step on Android.
steps: Background the app while the code-entry screen is open.
Wait briefly, then return to the app.
Inspect the screen and complete sign-in with a valid code.
expected: The app resumes safely without showing credentials or codes in notifications or app previews. The tester can complete sign-in, or must reauthenticate if the session has expired.

title: Display a boiler fault for its zone
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. A zone's thermostat reports boiler fault code E-312.
steps: Open the zones overview.
Open the affected zone's details.
Review its fault status and any displayed code.
expected: The fault is associated with the correct zone and identifies E-312 as a boiler fault. The dashboard does not show the zone as heating normally.

title: Receive boost completion notification
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in, notifications are allowed, and a paired thermostat is online. Boost notifications are enabled, if that setting is available.
steps: Start a one-hour boost from the app.
Confirm the thermostat indicates that boost is active.
Wait until the one-hour boost ends.
Check the iPhone notification centre.
expected: A notification reports that boost has ended. It is delivered once and refers to the correct thermostat or zone.

title: Enable geofencing away mode
preconditions: The Android app is signed in, location permission is available, and geofencing is configured for the home. Away mode is off.
steps: Open away mode settings.
Enable geofencing.
Leave the configured home area with the phone.
expected: The app detects that the phone has left the home area and activates away mode according to the configured geofence behaviour.

title: Check that a persistent fault does not spam notifications
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and notifications are enabled. A safe setup can keep a thermostat fault active for the duration of the test.
steps: Simulate a persistent thermostat fault.
Wait for the initial notification.
Keep the fault active and check notifications for ten minutes.
expected: The initial fault notification is delivered. The app does not send repeated identical alerts at short intervals while the fault remains unchanged.

title: Set minimum target temperature
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and online. The Android app is signed in.
steps: Open heating controls.
Set the target to 5 degrees.
Try to lower the target once more.
expected: The target is set to 5 degrees. It cannot be set below 5 degrees.

title: Check report for a newly paired thermostat
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to a household whose thermostat was paired this month and has little or no report history.
steps: Open Energy reports.
Select the current month.
Review the report period and any empty or partial data indication.
expected: The app shows only data available since pairing, or clearly states that data is not yet available. It does not imply that the thermostat was reporting before it was paired.

title: Check zone status when Wi-Fi is lost
preconditions: A zone is paired and online in the Android app. Wi-Fi access for its thermostat can be interrupted.
steps: Interrupt the thermostat's Wi-Fi connection.
Open the zone in the app and refresh its status.
Restore Wi-Fi and check the zone again.
expected: The app identifies the zone or thermostat as offline or unavailable and does not present stale status as current. After reconnection, the zone returns to an online state.

title: Handle an expired invitation
preconditions: A household invitation is available in an expired state through the test setup. The invitee can open it on Android.
steps: Open the expired invitation link.
Try to accept the invitation.
Return to the app and review the household list.
expected: The app explains that the invitation has expired and does not add the invitee. The invitee can request or receive a new invitation.

title: Handle humidity sensor fault during heating use
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and online. Its humidity sensor can be made faulty, and the Android app is signed in.
steps: Cause the humidity sensor to report a fault.
Open the heating screen in the Android app.
Check the displayed heating controls and error information.
expected: The thermostat displays E-221. The app identifies the humidity sensor fault while keeping heating controls available if heating itself remains operational.

title: Use away mode with Android display magnification
preconditions: The Android app is signed in and away mode is off. Android display magnification is enabled in the phone's accessibility settings.
steps: Open the home's controls in the app.
Magnify the screen and locate the away mode control.
Enable away mode and inspect its status.
expected: The away mode control and its status remain visible and operable when magnified, with no clipped text or overlapping controls.

title: Check button operation after a long press
preconditions: Thermostat is on its home screen and boost is inactive. No critical warning is present.
steps: Press and hold the boost button for five seconds.
Release the button and inspect the display.
Check that no unintended menu or repeated command appears.
expected: The button performs only its documented long-press behaviour, if any; otherwise it behaves as a single press or safely ignores the hold. No repeated or unintended heating command occurs.

title: Recover from a zone thermostat Wi-Fi loss
preconditions: The thermostat is assigned to a zone and connected to Wi-Fi. The home has at least one other zone online.
steps: Disconnect the thermostat's Wi-Fi access point or otherwise interrupt its connection.
Check the display for connection status or an error code.
Restore Wi-Fi and wait for reconnection.
expected: The thermostat indicates loss of connectivity without changing another zone's controls. After Wi-Fi is restored, it reconnects and resumes normal zone operation.

title: Sign in with valid credentials
preconditions: A verified Dormouse account exists and the tester knows its correct email and password.
steps: Open the iOS app and choose sign in.
Enter the correct email and password.
Submit the form and complete two-step verification if requested.
expected: The app signs in to the correct account and displays its authenticated home screen.

title: Complete pairing using the thermostat dial
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. A known 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network with a valid password is available, and the Dormouse cloud is reachable.
steps: Open pairing on the thermostat.
Use the dial to select the network and enter its password.
Confirm the details and wait for pairing to finish.
Check the thermostat display for its connection status.
expected: The thermostat joins the selected network and completes pairing. The display confirms it is connected, with no pairing error shown.

title: Check report period boundaries
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and report data is available for consecutive months.
steps: Open the report for one month.
Note its displayed start and end dates.
Open the following month's report and check its displayed dates.
expected: Each report identifies the correct month and its boundaries. The displayed periods do not overlap or omit dates between consecutive months.

title: Handle a schedule save during cloud loss
preconditions: An owner is signed in and can open an online thermostat's schedule. A safe test method is available to interrupt access to the Dormouse cloud.
steps: Change a schedule period.
Interrupt cloud access before saving.
Attempt to save and observe the dashboard response.
Restore cloud access and check the schedule.
expected: The dashboard reports that the save could not be confirmed and does not claim success. After connectivity returns, the schedule is either unchanged or saved exactly once, with its actual state shown clearly.

title: Confirm member cannot manage household membership
preconditions: The test account is an accepted household member, not the owner. At least one other member is present.
steps: Open household sharing settings as the member.
Look for controls to invite, remove, or change household members.
Try to access any membership-management action.
expected: The member cannot invite or remove household members or change ownership. Owner-only controls are hidden or blocked with a clear message.

title: Check sensor values while boost is active
preconditions: The thermostat is powered, both sensors are functioning and heating control is available. The boost button is accessible.
steps: Record the temperature and humidity readings.
Press the boost button to start a one-hour boost.
Check the displayed sensor readings.
expected: The thermostat indicates that boost is active while continuing to show the correct types of sensor readings. Boost status is not mistaken for a room temperature or humidity value.

title: Verify email address using the confirmation link
preconditions: The tester can register a new account and receive email. The app requires email verification before the account is fully active.
steps: Register with a valid unused email address.
Open the verification email on the phone.
Tap the verification link and return to the app.
expected: The email address is marked verified and the app shows the resulting account state. The link does not lead to an unrelated account or expose credentials.

title: Remove a household member
preconditions: An owner is signed in and another person is an active member of the home.
steps: Open household sharing settings.
Remove the member and confirm the action if prompted.
Check the member list and the removed account's access.
expected: The member is removed from the list and can no longer access the home. Other members retain their access.

title: Handle cloud loss during zone control
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in and the home has an online thermostat. Network access can be disabled during the test.
steps: Open a zone's controls while online.
Disable network access on the iPhone.
Attempt to change the zone target.
Restore network access and refresh the zone.
expected: The app reports that it cannot complete or confirm the change while disconnected. After reconnection, the displayed zone status reflects the thermostat's confirmed state.

title: Handle a Wi-Fi network that is not found
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and unpaired. No network matching the attempted network selection is available during pairing.
steps: Open pairing on the thermostat.
Attempt to select or connect to the unavailable network.
Observe the displayed error and recovery options.
expected: The display shows E-101 for the network that cannot be found. The thermostat remains responsive and offers a way to retry or exit pairing.

title: Set a half-degree scheduled target
preconditions: The thermostat is paired and has an editable scheduled period. The target temperature is not already at the chosen value.
steps: Open the period in the schedule editor.
Turn the dial to a target ending in .5 degrees.
Save the schedule.
Reopen the period and inspect its target.
expected: The half-degree target is saved and displayed without rounding to a whole degree.

title: Check spoken or accessible reading presentation
preconditions: The thermostat has an available accessibility feature for reading display content aloud or otherwise improving access. Both sensor readings are available.
steps: Enable the accessibility feature using the thermostat controls.
Request or trigger reading of the screen content.
Listen to or inspect the accessible output.
expected: The accessible output identifies the temperature and humidity readings distinctly and includes their units. It does not confuse a sensor value with the target temperature.

title: Handle an empty zone
preconditions: An owner is signed in to the web dashboard. An empty zone exists.
steps: Open the empty zone.
Review its controls, readings and status.
Return to the zones overview.
expected: The empty zone is identified as having no thermostat. The dashboard does not show fabricated readings or imply that heating is being controlled.

title: Recover pairing after the app is terminated
preconditions: The iOS app is installed and the user is signed in. The thermostat is ready to pair on a suitable 2.4 GHz network.
steps: Start pairing and reach the connection attempt.
Force-close the app.
Reopen the app and return to add a thermostat.
Complete pairing or restart the flow as prompted.
expected: The app provides a clear recovery path and reports the actual pairing state. Completing the flow adds one thermostat, not duplicates.

title: Check humidity display at dry-room conditions
preconditions: The thermostat is powered and its humidity sensor is connected. The room is dry but within the sensor's supported operating range.
steps: Wake the thermostat display.
Read the humidity value.
Check that a percent sign or other clear percentage indication is shown.
expected: The thermostat displays a numeric humidity percentage without a sensor fault or a value outside the valid 0 to 100 percent range.

title: Update with multiple thermostats
preconditions: Two or more thermostats in one home are online and have an update available. Their zones have distinct names and heating settings.
steps: Review each thermostat and zone in the iOS app.
Allow the overnight update window to run.
Check each device's update status, version and zone settings.
expected: Each thermostat reports its own update outcome and version. Zone assignments and heating settings remain associated with the correct thermostat.

title: Use schedule controls with low vision
preconditions: A schedule is saved and the thermostat display is functioning. The tester can assess the display at the intended viewing distance and use any available display contrast or brightness controls.
steps: Open Schedules on the thermostat.
Read the selected day, period time, and target temperature from the usual viewing position.
Use available display settings to improve readability, if present.
Change a period and verify the value before saving.
expected: Schedule labels and values are legible enough to distinguish the selected item, time, and temperature. The tester can verify the intended value before saving.

title: Compare reports across two zones
preconditions: The iOS app is signed in to a household with two zones and report data for both.
steps: Open Energy reports.
Select the first zone and note its monthly data.
Select the second zone and compare its report.
expected: Each zone's report is clearly identified and shows its own data. Changing zones does not leave the previous zone's values labelled as the new zone.

title: Pair with a hidden 2.4 GHz network
preconditions: A hidden 2.4 GHz network is available, with its exact network name and password. The thermostat is in pairing mode.
steps: Start adding a thermostat in the app.
Choose the option to enter network details manually.
Enter the exact network name and password, then continue.
expected: The app submits the entered network details and pairing completes. The thermostat appears online in the app.
